steps.text: Place on a hot tawa on medium flame. Spread a little water over the top with your fingers to prevent cracks.

steps.title: Flip
steps.text: When the bottom has light spots (about 1 minute), flip and cook the other side for 1 minute.

steps.title: Puff
steps.text: Roast directly on the flame with tongs, or press with a cloth on the tawa, until it puffs and both sides are cooked.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Apply a little ghee and serve hot.

tips: Knead each portion just before rolling; millet dough dries out quickly.
Patting with wet hands is easier than rolling for beginners.
serving_ideas: dal, sabzi, pithla or a garlic chutney, plus a little white butter or jaggery (traditional).
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: best eaten hot; it hardens as it cools.

recipes.description: A gluten-free buckwheat and potato paratha for fasting days.

steps.title: Prepare the add-ins
steps.text: Mash the potato; it binds the gluten-free flour.

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: In a bowl, combine the kuttu with the potato, spices and salt. Add water gradually and knead into a soft dough. Rest for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Divide
steps.text: Divide the dough into 6 equal balls.

steps.title: Roll
steps.text: Dust a ball with flour and roll it into a thin 6-inch round.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Place on a hot tawa on medium flame. Flip when small bubbles appear and cook the other side for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Apply a few drops of oil, flip and press gently with a spatula. Cook until both sides have golden-brown spots.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Keep warm in a cloth-lined box and serve with curd, chutney or a sabzi.

tips: Rest the dough so it rolls thin without shrinking back.
serving_ideas: plain curd or raita, a little white butter (optional) and pickle or green chutney.
Best time: breakfast or lunch.
recipes.storage: keeps in an airtight box for 1 day at room temperature (theplas up to 3 days) and is ideal for travel.

recipes.description: A soft, light paratha stuffed with grated bottle gourd.

steps.title: Knead the dough
steps.text: Mix the whole-wheat flour with salt and oil. Add water little by little and knead into a soft, smooth dough. Cover and rest for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare the stuffing
steps.text: Squeeze the grated lauki very well and mix with chillies, coriander and spices.

steps.title: Divide
steps.text: Divide the dough and the stuffing into 4 equal portions each. The stuffing should be dry; moisture makes parathas tear.

steps.title: Stuff
steps.text: Roll a dough ball into a 4-inch disc, place a portion of stuffing in the centre, gather the edges, pinch to seal and flatten gently.

steps.title: Roll
steps.text: Dust with flour and roll gently into a 6–7 inch paratha, applying even pressure so the stuffing does not break through.

steps.title: Cook the first side
steps.text: Place on a hot tawa over medium flame. Cook for 1 minute until small bubbles appear, then flip.

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Brush the cooked side with ½ tsp ghee or oil, flip again and press the edges with a spatula. Cook both sides until golden-brown spots appear.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with curd. Make the remaining parathas the same way.

tips: Seal the stuffing well and roll with light pressure to avoid tearing.
Use only ½ tsp ghee per side; dry-roasting first keeps the paratha light.
serving_ideas: plain curd or raita, a little white butter (optional) and pickle or green chutney.
Best time: breakfast or lunch.
recipes.storage: best eaten hot. Cooked parathas keep in a tiffin for 5–6 hours; the stuffing keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

steps.text: Mix the multigrain atta with a pinch of salt. Add water little by little and knead into a soft, smooth dough.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Cover and rest for 20–30 minutes; rested dough makes softer rotis.

steps.title: Divide & roll
steps.text: Divide into 6 balls. Dust with flour and roll each into a thin, even 6-inch circle.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Place on a hot tawa. Flip when small bubbles appear (about 20 seconds).

steps.title: Cook the other side
steps.text: Cook until light brown spots form (about 40 seconds).

steps.title: Puff
steps.text: Place the roti directly on a medium flame with tongs; it will puff up fully. Flip once.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Apply a little ghee if you like, and keep in a cloth-lined box.

tips: Roll evenly; thick and thin patches stop the roti from puffing.

serving_ideas: any dal, sabzi or curry.
Best time: lunch and dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps soft in a cloth-lined box for 6–8 hours.

recipes.description: Paratha stuffed with paneer and fresh methi, aromatic and protein-rich.

steps.title: Knead the dough
steps.text: Mix the whole-wheat flour with salt and oil. Add water little by little and knead into a soft, smooth dough. Cover and rest for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare the stuffing
steps.text: Mix the grated paneer with methi, chilli, roasted cumin and salt.

steps.text: Divide the dough and the stuffing into 4 equal portions each. The stuffing should be dry; moisture makes parathas tear.

steps.text: Roll a dough ball into a 4-inch disc, place a portion of stuffing in the centre, gather the edges, pinch to seal and flatten gently.

recipes.description: Soft, puffed whole-wheat rotis made without oil, the healthiest everyday Indian bread.

steps.title: Knead
steps.text: Mix the whole-wheat flour with a pinch of salt. Add water little by little and knead into a soft, smooth dough.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Cover and rest for 20–30 minutes; rested dough makes softer rotis.

steps.title: Divide & roll
steps.text: Divide into 6 balls. Dust with flour and roll each into a thin, even 6-inch circle.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Place on a hot tawa. Flip when small bubbles appear (about 20 seconds).

steps.title: Cook the other side
steps.text: Cook until light brown spots form (about 40 seconds).

steps.text: Place the roti directly on a medium flame with tongs; it will puff up fully. Flip once.

steps.text: Apply a little ghee if you like, and keep in a cloth-lined box.

serving_ideas: any dal, sabzi or curry.
Best time: lunch and dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps soft in a cloth-lined box for 6–8 hours.

recipes.description: Karnataka-style finger millet roti, an excellent source of calcium.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Take the ragi with the onion, green chilli, coriander leaves and curry leaves and salt in a wide plate.

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: Add hot water little by little and mix with a spoon, then knead with the heel of your palm for 3–4 minutes into a smooth, crack-free dough. Millet dough has no gluten, so knead only one portion at a time.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Take a lemon-sized ball and pat it between your palms, or roll it between two sheets of butter paper, into a 6-inch round.

steps.title: Cook the first side
steps.text: Place on a hot tawa on medium flame. Spread a little water over the top with your fingers to prevent cracks.

steps.title: Flip
steps.text: When the bottom has light spots (about 1 minute), flip and cook the other side for 1 minute.

steps.title: Puff
steps.text: Roast directly on the flame with tongs, or press with a cloth on the tawa, until it puffs and both sides are cooked.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Apply a little ghee and serve hot.

tips: Knead each portion just before rolling; millet dough dries out quickly.
Patting with wet hands is easier than rolling for beginners.
serving_ideas: dal, sabzi, pithla or a garlic chutney, plus a little white butter or jaggery (traditional).
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: best eaten hot; it hardens as it cools.

recipes.description: Sama (barnyard millet) upma with potato and peanuts, suitable for fasting.

steps.title: Rinse
steps.text: Rinse the barnyard millet and drain well.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat oil in a kadhai. Crackle the mustard seeds, then add the dals and cashews and fry until golden. Add curry leaves, green chilli, ginger and hing.

steps.title: Cook the vegetables
steps.text: Add the potato and peanuts and sauté for 3–4 minutes until slightly soft.

steps.title: Boil the water
steps.text: Add 400 ml water and salt and bring to a rolling boil.

steps.title: Add the grain
steps.text: Lower the flame and add the barnyard millet in a thin stream with one hand while stirring continuously with the other, so no lumps form.

steps.title: Cook covered

steps.text: Add the ghee, lemon juice and coriander, fluff gently and serve hot.

recipes.description: The classic Maharashtrian fasting dish: soft sago pearls with peanuts, potato and green chilli.

steps.title: Soak the sabudana
steps.text: Rinse the sabudana 2–3 times until the water runs clear. Soak in just enough water to cover it (about ¾ cup) for 5–6 hours or overnight.

steps.title: Check
steps.text: Press a pearl between your fingers; it should mash easily with no hard centre. Drain any extra water completely.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Mix the sabudana with the crushed peanuts, salt and sugar so every pearl is coated and stays separate.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee in a kadhai, crackle the cumin, then add green chillies and curry leaves.

steps.title: Add potatoes
steps.text: Add the boiled potato cubes and sauté for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Add the sabudana mixture and cook on low flame, stirring gently, for 5–7 minutes until the pearls turn translucent.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Switch off the flame, add lemon juice and coriander and serve warm.

tips: Overcooking makes sabudana sticky; switch off as soon as the pearls turn translucent.
Roasted peanut powder keeps the pearls separate.
serving_ideas: a bowl of curd or a glass of buttermilk.
Best time: breakfast or vrat meals.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh; it becomes chewy when cold.

steps.text: In the same oil, crackle the mustard seeds and cumin, then add curry leaves, green chilli and hing.

steps.title: Cook the vegetables
steps.text: Add the onion, soya granules and green peas and sauté on medium flame until the onion is soft and translucent and the vegetables are just tender (3–5 minutes).

steps.title: Add the poha
steps.text: Add the seasoned poha and mix gently. Cover and cook on low flame for 2–3 minutes so it steams through.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Switch off the flame and add the lemon juice and coriander leaves and the roasted crunch. Toss gently and serve hot.

tips: Use thick poha; thin poha turns mushy.
Add lemon juice only after switching off the flame, or it turns bitter.

Best time: breakfast or evening snack.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh; it dries out when reheated.

recipes.description: Rava upma with soya granules for a high-protein breakfast.

steps.title: Roast the grain
steps.text: Dry-roast the rava / suji on low flame for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until aromatic and lightly golden. Transfer to a plate.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat oil in a kadhai. Crackle the mustard seeds, then add the dals and cashews and fry until golden. Add curry leaves, green chilli, ginger and hing.

steps.title: Cook the vegetables
steps.text: Add the onion, soya granules, carrot and green peas and sauté for 3–4 minutes until slightly soft.

steps.title: Boil the water
steps.text: Add 420 ml water and salt and bring to a rolling boil.

steps.title: Add the grain
steps.text: Lower the flame and add the rava / suji in a thin stream with one hand while stirring continuously with the other, so no lumps form.

steps.title: Cook covered
steps.text: Cover and cook on the lowest flame for 3–4 minutes until the water is absorbed and the grain is soft.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Add the ghee, lemon juice and coriander, fluff gently and serve hot.

tips: Roasting the grain well keeps the upma fluffy and non-sticky.
For a softer upma, add ¼ cup more water.

Best time: breakfast or a light dinner.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh. Sprinkle a little water and reheat leftovers covered.

recipes.name_hi: गेहूं और ओट्स दलिया संग खजूर
recipes.description: A warm porridge of broken wheat and oats, sweetened lightly with dates.

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Dry-roast the dalia and rolled oats on low flame for 3–4 minutes, stirring, until aromatic.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Add the remaining toned milk and bring to a gentle boil, stirring continuously so it does not stick.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Lower the flame and cook for 15 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy.

steps.title: Sweeten
steps.text: Switch off the flame and stir in the dates. Adding jaggery off the heat stops milk from curdling.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Pour into bowls.

tips: Stir often and keep the flame low so the porridge does not catch at the bottom.
Porridge thickens as it cools; loosen it with a little warm milk or water.
serving_ideas: a handful of nuts or seeds and a fruit.
Best time: breakfast.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh; keeps in the fridge for 1 day. Reheat with a splash of milk or water.

recipes.description: A tangy rasam with gooseberries, very rich in vitamin C.

steps.title: Cook the dal
steps.text: Pressure-cook the moong dal with 2 cups water for 3 whistles and mash; keep the dal water.

steps.title: Crush the spices
steps.text: Coarsely crush the pepper, cumin and garlic in a mortar.

steps.title: Boil the base
steps.text: In a pot, add the tamarind water, crushed tomatoes, turmeric, salt, jaggery, curry leaves, the crushed spices and rasam powder along with the amla. Boil for 7–8 minutes until the raw smell goes.

steps.title: Add water & dal
steps.text: Add the remaining water and the dal. Heat until it turns frothy on top, then switch off. Do not boil it hard after this.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee, crackle mustard seeds, add dry red chillies, curry leaves and hing and pour over the rasam.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Add coriander, cover for 5 minutes, and serve hot with rice or as a soup.

tips: Switch off rasam as soon as it froths up; over-boiling makes it bitter.
Rasam tastes better after resting covered for 10 minutes.
serving_ideas: steamed rice with a little ghee, or sip it hot like a soup.
Best time: lunch or dinner; very soothing during colds.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

recipes.description: Sambar with a freshly roasted and ground coconut-spice paste.

steps.title: Cook the dal
steps.text: Wash the toor / arhar dal and pressure-cook with water and turmeric for 3–4 whistles until soft. Mash well.

steps.title: Soak the tamarind
steps.text: Soak the tamarind in ½ cup warm water for 10 minutes and squeeze out the pulp.

steps.title: Cook the vegetables
steps.text: In a pot, boil the drumsticks, brinjal, shallots and tomato with 1¼ cups water and salt for 7–8 minutes until tender but not mushy.

steps.title: Roast & grind the masala
steps.text: Dry-roast the grated coconut and spices on low flame until golden and aromatic, then grind to a smooth paste with a little water. Add it along with the sambar powder in the next step.

steps.title: Add tamarind & spices
steps.text: Add the tamarind extract, sambar powder and jaggery and simmer for 5 minutes until the raw smell of tamarind goes.

steps.title: Add the dal
steps.text: Add the mashed dal, adjust the consistency with hot water and simmer for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat oil, crackle mustard and methi seeds, add dry red chillies, curry leaves and hing, and pour over the sambar.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with coriander and serve hot.

tips: Simmer the sambar after adding dal; boiling hard makes it lose its aroma.
Freshly ground sambar powder makes a big difference to flavour.
serving_ideas: steamed rice, idli, dosa or vada.
Best time: breakfast, lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2 days. Dal thickens when cold; add hot water while reheating.

recipes.description: Kadhi with sautéed okra, a Rajasthani favourite.

steps.title: Whisk
steps.text: Whisk the curd with the besan, turmeric, chilli powder and salt until completely smooth. Add the water and whisk again.

steps.title: Start cooking
steps.text: Pour into a heavy pot and bring to a boil on medium flame, stirring continuously so the curd does not split.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Once it boils, lower the flame and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it thickens slightly and the raw besan smell goes.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Sauté the okra in 1 tsp oil until lightly crisp and add it to the kadhi for the last 4 minutes.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat oil or ghee, crackle cumin, methi and mustard seeds, add dry red chillies, curry leaves and hing and pour over the kadhi.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with coriander and serve hot.

tips: Use slightly sour curd for the best flavour.
Keep stirring until the kadhi comes to a boil to stop it from curdling.
serving_ideas: steamed rice, jeera rice or khichdi.
Best time: lunch.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

recipes.description: Nutty, thick chana dal with an onion-tomato tadka, low in glycaemic index.

steps.title: Wash & soak
steps.text: Wash the chana dal 3–4 times until the water runs clear and soak for 60 minutes.

steps.title: Pressure-cook
steps.text: Cook the dal with the water, turmeric and salt for 3–4 whistles on medium flame, until completely soft. Let the pressure release naturally.

steps.title: Mash
steps.text: Open the cooker and whisk the dal lightly until creamy. Add hot water to get the consistency you like and simmer for 3–4 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare the tadka
steps.text: Heat oil, crackle the cumin and hing, add onion and sauté until golden. Add ginger, garlic and green chilli, then tomato, chilli powder and garam masala, and cook until the tomato turns soft and oil separates.

steps.title: Temper the dal
steps.text: Pour the sizzling tadka over the dal and cover immediately for 1 minute to trap the aroma.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with coriander and serve hot.

tips: Soaking dal makes it cook faster and easier to digest.
Add the tadka just before serving for the best aroma.
serving_ideas: phulka, jeera rice or brown rice, with a salad.
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2 days. Dal thickens when cold; add hot water while reheating.

steps.title: Whisk
steps.text: Whisk the curd with the besan, turmeric, chilli powder and salt until completely smooth. Add the water and whisk again.

steps.title: Start cooking
steps.text: Pour into a heavy pot and bring to a boil on medium flame, stirring continuously so the curd does not split.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Once it boils, lower the flame and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it thickens slightly and the raw besan smell goes.

steps.title: Balance
steps.text: Stir in the jaggery.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat oil or ghee, crackle cumin, methi and mustard seeds, add dry red chillies, curry leaves and hing and pour over the kadhi.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with coriander and serve hot.

tips: Use slightly sour curd for the best flavour.
Keep stirring until the kadhi comes to a boil to stop it from curdling.
serving_ideas: steamed rice, jeera rice or khichdi.
Best time: lunch.

steps.title: Cook the dal
steps.text: Pressure-cook the moong dal with 2 cups water for 3 whistles and mash; keep the dal water.

steps.title: Crush the spices
steps.text: Coarsely crush the pepper, cumin and garlic in a mortar.

steps.title: Boil the base
steps.text: In a pot, add the tamarind water, crushed tomatoes, turmeric, salt, jaggery, curry leaves, the crushed spices and rasam powder along with the mint leaves and coriander leaves. Boil for 7–8 minutes until the raw smell goes.

steps.title: Add water & dal
steps.text: Add the remaining water and the dal. Heat until it turns frothy on top, then switch off. Do not boil it hard after this.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee, crackle mustard seeds, add dry red chillies, curry leaves and hing and pour over the rasam.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Add coriander, cover for 5 minutes, and serve hot with rice or as a soup.

tips: Switch off rasam as soon as it froths up; over-boiling makes it bitter.
Rasam tastes better after resting covered for 10 minutes.

steps.text: Soak the tamarind in ½ cup warm water for 10 minutes and squeeze out the pulp.

steps.text: In a pot, boil the drumsticks, carrot, brinjal, pumpkin, onion and tomato with 1¼ cups water and salt for 7–8 minutes until tender but not mushy.

Freshly ground sambar powder makes a big difference to flavour.

Best time: breakfast, lunch or dinner.

recipes.description: A thin, spicy Rajasthani kadhi with no pakodas, light and tangy.

steps.title: Whisk
steps.text: Whisk the curd with the besan, turmeric, chilli powder and salt until completely smooth. Add the water and whisk again.

steps.title: Start cooking
steps.text: Pour into a heavy pot and bring to a boil on medium flame, stirring continuously so the curd does not split.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Once it boils, lower the flame and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it thickens slightly and the raw besan smell goes.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat oil or ghee, crackle cumin, methi and mustard seeds, add dry red chillies, curry leaves and hing and pour over the kadhi.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with coriander and serve hot.

tips: Use slightly sour curd for the best flavour.
Keep stirring until the kadhi comes to a boil to stop it from curdling.
serving_ideas: steamed rice, jeera rice or khichdi.
Best time: lunch.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

steps.title: Prepare the base
steps.text: Soak the tamarind in warm water for 10 minutes and extract the juice.

steps.title: Crush the spices
steps.text: Coarsely crush the pepper, cumin and garlic in a mortar.

steps.title: Boil the base
steps.text: In a pot, add the tamarind water, crushed tomatoes, turmeric, salt, jaggery, curry leaves, the crushed spices and rasam powder. Boil for 7–8 minutes until the raw smell goes.

steps.title: Add water
steps.text: Add the remaining water. Heat until it turns frothy on top, then switch off. Do not boil it hard after this.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee, crackle mustard seeds, add dry red chillies, curry leaves and hing and pour over the rasam.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Add coriander, cover for 5 minutes, and serve hot with rice or as a soup.

tips: Switch off rasam as soon as it froths up; over-boiling makes it bitter.
Rasam tastes better after resting covered for 10 minutes.
serving_ideas: steamed rice with a little ghee, or sip it hot like a soup.
Best time: lunch or dinner; very soothing during colds.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Wash the chana dal well and soak in plenty of water for 1 hour.

steps.title: Pressure-cook
steps.text: Drain, add fresh water and salt and pressure-cook for 3 whistles until soft enough to mash between your fingers. Keep the cooking water.

steps.title: Make the masala
steps.text: Heat oil, add cumin and bay leaf. Add onion and sauté on medium flame for 8–10 minutes until deep golden. Add ginger, garlic and green chilli and cook 1 minute. Add the tomato purée and powdered spices and cook until the masala thickens and oil separates (6–8 minutes).

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the lauki and cook covered for 6 minutes.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Add the cooked chana dal with enough cooking water to make a gravy. Mash a few pieces against the side of the pan to thicken it.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Cover and simmer on low flame for 15 minutes so the chana dal absorb the masala.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Add the coriander leaves and lemon juice, check the salt and serve hot.

tips: Brown the onions slowly; this gives the gravy its depth without cream.
Use the legume cooking water in the gravy; it holds flavour and nutrients.
serving_ideas: steamed rice, jeera rice, phulka or bhakri, with onion-cucumber salad.
Best time: lunch.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2–3 days and tastes even better the next day. Freezes well for a month.

recipes.description: Okra cooked with tangy pickle spices.

steps.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps.text: Wash, peel if needed and cut the bhindi into even, bite-sized pieces so they cook evenly.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat mustard oil until it smokes lightly, lower the flame and add fennel, kalonji, methi and mustard seeds (the pickle spices), then hing and green chilli.

steps.title: Add the spices
steps.text: Lower the flame and add the turmeric and powdered spices with 1 tbsp water so they do not burn. Stir for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the bhindi and salt and toss well to coat with the masala.

steps.title: Cook uncovered
steps.text: Cook on medium flame for 15 minutes, stirring gently now and then, until tender and lightly browned. Do not cover.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Uncover, raise the flame for 1 minute to dry any moisture, then add the coriander leaves and mix gently.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with phulka, paratha or dal-rice.

tips: Cut vegetables to the same size so they cook evenly.
Cook on low heat with the lid on; the vegetables steam in their own moisture and need very little oil.
serving_ideas: phulka, paratha or bhakri, with dal and curd.
Best time: lunch or dinner; also great in tiffin boxes.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1–2 days.

recipes.description: Thin potato strips cooked with cumin until lightly crisp.

steps.text: Wash, peel if needed and cut the potato into even, bite-sized pieces so they cook evenly.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat oil in a kadhai, crackle the cumin, then add hing, green chilli and ginger and sauté for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Add the spices
steps.text: Lower the flame and add the turmeric and powdered spices with 1 tbsp water so they do not burn. Stir for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the potato and salt and toss well to coat with the masala.

steps.title: Cook uncovered
steps.text: Cook on medium flame for 12 minutes, stirring gently now and then, until tender and lightly browned. Do not cover.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Uncover, raise the flame for 1 minute to dry any moisture, then add the coriander leaves and mix gently.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with phulka, paratha or dal-rice.

tips: Cut vegetables to the same size so they cook evenly.
Cook on low heat with the lid on; the vegetables steam in their own moisture and need very little oil.
serving_ideas: phulka, paratha or bhakri, with dal and curd.
Best time: lunch or dinner; also great in tiffin boxes.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1–2 days.

recipes.description: Small brinjals stuffed with a peanut-sesame-coconut masala.

steps.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps.text: Make a cross slit in each small brinjal, keeping the stem intact. Soak in salted water.

steps.title: Make the stuffing
steps.text: Mix the peanuts, sesame seeds, grated coconut, jaggery and tamarind pulp with all the powdered spices and salt. Sprinkle a few drops of water if needed so it just holds together.

steps.title: Stuff
steps.text: Fill each slit vegetable with the masala, pressing it in firmly. Keep any leftover masala.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat oil in a wide pan, crackle the cumin and add hing.

steps.title: Arrange
steps.text: Place the stuffed vegetables in a single layer and sprinkle over the leftover masala.

steps.title: Cook covered
steps.text: Cover and cook on low flame for 18 minutes, turning gently every 4–5 minutes, until tender and evenly browned.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with phulka or as a side with dal-rice.

tips: Cook on low heat so the vegetable cooks through before the masala burns.
Turn gently with tongs so the stuffing stays in.
serving_ideas: phulka, paratha or dal-rice.
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

recipes.description: Crisp-tender okra tossed with onion and spices.

steps.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps.text: Wash, peel if needed and cut the bhindi into even, bite-sized pieces so they cook evenly.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat oil, crackle the cumin, add the onion and sauté until light golden. Add ginger, garlic and green chilli and cook for 1 minute.

steps.title: Add the spices
steps.text: Lower the flame and add the turmeric and powdered spices with 1 tbsp water so they do not burn. Stir for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the bhindi and salt and toss well to coat with the masala.

steps.title: Cook uncovered
steps.text: Cook on medium flame for 15 minutes, stirring gently now and then, until tender and lightly browned. Do not cover.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Uncover, raise the flame for 1 minute to dry any moisture, then add the coriander leaves and mix gently.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with phulka, paratha or dal-rice.

tips: Cut vegetables to the same size so they cook evenly.
Cook on low heat with the lid on; the vegetables steam in their own moisture and need very little oil.
serving_ideas: phulka, paratha or bhakri, with dal and curd.
Best time: lunch or dinner; also great in tiffin boxes.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1–2 days.

steps.text: Heat coconut oil, crackle the mustard seeds, then add urad dal and fry until golden. Add dry red chillies, curry leaves and hing.

steps.title: Add the spices
steps.text: Lower the flame and add the turmeric and powdered spices with 1 tbsp water so they do not burn. Stir for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the kundru and salt and toss well to coat with the masala.

steps.title: Cook uncovered
steps.text: Cook on medium flame for 15 minutes, stirring gently now and then, until tender and lightly browned. Do not cover.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Uncover, raise the flame for 1 minute to dry any moisture, then add the grated coconut and mix gently.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with phulka, paratha or dal-rice.

tips: Cut vegetables to the same size so they cook evenly.
Cook on low heat with the lid on; the vegetables steam in their own moisture and need very little oil.
serving_ideas: phulka, paratha or bhakri, with dal and curd.
Best time: lunch or dinner; also great in tiffin boxes.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1–2 days.

steps.text: Wash, peel if needed and cut the parwal into even, bite-sized pieces so they cook evenly.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat oil, crackle the cumin, add the onion and sauté until light golden. Add ginger, garlic and green chilli and cook for 1 minute.

steps.title: Add the spices
steps.text: Lower the flame and add the turmeric and powdered spices with 1 tbsp water so they do not burn. Stir for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the parwal and salt and toss well to coat with the masala.

steps.title: Cook covered
steps.text: Cover and cook on low flame for 15 minutes, stirring every few minutes. Sprinkle a little water only if it starts to stick.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Uncover, raise the flame for 1 minute to dry any moisture, then add the coriander leaves and mix gently.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with phulka, paratha or dal-rice.

tips: Cut vegetables to the same size so they cook evenly.
Cook on low heat with the lid on; the vegetables steam in their own moisture and need very little oil.
serving_ideas: phulka, paratha or bhakri, with dal and curd.
Best time: lunch or dinner; also great in tiffin boxes.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1–2 days.

recipes.description: Potato and brinjal in a tangy pickle-spiced gravy.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Wash and cut the potato and brinjal into bite-sized pieces.

steps.title: Make the gravy
steps.text: Heat mustard oil until it smokes lightly, lower the flame and add the pickle spices (fennel, kalonji, methi, mustard). Sauté the onion until golden, add ginger, garlic and tomato and cook until thick. Lower the flame and stir in the whisked curd.

steps.title: Adjust
steps.text: Add water as needed for a medium-thick gravy, add salt and bring to a gentle boil.

steps.title: Add the main ingredients
steps.text: Add the potato and brinjal and stir gently to coat with the gravy.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Cover and simmer on low flame for 12 minutes until everything is cooked and the flavours blend.

steps.title: Finish & serve
steps.text: Add the coriander leaves and serve hot.

tips: Cook the masala until oil separates; this removes the raw taste and gives a rich gravy with less fat.
Add paneer or soft vegetables at the end so they stay soft and hold their shape.
serving_ideas: phulka, multigrain roti, jeera rice or brown rice.
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2 days. Reheat gently, adding a splash of water.

steps.title: Make the gravy
steps.text: Heat oil and sauté the onion petals for 2 minutes; remove. In the same pan, crackle cumin, sauté chopped onion until golden, add ginger, garlic, tomato and spices and cook until thick.

steps.title: Adjust
steps.text: Add water as needed for a medium-thick gravy, add salt and bring to a gentle boil.

steps.title: Add the main ingredients
steps.text: Add the mushrooms and stir gently to coat with the gravy.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Cover and simmer on low flame for 6 minutes until everything is cooked and the flavours blend.

steps.title: Finish & serve
steps.text: Add the coriander leaves and serve hot.

tips: Cook the masala until oil separates; this removes the raw taste and gives a rich gravy with less fat.
Add paneer or soft vegetables at the end so they stay soft and hold their shape.
serving_ideas: phulka, multigrain roti, jeera rice or brown rice.
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2 days. Reheat gently, adding a splash of water.

recipes.description: Rajasthani winter khichdi of whole pearl millet and moong dal.

steps.title: Wash & soak
steps.text: Wash the bajra and moong dal together until the water runs clear and soak for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee in a pressure cooker, crackle the cumin, add hing, ginger and green chilli.

steps.title: Toast
steps.text: Add the drained grains and stir for 1 minute.

steps.title: Add grains & water
steps.text: Add the drained grains, turmeric, salt and 720 ml water. Stir well.

steps.title: Pressure-cook
steps.text: Cook for 6–7 whistles on medium flame. Let the pressure release naturally.

steps.title: Adjust
steps.text: Open, mash lightly and add hot water if you like a softer, porridge-like consistency.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with a spoon of ghee, curd and roasted papad.

tips: A softer, mushier khichdi is easier to digest when you are unwell.
Add a little extra ghee on top just before serving for aroma.
serving_ideas: curd, kadhi or raita, roasted papad and a pickle (in moderation).
Best time: dinner; ideal when unwell.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh; keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

recipes.description: A pink pulao with grated beetroot.

steps.title: Rinse & soak
steps.text: Wash the basmati rice 3–4 times until the water runs clear and soak for 20 minutes. Drain.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee and oil in a heavy pot or cooker. Add the whole spices and fry for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the onion and sauté until light golden, then ginger, garlic and green chilli.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the beetroot and green peas and sauté for 2–3 minutes.

steps.title: Add the basmati rice
steps.text: Add the drained grain and stir gently for 1–2 minutes to coat it with ghee.

steps.title: Add water
steps.text: Add 400 ml hot water and salt; taste the water, it should be slightly salty.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Cover and cook on the lowest flame for 12–15 minutes (or 1 whistle in a pressure cooker) until the water is absorbed and the grains are tender.

steps.title: Rest & fluff
steps.text: Rest covered for 5–10 minutes, then fluff gently with a fork. Garnish and serve.

tips: Rest the rice for 5 minutes after cooking; the grains firm up and stay separate.
Use a heavy-bottomed pot and the lowest flame so the bottom does not burn.
serving_ideas: raita, a green salad and papad (roasted).
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day. Reheat with a sprinkle of water.

recipes.description: Karnataka’s hot, spicy rice-lentil-vegetable one-pot meal.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: Wash and cook the rice with water and salt until each grain is soft but separate. Spread on a plate to cool completely.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat the oil and crackle the mustard seeds, then add the urad dal, chana dal, dry red chillies, curry leaves, hing and peanuts and fry until the dals and nuts turn golden.

steps.title: Cook the vegetables
steps.text: Cook the vegetables with tamarind water, bisi bele bath powder and jaggery until tender.

steps.title: Add dal
steps.text: Add the cooked dal and simmer for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Add the cooled rice and gently fold everything together without mashing the grains.

steps.title: Rest & serve
steps.text: Rest for 10 minutes so the flavours soak in. Garnish and serve warm or at room temperature.

tips: Use cooled, day-old or fully cooled rice so the grains stay separate.
serving_ideas: curd or raita, a poriyal and roasted papad.
Best time: lunch and lunch boxes; ideal for travel.
recipes.storage: keeps for 6–8 hours at room temperature (great for travel) or 1 day in the fridge.

recipes.description: Chicken biryani made with brown rice for extra fibre.

steps.title: Soak the rice
steps.text: Wash the brown rice gently 3–4 times and soak for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Marinate the chicken for at least 1 hour.

steps.title: Caramelise the onions
steps.text: Heat oil and half the ghee in a heavy pot and fry the sliced onions on medium flame, stirring, until deep golden (12–15 minutes). Remove half for layering.

steps.title: Cook the base
steps.text: Add the marinated chicken to the remaining onions and cook on medium flame until almost done and the masala is thick.

steps.title: Par-boil the rice
steps.text: Boil the water with salt and whole spices. Add the drained rice and cook for 5–6 minutes until 70% done (the grain should still have a bite). Drain.

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: Spread the rice over the base. Top with fried onions, mint, coriander, garam masala, saffron soaked in warm milk and the remaining ghee.

steps.title: Dum
steps.text: Cover tightly (seal with foil or dough) and cook on the lowest flame for 25 minutes, or place the pot on a hot tawa.

steps.title: Rest & serve
steps.text: Rest for 10 minutes, then gently mix from the side and serve with raita.

tips: Par-boil the rice only 70%; it finishes cooking on dum.
Use a heavy pot or place it on a tawa so the bottom layer does not burn.
serving_ideas: onion-cucumber raita and a fresh salad.
Best time: lunch or festive meals.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1–2 days; sprinkle water and reheat covered.

recipes.description: Vegetable fried rice made with brown rice.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: Cook the brown rice until just done, spread on a plate and cool completely (day-old rice is ideal).

steps.title: Heat the wok
steps.text: Heat oil in a wok on the highest flame until it just starts to smoke.

steps.title: Aromatics
steps.text: Add garlic, ginger and the white part of the spring onions and stir-fry for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Stir-fry
steps.text: Add the vegetables and sweet corn kernels and green peas and toss on high heat for 2–3 minutes; they should stay crunchy.

steps.title: Add rice
steps.text: Add the cold rice, soy sauce, vinegar, pepper and a little salt. Toss on high heat for 2 minutes, breaking up any lumps.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Add the spring onion greens, toss once and serve immediately.

tips: Use cold rice and a very hot wok so the rice does not turn mushy.
Low-sodium soy sauce keeps the salt in check.
serving_ideas: a bowl of clear soup or a light Indo-Chinese gravy.
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh; keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

recipes.description: A low-GI biryani made with foxtail millet instead of rice.

steps.title: Soak the rice
steps.text: Wash the foxtail millet gently 3–4 times and soak for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Mix the carrot, french beans, green peas and cauliflower with the marinade ingredients and rest for at least 30 minutes.

steps.title: Caramelise the onions
steps.text: Heat oil and half the ghee in a heavy pot and fry the sliced onions on medium flame, stirring, until deep golden (12–15 minutes). Remove half for layering.

steps.title: Cook the base
steps.text: Add the marinated carrot, french beans, green peas and cauliflower to the remaining onions and cook on medium flame until almost done and the masala is thick.

steps.title: Par-boil the rice
steps.text: Boil the water with salt and whole spices. Add the drained rice and cook for 5–6 minutes until 70% done (the grain should still have a bite). Drain.

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: Spread the rice over the base. Top with fried onions, mint, coriander, garam masala, saffron soaked in warm milk and the remaining ghee.

steps.title: Dum
steps.text: Cover tightly (seal with foil or dough) and cook on the lowest flame for 20 minutes, or place the pot on a hot tawa.

steps.title: Rest & serve
steps.text: Rest for 10 minutes, then gently mix from the side and serve with raita.

tips: Par-boil the rice only 70%; it finishes cooking on dum.
Use a heavy pot or place it on a tawa so the bottom layer does not burn.
serving_ideas: onion-cucumber raita and a fresh salad.
Best time: lunch or festive meals.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1–2 days; sprinkle water and reheat covered.

recipes.description: The ultimate Indian comfort food: rice and moong dal cooked soft with ghee and cumin, easy to digest.

steps.title: Wash & soak
steps.text: Wash the rice and moong dal together until the water runs clear and soak for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee in a pressure cooker, crackle the cumin, add hing, ginger and green chilli.

steps.title: Toast
steps.text: Add the drained grains and stir for 1 minute.

steps.title: Add grains & water
steps.text: Add the drained grains, turmeric, salt and 800 ml water. Stir well.

steps.title: Pressure-cook
steps.text: Cook for 3–4 whistles on medium flame. Let the pressure release naturally.

steps.title: Adjust
steps.text: Open, mash lightly and add hot water if you like a softer, porridge-like consistency.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with a spoon of ghee, curd and roasted papad.

tips: A softer, mushier khichdi is easier to digest when you are unwell.
Add a little extra ghee on top just before serving for aroma.
serving_ideas: curd, kadhi or raita, roasted papad and a pickle (in moderation).
Best time: dinner; ideal when unwell.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh; keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

steps.text: Heat oil in a wok on the highest flame until it just starts to smoke.

steps.text: Add the vegetables and mushrooms and toss on high heat for 2–3 minutes; they should stay crunchy.

steps.text: Wash the basmati rice 3–4 times until the water runs clear and soak for 20 minutes. Drain.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee and oil in a heavy pot or cooker. Add the whole spices and fry for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the onion and sauté until light golden, then ginger, garlic and green chilli.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the rajma and tomato and sauté for 2–3 minutes.

steps.title: Add the basmati rice
steps.text: Add the drained grain and stir gently for 1–2 minutes to coat it with ghee.

steps.title: Add water
steps.text: Add 360 ml hot water and salt; taste the water, it should be slightly salty.

recipes.description: High-protein biryani with soya chunks.

steps.title: Soak the rice
steps.text: Wash the basmati rice gently 3–4 times and soak for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Mix the soya chunks and green peas with the marinade ingredients and rest for at least 30 minutes.

steps.title: Caramelise the onions
steps.text: Heat oil and half the ghee in a heavy pot and fry the sliced onions on medium flame, stirring, until deep golden (12–15 minutes). Remove half for layering.

steps.title: Cook the base
steps.text: Add the marinated soya chunks and green peas to the remaining onions and cook on medium flame until almost done and the masala is thick.

steps.text: Spread the rice over the base. Top with fried onions, mint, coriander, garam masala, saffron soaked in warm milk and the remaining ghee.

steps.title: Dum
steps.text: Cover tightly (seal with foil or dough) and cook on the lowest flame for 15 minutes, or place the pot on a hot tawa.

steps.title: Rest & serve
steps.text: Rest for 10 minutes, then gently mix from the side and serve with raita.

tips: Par-boil the rice only 70%; it finishes cooking on dum.
Use a heavy pot or place it on a tawa so the bottom layer does not burn.

recipes.description: A vivid beetroot soup, rich in folate and nitrates.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Wash and roughly chop the beetroot, carrot and tomato.

steps.title: Sauté
steps.text: Heat oil in a pot and sauté the garlic, ginger and onion for 2–3 minutes until soft and fragrant.

steps.title: Add vegetables
steps.text: Add the beetroot, carrot and tomato and sauté for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Add the water and salt, bring to a boil and simmer covered for 15 minutes until soft.

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: Cool slightly and blend until smooth. Strain if you like a silky soup.

steps.title: Reheat
steps.text: Return to the pot, adjust the thickness with hot water and bring to a gentle boil.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Add pepper and check the salt.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Pour into bowls, garnish with the coriander leaves and lemon juice and serve hot.

tips: Thicken soups with a little blended potato, oats or dal instead of cornflour or cream.
Add lemon juice only after switching off the heat.
serving_ideas: a slice of whole-wheat toast or a small salad.
Best time: as a starter or a light dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2 days; can be frozen for 1 month (without cream).

steps.text: Cool slightly and blend until smooth. Strain if you like a silky soup.

recipes.description: A tangy amla chutney packed with vitamin C.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Wash and roughly chop the amla, coriander leaves, green chilli and ginger.

steps.title: Grind
steps.text: Put everything in a mixer jar and grind to a smooth (or slightly coarse) paste, adding water a spoon at a time.

steps.title: Taste
steps.text: Check the salt, sourness and heat and adjust.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Transfer to a bowl and serve fresh.

tips: Grind with a little ice-cold water to keep green chutneys bright.
A squeeze of lemon helps green chutneys keep their colour.
serving_ideas: dosa, idli, chila, paratha, sandwiches or as a dip for snacks.
Use 1–2 tbsp per serving.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2–3 days.

recipes.description: Paneer tikka in a tangy pickle-spice marinade.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Cut the paneer, capsicum and onion into even 1½-inch pieces.

steps.title: Make the marinade
steps.text: Whisk hung curd with roasted besan, ginger-garlic, spices, lemon juice, mustard oil and salt into a thick paste.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Coat everything well and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes (up to 4 hours).

steps.title: Skewer
steps.text: Thread onto skewers (soak wooden ones in water for 20 minutes first), alternating with capsicum and onion.

steps.title: Grill
steps.text: Grill in an oven, air fryer or on a grill pan at 200°C for 12–15 minutes, turning once, until charred at the edges. Brush with a few drops of oil halfway.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Sprinkle chaat masala and lemon juice and serve hot with onion rings and mint chutney.

tips: Use thick hung curd so the marinade clings and does not drip.
Roasted besan in the marinade helps it stick and adds a smoky flavour.
serving_ideas: mint chutney and an onion-cucumber salad.
Best time: starter or a high-protein snack.
recipes.storage: marinated pieces keep in the fridge for 1 day; grill just before serving.

recipes.description: Crisp colocasia slices with ajwain and chilli.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Wash, dry and slice the arbi as listed.

steps.title: Coat
steps.text: Mix the coating ingredients into a thick batter (or dry rub) and toss the arbi so every piece is coated.

steps.title: Preheat
steps.text: Preheat the air fryer to 190°C for 3 minutes and brush the basket with oil.

steps.title: Arrange
steps.text: Place the pieces in a single layer without overlapping. Spray or brush lightly with oil.

steps.title: Air-fry
steps.text: Cook for 12–15 minutes, shaking or turning halfway, until golden and crisp.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with green chutney.

tips: Do not overcrowd the basket; crispness needs hot air around every piece.
No air fryer? Bake at 210°C for 18–20 minutes, turning once.
serving_ideas: green chutney or hung curd dip, and a cup of tea or buttermilk.
Best time: evening snack or a starter.
recipes.storage: best eaten hot and fresh.

recipes.description: The classic street-style potato tikki, pan-roasted instead of fried.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Boil, steam or chop the potato, green peas, green chilli, ginger and coriander leaves as listed and let them cool.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Combine everything in a bowl and mash well. The mixture should hold its shape when pressed; add a little more cornflour if it is too soft.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Grease your palms and shape into 8 round, flat tikkis about ½ inch thick.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Refrigerate for 15 minutes so they hold firm while cooking.

steps.title: Pan-roast
steps.text: Heat a non-stick tawa, brush with oil and cook the tikkis on medium flame for 3–4 minutes per side until golden and crisp.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with green chutney or hung curd dip.

tips: Chilling the tikkis before cooking stops them from breaking.
Use a non-stick pan and a light brush of oil; there is no need to deep-fry.
serving_ideas: green chutney or hung curd dip, and a cup of tea or buttermilk.
Best time: evening snack or a starter.
Stuff in a whole-wheat wrap with salad for a quick meal.
recipes.storage: uncooked tikkis keep in the fridge for 1 day or can be frozen for 1 month.

recipes.description: Khaman dhokla with crushed sweet corn, loved by children.

steps.title: Make the batter
steps.text: Mix the besan, sweet corn kernels, curd, ginger, green chilli and turmeric powder and salt with enough water to make a smooth, thick, pourable batter.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Cover and rest the batter for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare the steamer
steps.text: Boil water in a steamer or large pot with a stand. Grease a 7-inch tin or plate with oil.

steps.title: Add the leavening
steps.text: Just before steaming, add the fruit salt with 1 tsp water and stir gently in one direction until frothy.

steps.title: Steam
steps.text: Pour into the greased tin immediately and steam on medium-high flame for 15 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the centre comes out clean.

steps.title: Cool & cut
steps.text: Rest for 5 minutes, then cut into squares or diamonds.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat oil, crackle the mustard seeds and sesame, add curry leaves, green chillies and hing. Add water and lemon juice and pour evenly over the pieces.

steps.title: Garnish & serve
steps.text: Sprinkle with coriander and coconut and serve.

tips: Do not open the steamer for the first 10 minutes; the batter can collapse.
Pour the tempering water slowly so the pieces stay soft and moist.
serving_ideas: green chutney or hung curd dip, and a cup of tea or buttermilk.
Best time: evening snack or a starter.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day; best at room temperature.

recipes.description: Steamed cabbage muthia, crunchy outside after tempering.

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: Mix the whole-wheat flour, besan, rava / suji and cabbage with ginger, chilli, spices, sesame, lemon juice, sugar, salt, soda and oil. Knead into a soft dough without water (or just a few drops).

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Grease your palms and shape into 4–5 cylindrical rolls about 1 inch thick.

steps.title: Steam
steps.text: Steam the rolls on a greased plate for 20–25 minutes, until a knife comes out clean.

steps.title: Cool & slice
steps.text: Cool for 10 minutes and slice into ½-inch rounds.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat oil, crackle mustard and sesame, add curry leaves and hing, then the muthia slices.

steps.title: Crisp
steps.text: Toss on medium flame for 4–5 minutes until lightly crisp.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with coriander and serve with green chutney and tea.

tips: Do not add water; the vegetables release enough moisture.
Steamed muthia keep in the fridge for 2 days; temper just before serving.
serving_ideas: green chutney or hung curd dip, and a cup of tea or buttermilk.
Best time: evening snack or a starter.
recipes.storage: steamed rolls keep in the fridge for 2 days.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Cut the cauliflower, capsicum and onion into even 1½-inch pieces.

steps.text: Whisk hung curd with roasted besan, ginger-garlic, spices, lemon juice, mustard oil and salt into a thick paste.

steps.text: Coat everything well and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes (up to 4 hours).

steps.text: Grill in an oven, air fryer or on a grill pan at 200°C for 12–15 minutes, turning once, until charred at the edges. Brush with a few drops of oil halfway.

tips: Use thick hung curd so the marinade clings and does not drip.

Best time: starter or a high-protein snack.
recipes.storage: marinated pieces keep in the fridge for 1 day; grill just before serving.

recipes.description: Soft, spongy steamed gram flour cakes from Gujarat, light and high in protein.

steps.title: Make the batter
steps.text: Mix the besan, curd, ginger, green chilli, turmeric powder, sugar and lemon juice and salt with enough water to make a smooth, thick, pourable batter.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Cover and rest the batter for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare the steamer
steps.text: Boil water in a steamer or large pot with a stand. Grease a 7-inch tin or plate with oil.

steps.title: Add the leavening
steps.text: Just before steaming, add the fruit salt with 1 tsp water and stir gently in one direction until frothy.

steps.title: Steam
steps.text: Pour into the greased tin immediately and steam on medium-high flame for 15 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the centre comes out clean.

steps.title: Cool & cut
steps.text: Rest for 5 minutes, then cut into squares or diamonds.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat oil, crackle the mustard seeds and sesame, add curry leaves, green chillies and hing. Add water and lemon juice and pour evenly over the pieces.

steps.title: Garnish & serve
steps.text: Sprinkle with coriander and coconut and serve.

tips: Do not open the steamer for the first 10 minutes; the batter can collapse.
Pour the tempering water slowly so the pieces stay soft and moist.
serving_ideas: green chutney or hung curd dip, and a cup of tea or buttermilk.
Best time: evening snack or a starter.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day; best at room temperature.

steps.title: Make the batter

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Cover and rest the batter for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare the steamer
steps.text: Boil water in a steamer or large pot with a stand. Grease a 7-inch tin or plate with oil.

steps.title: Add the leavening
steps.text: Just before steaming, add the fruit salt with 1 tsp water and stir gently in one direction until frothy.

steps.title: Steam
steps.text: Pour into the greased tin immediately and steam on medium-high flame for 15 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the centre comes out clean.

steps.title: Cool & cut
steps.text: Rest for 5 minutes, then cut into squares or diamonds.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat oil, crackle the mustard seeds and sesame, add curry leaves, green chillies and hing. Add water and lemon juice and pour evenly over the pieces.

steps.title: Garnish & serve
steps.text: Sprinkle with coriander and coconut and serve.

tips: Do not open the steamer for the first 10 minutes; the batter can collapse.
Pour the tempering water slowly so the pieces stay soft and moist.
serving_ideas: green chutney or hung curd dip, and a cup of tea or buttermilk.
Best time: evening snack or a starter.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day; best at room temperature.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Grease your palms and shape into 8 round, flat tikkis about ½ inch thick.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Refrigerate for 15 minutes so they hold firm while cooking.

steps.title: Pan-roast
steps.text: Heat a non-stick tawa, brush with oil and cook the tikkis on medium flame for 3–4 minutes per side until golden and crisp.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with green chutney or hung curd dip.

tips: Chilling the tikkis before cooking stops them from breaking.
Use a non-stick pan and a light brush of oil; there is no need to deep-fry.
serving_ideas: green chutney or hung curd dip, and a cup of tea or buttermilk.
Best time: evening snack or a starter.
Stuff in a whole-wheat wrap with salad for a quick meal.
recipes.storage: uncooked tikkis keep in the fridge for 1 day or can be frozen for 1 month.

recipes.description: Paneer slices in a spiced besan coating, air-fried until crisp.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Wash, dry and slice the paneer as listed.

steps.title: Coat
steps.text: Mix the coating ingredients into a thick batter (or dry rub) and toss the paneer so every piece is coated.

steps.title: Preheat
steps.text: Preheat the air fryer to 190°C for 3 minutes and brush the basket with oil.

steps.title: Arrange
steps.text: Place the pieces in a single layer without overlapping. Spray or brush lightly with oil.

steps.title: Air-fry
steps.text: Cook for 12–15 minutes, shaking or turning halfway, until golden and crisp.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with green chutney.

tips: Do not overcrowd the basket; crispness needs hot air around every piece.
No air fryer? Bake at 210°C for 18–20 minutes, turning once.
serving_ideas: green chutney or hung curd dip, and a cup of tea or buttermilk.
Best time: evening snack or a starter.
recipes.storage: best eaten hot and fresh.

recipes.description: Smoky, charred cubes of spiced paneer with peppers and onion, made in the oven or air fryer.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Cut the paneer, capsicum and onion into even 1½-inch pieces.

steps.title: Make the marinade
steps.text: Whisk hung curd with roasted besan, ginger-garlic, spices, lemon juice, mustard oil and salt into a thick paste.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Coat everything well and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes (up to 4 hours).

steps.title: Skewer
steps.text: Thread onto skewers (soak wooden ones in water for 20 minutes first), alternating with capsicum and onion.

steps.title: Grill
steps.text: Grill in an oven, air fryer or on a grill pan at 200°C for 12–15 minutes, turning once, until charred at the edges. Brush with a few drops of oil halfway.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Sprinkle chaat masala and lemon juice and serve hot with onion rings and mint chutney.

tips: Use thick hung curd so the marinade clings and does not drip.
Roasted besan in the marinade helps it stick and adds a smoky flavour.
serving_ideas: mint chutney and an onion-cucumber salad.
Best time: starter or a high-protein snack.
recipes.storage: marinated pieces keep in the fridge for 1 day; grill just before serving.

recipes.description: Gujarati colocasia leaf rolls with a sweet-sour besan paste, steamed and tempered.

steps.title: Prepare the leaves
steps.text: Wash the leaves, remove the thick veins and pat dry.

steps.title: Make the paste
steps.text: Mix besan with tamarind, jaggery, spices and water into a thick paste.

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: Place a leaf vein-side up, spread paste thinly, place another leaf over it and repeat for 3–4 layers.

steps.title: Roll
steps.text: Fold in the sides and roll tightly into a log.

steps.title: Steam
steps.text: Steam for 25 minutes. Cool and slice into rounds.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat oil, crackle mustard and sesame, add curry leaves and hing and pour over.

steps.title: Garnish & serve
steps.text: Sprinkle coconut and coriander and serve at room temperature.

tips: Keep all the components ready before you start; the process moves quickly.
serving_ideas: green chutney or hung curd dip, and a cup of tea or buttermilk.
Best time: evening snack or a starter.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

recipes.description: Boiled peanuts tempered with coconut and curry leaves.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Pressure-cook the raw peanuts with salt for 3–4 whistles.

steps.title: Drain
steps.text: Drain well; keep the water for soups or dal.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat coconut oil, crackle mustard seeds, add urad dal, dry red chillies, curry leaves, hing, green chilli and ginger.

steps.title: Toss
steps.text: Add the cooked peanuts and salt and toss for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Switch off, add the grated coconut, lemon juice and coriander and mix.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve warm as an evening snack.

tips: Cook the legumes until soft but still whole; mushy legumes make a sticky sundal.
serving_ideas: a cup of tea or buttermilk.
Best time: evening snack; a traditional Navratri offering.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

recipes.description: Makhana tossed in a smoky, spicy peri-peri style spice mix.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Measure out the makhana.

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Heat the ghee in a wide pan on low flame. Add the makhana and roast, stirring often, for 10 minutes until crisp and crunchy.

steps.title: Test
steps.text: Cool one piece for a few seconds and bite; it should break with a crunch.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Switch off the flame and sprinkle the kashmiri red chilli powder, dried oregano / mixed herbs, garlic and amchur. Toss well.

steps.title: Cool & store
steps.text: Cool completely before storing in an airtight jar.

tips: Roast on low heat; high heat browns the outside while the inside stays chewy.
Store only after cooling completely, or it turns soggy.
serving_ideas: a cup of tea, green tea or buttermilk.
A perfect office or travel snack.
recipes.storage: keeps crisp in an airtight jar for 1–2 weeks.

recipes.description: Protein-rich dhokla from ground quinoa and besan.

steps.title: Make the batter
steps.text: Mix the quinoa, besan, curd, ginger and green chilli and salt with enough water to make a smooth, thick, pourable batter.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Cover and rest the batter for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare the steamer
steps.text: Boil water in a steamer or large pot with a stand. Grease a 7-inch tin or plate with oil.

steps.title: Add the leavening
steps.text: Just before steaming, add the fruit salt with 1 tsp water and stir gently in one direction until frothy.

steps.title: Steam
steps.text: Pour into the greased tin immediately and steam on medium-high flame for 15 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the centre comes out clean.

steps.title: Cool & cut
steps.text: Rest for 5 minutes, then cut into squares or diamonds.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat oil, crackle the mustard seeds and sesame, add curry leaves, green chillies and hing. Add water and lemon juice and pour evenly over the pieces.

steps.title: Garnish & serve
steps.text: Sprinkle with coriander and coconut and serve.

tips: Do not open the steamer for the first 10 minutes; the batter can collapse.
Pour the tempering water slowly so the pieces stay soft and moist.
serving_ideas: green chutney or hung curd dip, and a cup of tea or buttermilk.
Best time: evening snack or a starter.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day; best at room temperature.

recipes.description: A colourful sundal of corn and peas.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Steam the corn and peas for 6 minutes.

steps.text: Drain well; keep the water for soups or dal.

steps.text: Heat coconut oil, crackle mustard seeds, add urad dal, dry red chillies, curry leaves, hing, green chilli and ginger.

steps.text: Add the cooked sweet corn kernels and green peas and salt and toss for 2 minutes.

recipes.description: Mildly sweet, crisp sweet potato tikkis.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Combine everything in a bowl and mash well. The mixture should hold its shape when pressed; add a little more rajgira if it is too soft.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Grease your palms and shape into 8 round, flat tikkis about ½ inch thick.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Refrigerate for 15 minutes so they hold firm while cooking.

steps.title: Pan-roast
steps.text: Heat a non-stick tawa, brush with oil and cook the tikkis on medium flame for 3–4 minutes per side until golden and crisp.

recipes.description: Baby potatoes in a tandoori marinade, grilled until crisp.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Cut the potato, capsicum and onion into even 1½-inch pieces.

steps.title: Make the marinade
steps.text: Whisk hung curd with roasted besan, ginger-garlic, spices, lemon juice, mustard oil and salt into a thick paste.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Coat everything well and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes (up to 4 hours).

steps.title: Skewer
steps.text: Thread onto skewers (soak wooden ones in water for 20 minutes first), alternating with capsicum and onion.

steps.title: Grill
steps.text: Grill in an oven, air fryer or on a grill pan at 200°C for 12–15 minutes, turning once, until charred at the edges. Brush with a few drops of oil halfway.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Sprinkle chaat masala and lemon juice and serve hot with onion rings and mint chutney.

tips: Use thick hung curd so the marinade clings and does not drip.
Roasted besan in the marinade helps it stick and adds a smoky flavour.
serving_ideas: mint chutney and an onion-cucumber salad.
Best time: starter or a high-protein snack.
recipes.storage: marinated pieces keep in the fridge for 1 day; grill just before serving.

steps.title: Roast the eggs
steps.text: Toss the eggs in ½ tsp oil with a pinch of turmeric and chilli for 2 minutes until lightly golden. Set aside.

steps.title: Make the gravy
steps.text: Heat coconut oil, crackle mustard seeds, add curry leaves and onion and sauté until soft. Add ginger, garlic, tomato and spices, cook until soft, then add coconut milk.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Add water to the consistency you like, add salt and simmer for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Add the eggs
steps.text: Add the eggs and simmer for 4–5 minutes so they absorb the flavours.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with coriander and serve hot.

tips: Slit the boiled eggs so the gravy flavours them all the way through.
serving_ideas: phulka, jeera rice or brown rice, with a salad and curd.

steps.title: Chop
steps.text: Finely chop the rolled oats, onion, tomato and green chilli.

steps.title: Beat
steps.text: Beat the eggs with turmeric, pepper and salt until frothy (about 30 seconds).

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Stir the chopped ingredients into the beaten eggs.

steps.title: Heat the pan
steps.text: Heat a non-stick pan on medium flame and brush with oil.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Pour in the egg mixture and swirl to spread. Cook on medium-low flame for 2 minutes until the bottom is set and lightly golden.

steps.title: Flip or fold
steps.text: Flip carefully (or fold in half) and cook for 1 minute more until fully set.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with whole-wheat toast or a roti.

tips: Cook on medium-low heat so the omelette sets evenly without browning too much.

recipes.description: Chicken in a tangy gravy flavoured with pickling spices.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Wash and drain the chicken. Mix with the marinade ingredients and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes (overnight is best).

steps.title: Make the masala
steps.text: Heat mustard oil until it smokes, lower the flame and add the pickle spices. Sauté the onion until golden, add ginger-garlic and tomato, then the spices. Stir in the whisked curd on low flame.

steps.title: Add the chicken
steps.text: Add the marinated chicken and cook on high flame for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until it changes colour and is coated in masala.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Add water as needed, cover and simmer on low flame for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is tender and cooked through.

steps.title: Check
steps.text: The chicken is done when the juices run clear and there is no pink near the bone.

steps.title: Finish & serve
steps.text: Add the coriander leaves and serve hot.

tips: Use skinless chicken to cut saturated fat.
Simmer gently; boiling hard makes chicken tough.
serving_ideas: phulka, jeera rice or brown rice, with a salad and curd.
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2 days; freezes for 1 month.

recipes.description: Creamy, pepper-flavoured Afghani-style grilled chicken.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Clean the chicken, pat dry and make deep slits so the marinade penetrates.

steps.title: First marinade
steps.text: Rub with lemon juice, salt and chilli and rest for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Second marinade
steps.text: Mix the remaining marinade ingredients into a thick paste, coat well and refrigerate for at least 2 hours (overnight is best).

steps.title: Preheat
steps.text: Preheat the oven or air fryer to 200°C.

steps.title: Grill
steps.text: Grill for 22–27 minutes, turning once and brushing with a few drops of oil, until charred at the edges and cooked through.

steps.title: Rest & serve
steps.text: Rest for 3 minutes, sprinkle chaat masala and lemon and serve with onion rings and mint chutney.

tips: Hung curd marinade keeps the meat juicy without frying.
Check doneness at the thickest part; there should be no pink.
serving_ideas: mint chutney, onion rings and a green salad.
Best time: a high-protein starter or dinner.
recipes.storage: marinated meat keeps in the fridge for 1 day; cooked tikka keeps 1 day.

recipes.description: Mutton slow-roasted in its own juices with a thick, dark masala.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Wash the mutton, drain well and mix with the marinade. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight.

steps.title: Make the masala
steps.text: Heat oil, add the whole spices, then the onions, and sauté until deep golden (12–15 minutes). Add ginger and garlic, then the tomato purée and powdered spices, and cook until the oil separates. Keep stirring (bhuno) until the masala darkens and clings to the meat.

steps.title: Bhuno
steps.text: Add the marinated mutton and cook on high flame, stirring often, for 8–10 minutes until it is well coated and the masala starts to stick.

steps.title: Pressure-cook
steps.text: Add 1½ cups hot water and pressure-cook for 5–6 whistles on medium flame (or simmer covered for 1½ hours) until the mutton is tender.

steps.title: Reduce
steps.text: Open the cooker and simmer uncovered to the consistency you like.

steps.title: Finish & serve
steps.text: Skim off any surface fat, add the coriander leaves and serve hot.

tips: Choose lean cuts and trim visible fat to lower saturated fat.
Skim the fat that rises after cooking; it makes a big difference.
serving_ideas: phulka, jeera rice or brown rice, with a salad and curd.
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2 days; tastes better the next day. Freezes for 1 month.

recipes.description: Tangy, spicy Andhra tamarind fish curry.

steps.title: Clean & season
steps.text: Wash the fish fillets well, pat dry and rub with turmeric, chilli and salt. Rest for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Sear (optional)
steps.text: Lightly sear the pieces in a non-stick pan with a few drops of oil for 1 minute per side; this helps them hold their shape.

steps.title: Make the curry
steps.text: Temper mustard and methi seeds and curry leaves, sauté onion and tomato, add the spices and tamarind extract and simmer 10 minutes.

steps.title: Boil
steps.text: Add water as needed, check the salt and bring to a gentle boil.

steps.title: Add the fish
steps.text: Slide in the pieces in a single layer. Simmer for 8 minutes without stirring; swirl the pan gently instead.

steps.title: Rest & serve
steps.text: Switch off, cover and rest for 10 minutes so the flavours develop. Serve hot.

tips: Do not stir after adding the fish; swirl the pan so the pieces stay whole.
Fish cooks fast; it is done when it flakes easily.
serving_ideas: steamed rice or red rice, with a vegetable side.
Best time: lunch.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day. Reheat gently.

recipes.description: Kheer made with grated apple stirred into thickened milk, sweetened only with dates.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Peel and grate the apple and cook it for 3 minutes; cool. Reduce the milk first and add the apple only after it cools slightly, so the milk does not split.

steps.title: Boil the toned milk
steps.text: Bring the toned milk to a boil in a heavy-bottomed pan, stirring so it does not stick.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Add the apple and simmer on low flame for 20 minutes, stirring often and scraping the sides, until soft and creamy.

steps.title: Flavour
steps.text: Add the cardamom and saffron and simmer for 2 more minutes.

steps.title: Sweeten
steps.text: Switch off the flame and let it cool for 5 minutes, then stir in the dates. Adding jaggery off the heat keeps the milk from curdling.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with the almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled.

tips: Use a heavy-bottomed pan and stir often so the milk does not burn.
Kheer thickens as it cools; add a little warm milk to loosen it.
serving_ideas: enjoy a small portion after a meal, or with a cup of tea.
Keep sweets to a small bowl or 1–2 pieces.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

steps.text: Prepare the whole-wheat flour as listed.

steps.text: Heat the ghee and roast the whole-wheat flour on low flame, stirring constantly, until golden and aromatic.

steps.title: Add the liquid
steps.text: Add the water (it will splutter, so pour carefully) and stir continuously.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Cook on medium-low flame for 6 minutes, stirring often, until the liquid is absorbed and the halwa thickens.

steps.title: Sweeten
steps.text: Add the jaggery and cardamom and cook for 3–4 minutes until the halwa leaves the sides of the pan.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with the almonds and cashews and serve warm.

tips: Halwa needs patient stirring on low heat; do not rush it.
This lighter version uses less ghee and jaggery instead of sugar.
serving_ideas: enjoy a small portion after a meal, or with a cup of tea.
Keep sweets to a small bowl or 1–2 pieces.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 3 days; warm before serving.

recipes.description: Soft idlis with pearl millet flour stirred into the batter.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Wash and soak the idli and bajra for 5–6 hours. Separately soak the urad dal with methi seeds for 4 hours.

steps.title: Grind the dal
steps.text: Grind the urad dal with ice-cold water, a little at a time, to a light, fluffy, smooth batter.

steps.title: Grind the grain
steps.text: Grind the soaked grain to a slightly coarse, semolina-like batter. Mix both batters well with your hand.

steps.title: Ferment
steps.text: Add salt, cover and leave in a warm place for 8–12 hours until it doubles and smells pleasantly sour.

steps.title: Prepare the steamer
steps.text: Boil 2 cups water in an idli steamer or pressure cooker (without the whistle). Grease the idli moulds lightly.

steps.title: Fill the moulds
steps.text: Gently stir the batter without knocking out the air and pour into the moulds until three-quarters full.

steps.title: Steam
steps.text: Steam on medium-high flame for 10–12 minutes. A toothpick inserted in the centre should come out clean.

steps.title: Rest & demould
steps.text: Rest for 2 minutes, then scoop out the idlis with a wet spoon and serve hot.

tips: Use a 4:1 ratio of idli rice to urad dal for soft idlis.
Do not over-stir fermented batter; it loses the air that makes idlis fluffy.
serving_ideas: sambar and coconut or tomato chutney.
Best time: breakfast; also great for tiffin boxes.
recipes.storage: batter keeps in the fridge for 3–4 days; steamed idlis keep for 1 day and can be re-steamed.

recipes.description: Barnyard millet dosa with potato masala.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Wash the barnyard millet and soak for 5–6 hours. Separately wash and soak the urad dal with the methi seeds for 4–5 hours.

steps.title: Grind
steps.text: Grind the urad dal with ice-cold water until light, fluffy and doubled in volume. Grind the soaked grain to a smooth paste. Mix both with clean hands.

steps.title: Ferment
steps.text: Add salt, cover and keep in a warm place for 8–12 hours (overnight) until the batter rises and smells mildly sour.

steps.title: Prepare the filling
steps.text: Heat oil, crackle mustard seeds and urad dal, add curry leaves, ginger, green chillies and onion and sauté until soft. Add turmeric, the potatoes, salt and 3 tbsp water, mash lightly and mix in coriander.

steps.title: Heat the tawa
steps.text: Heat a cast-iron or non-stick tawa on medium-high flame. Sprinkle water; it should sizzle and evaporate. Wipe with an oiled cloth or half an onion.

steps.title: Spread the dosa
steps.text: Pour a ladle of batter in the centre and spread it in quick outward circles into a thin round.

steps.title: Crisp it up
steps.text: Drizzle ½ tsp oil or ghee over the dosa and cook on medium flame for 1–2 minutes until the base turns golden and crisp.

steps.title: Fill & fold
steps.text: Place 2–3 tbsp of filling in the centre, fold the dosa over and lift onto a plate.

steps.title: Repeat
steps.text: Wipe the tawa with a damp cloth between dosas to cool it slightly so the batter spreads evenly.
