recipes.description: A winter besan chila with bathua greens.

steps.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps.text: Finely chop the onion and green chilli and grate the ginger. Small, even pieces keep the chila thin and help it cook evenly.

steps.title: Make the batter
steps.text: In a mixing bowl, combine the besan and bathua leaves with turmeric, ajwain, chilli powder and salt. Add water a little at a time and whisk to a smooth, lump-free batter that flows like dosa batter.

steps.title: Add vegetables & rest
steps.text: Fold in the chopped vegetables, ginger and coriander. Rest the batter for 10 minutes so it thickens slightly and the chila turns soft.

steps.title: Heat the pan
steps.text: Heat a non-stick or well-seasoned iron tawa on medium flame and brush it with ¼ tsp oil. A few drops of water should sizzle when the pan is ready.

steps.title: Spread the chila
steps.text: Pour one ladle of batter in the centre and spread it gently in circles into a 6–7 inch round. Drizzle a few drops of oil around the edges.

steps.title: Cook the first side
steps.text: Cook on medium-low flame for 2–3 minutes, until the top looks set and the edges lift easily and turn golden.

steps.title: Flip & cook
steps.text: Flip with a flat spatula and cook the other side for 1–2 minutes, pressing lightly, until golden spots appear.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with mint-coriander chutney or curd. Make the remaining chilas the same way, adding only a few drops of oil each time.

tips: Rest the batter for 10 minutes; it makes the chila softer and easier to flip.
Keep the flame medium-low so the centre cooks before the outside browns.
serving_ideas: mint-coriander chutney, plain curd or raita, and a cucumber-tomato salad.
Best time: breakfast, or an early evening meal.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh. Plain batter (without vegetables) keeps in the fridge in an airtight box for up to 12 hours.

recipes.description: Pink rava appe with beetroot.

steps.title: Prepare the batter
steps.text: Take the rava / suji and curd in a bowl; it should be thick, like idli batter.

steps.title: Add the flavourings
steps.text: Mix in the beetroot, onion, green chilli and fruit salt and salt.

steps.title: Heat the appe pan
steps.text: Heat a paniyaram (appe) pan on medium flame and add a few drops of oil to each cavity.

steps.title: Fill
steps.text: Pour batter into each cavity until three-quarters full.

steps.title: Cook covered
steps.text: Cover and cook on medium-low flame for 3–4 minutes until the base turns golden.

steps.title: Turn
steps.text: Turn each appe with a skewer or spoon handle, add a drop of oil and cook the other side for 2–3 minutes.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with coconut or tomato chutney.

tips: Keep the flame medium-low so the appe cooks through without burning.
Leftover idli or dosa batter is perfect for appe.
serving_ideas: coconut chutney or tomato chutney.
Great for tiffin boxes and evening snacks.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh; keeps in a tiffin for 4–5 hours.

recipes.description: Pink fermented idlis with beetroot purée.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Wash and soak the idli for 5–6 hours. Separately soak the urad dal with methi seeds for 4 hours.

steps.title: Grind the dal
steps.text: Grind the urad dal with ice-cold water, a little at a time, to a light, fluffy, smooth batter.

steps.title: Grind the grain
steps.text: Grind the soaked grain to a slightly coarse, semolina-like batter. Mix both batters well with your hand.

steps.title: Ferment
steps.text: Add salt, cover and leave in a warm place for 8–12 hours until it doubles and smells pleasantly sour.

steps.title: Add flavour
steps.text: Fold the beetroot purée into the batter.

steps.title: Prepare the steamer
steps.text: Boil 2 cups water in an idli steamer or pressure cooker (without the whistle). Grease the idli moulds lightly.

steps.title: Fill the moulds
steps.text: Gently stir the batter without knocking out the air and pour into the moulds until three-quarters full.

steps.title: Steam
steps.text: Steam on medium-high flame for 10–12 minutes. A toothpick inserted in the centre should come out clean.

steps.title: Rest & demould
steps.text: Rest for 2 minutes, then scoop out the idlis with a wet spoon and serve hot.

tips: Use a 4:1 ratio of idli rice to urad dal for soft idlis.
Do not over-stir fermented batter; it loses the air that makes idlis fluffy.
serving_ideas: sambar and coconut or tomato chutney.
Best time: breakfast; also great for tiffin boxes.
recipes.storage: batter keeps in the fridge for 3–4 days; steamed idlis keep for 1 day and can be re-steamed.

recipes.description: Pink beetroot dosa with potato masala.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Wash the idli and soak for 5–6 hours. Separately wash and soak the urad dal with the methi seeds for 4–5 hours.

steps.title: Grind
steps.text: Grind the urad dal with ice-cold water until light, fluffy and doubled in volume. Grind the soaked grain to a smooth paste. Mix both with clean hands.

steps.title: Ferment
steps.text: Add salt, cover and keep in a warm place for 8–12 hours (overnight) until the batter rises and smells mildly sour.

steps.title: Flavour the batter
steps.text: Blend the beetroot to a purée and stir into the batter.

steps.title: Prepare the filling
steps.text: Heat oil, crackle mustard seeds and urad dal, add curry leaves, ginger, green chillies and onion and sauté until soft. Add turmeric, the potatoes, salt and 3 tbsp water, mash lightly and mix in coriander.

steps.title: Heat the tawa
steps.text: Heat a cast-iron or non-stick tawa on medium-high flame. Sprinkle water; it should sizzle and evaporate. Wipe with an oiled cloth or half an onion.

steps.title: Spread the dosa
steps.text: Pour a ladle of batter in the centre and spread it in quick outward circles into a thin round.

steps.title: Crisp it up
steps.text: Drizzle ½ tsp oil or ghee over the dosa and cook on medium flame for 1–2 minutes until the base turns golden and crisp.

steps.title: Fill & fold
steps.text: Place 2–3 tbsp of filling in the centre, fold the dosa over and lift onto a plate.

steps.title: Repeat
steps.text: Wipe the tawa with a damp cloth between dosas to cool it slightly so the batter spreads evenly.

tips: In cold weather, ferment the batter in a switched-off oven with the light on.
Use non-iodised salt for better fermentation.
serving_ideas: coconut chutney and sambar.

recipes.storage: fermented batter keeps in the fridge for 3–4 days. Cooked dosas are best eaten fresh.

recipes.description: Uttapam topped with grated beetroot.

steps.title: Prepare the batter
steps.text: Soak the idli for 5 hours and the urad dal with methi seeds for 4 hours. Grind separately, mix, add salt and ferment overnight.

steps.title: Thicken
steps.text: Uttapam batter should be thicker than dosa batter; do not thin it.

steps.title: Chop the topping
steps.text: Finely chop the beetroot, onion and coriander leaves and mix them together.

steps.title: Heat the tawa
steps.text: Heat a tawa on medium flame and grease it lightly.

steps.title: Spread
steps.text: Pour a ladle of batter and spread it gently into a thick 5–6 inch round.

steps.title: Add the topping
steps.text: Sprinkle 2 tbsp of the topping evenly and press it in gently with the back of the ladle.

steps.title: Cook covered
steps.text: Drizzle oil around the edges, cover and cook on medium-low flame for 3 minutes until the base is golden.

steps.title: Flip
steps.text: Flip and cook the topping side for 1–2 minutes until lightly browned.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with chutney and sambar.

tips: Cooking covered on low heat makes the uttapam soft and fully cooked inside.
Press the topping into the batter so it does not fall off when flipped.
serving_ideas: coconut chutney, tomato chutney and sambar.
Best time: breakfast or a light dinner.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh.

recipes.description: Instant rava idlis with grated carrot.

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Dry-roast the rava / suji on low flame for 3–4 minutes until aromatic. Cool.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat oil, crackle mustard seeds, add urad dal, chana dal, cashews, curry leaves, green chilli and ginger and fry until golden. Add this to the roasted base.

steps.title: Mix the batter
steps.text: Add curd, salt and enough water to make a thick, idli-like batter. Stir in the carrot.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Cover and rest for 15–20 minutes so the grains soften and swell.

steps.title: Prepare the steamer
steps.text: Boil water in the steamer and grease the idli moulds.

steps.title: Add fruit salt
steps.text: Just before steaming, add the Eno with 1 tsp water and stir gently in one direction; the batter will turn frothy.

steps.title: Steam
steps.text: Fill the moulds immediately and steam for 10–12 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Rest 2 minutes, demould and serve hot.

tips: Steam immediately after adding Eno; the bubbles fade if the batter waits.
Use fresh, slightly sour curd for the best taste.
serving_ideas: sambar and coconut or tomato chutney.
Best time: breakfast; also great for tiffin boxes.
recipes.storage: best eaten the same day; re-steam leftovers for 3 minutes.

steps.text: Grind the soaked dal with ginger, green chillies and cumin, adding water little by little, to a smooth, thick batter. It should coat the back of a spoon.

steps.text: Add hing and salt and mix in the onion and coriander leaves. The batter does not need fermentation and can be used right away.

recipes.description: Instant rava dosa with fresh coconut.

steps.title: Mix the flours
steps.text: In a large bowl, combine the rava / suji, rice flour and whole-wheat flour and curd with salt.

steps.title: Make a thin batter
steps.text: Add water gradually, whisking constantly, to make a thin, flowing batter without lumps — much thinner than regular dosa batter.

steps.title: Add flavourings & rest
steps.text: Stir in the grated coconut, onion, green chilli, curry leaves and coriander leaves. Rest for 20 minutes; the flour absorbs water, so thin it again before cooking.

steps.title: Heat the tawa
steps.text: Heat a cast-iron or non-stick tawa on medium-high flame and grease it lightly.

steps.title: Pour the dosa
steps.text: Stir the batter from the bottom and pour it from a height, starting at the edges and filling the gaps. Do not spread it with the ladle.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Drizzle ½ tsp oil and cook on medium flame for 3–4 minutes until the dosa turns golden and crisp and leaves the pan easily.

steps.text: Fold and serve immediately; instant dosas lose their crispness as they cool. Stir the batter before each dosa.

tips: These dosas are cooked on one side only; flipping is not needed.

Best time: breakfast or dinner.
recipes.storage: best made fresh. Leftover batter keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

steps.text: Wipe the tawa with a damp cloth between dosas to cool it slightly so the batter spreads evenly.

recipes.description: Instant rava appe with sweet corn.

steps.title: Prepare the batter
steps.text: Take the rava / suji and curd in a bowl; it should be thick, like idli batter.

steps.title: Add the flavourings
steps.text: Mix in the sweet corn kernels, capsicum, green chilli and fruit salt and salt.

steps.title: Heat the appe pan
steps.text: Heat a paniyaram (appe) pan on medium flame and add a few drops of oil to each cavity.

steps.title: Fill
steps.text: Pour batter into each cavity until three-quarters full.

steps.title: Cook covered
steps.text: Cover and cook on medium-low flame for 3–4 minutes until the base turns golden.

steps.title: Turn
steps.text: Turn each appe with a skewer or spoon handle, add a drop of oil and cook the other side for 2–3 minutes.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with coconut or tomato chutney.

tips: Keep the flame medium-low so the appe cooks through without burning.
Leftover idli or dosa batter is perfect for appe.
serving_ideas: coconut chutney or tomato chutney.
Great for tiffin boxes and evening snacks.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh; keeps in a tiffin for 4–5 hours.

recipes.description: Idlis with crushed sweet corn.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Wash and soak the idli for 5–6 hours. Separately soak the urad dal with methi seeds for 4 hours.

steps.title: Grind the dal
steps.text: Grind the urad dal with ice-cold water, a little at a time, to a light, fluffy, smooth batter.

steps.title: Grind the grain
steps.text: Grind the soaked grain to a slightly coarse, semolina-like batter. Mix both batters well with your hand.

steps.title: Ferment
steps.text: Add salt, cover and leave in a warm place for 8–12 hours until it doubles and smells pleasantly sour.

steps.title: Add flavour
steps.text: Fold the crushed corn into the batter.

steps.title: Prepare the steamer
steps.text: Boil 2 cups water in an idli steamer or pressure cooker (without the whistle). Grease the idli moulds lightly.

steps.title: Fill the moulds
steps.text: Gently stir the batter without knocking out the air and pour into the moulds until three-quarters full.

steps.title: Steam
steps.text: Steam on medium-high flame for 10–12 minutes. A toothpick inserted in the centre should come out clean.

steps.title: Rest & demould
steps.text: Rest for 2 minutes, then scoop out the idlis with a wet spoon and serve hot.

tips: Use a 4:1 ratio of idli rice to urad dal for soft idlis.
Do not over-stir fermented batter; it loses the air that makes idlis fluffy.
serving_ideas: sambar and coconut or tomato chutney.
Best time: breakfast; also great for tiffin boxes.
recipes.storage: batter keeps in the fridge for 3–4 days; steamed idlis keep for 1 day and can be re-steamed.

recipes.description: A soft oats chila with sweet corn and capsicum, loved by children.

steps.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps.text: Finely chop the onion, capsicum and green chilli and grate the ginger. Small, even pieces keep the chila thin and help it cook evenly.

steps.title: Make the batter
steps.text: In a mixing bowl, combine the rolled oats, besan and sweet corn kernels with turmeric, ajwain, chilli powder and salt. Add water a little at a time and whisk to a smooth, lump-free batter that flows like dosa batter.

steps.title: Add vegetables & rest
steps.text: Fold in the chopped vegetables, ginger and coriander. Rest the batter for 15 minutes so it thickens slightly and the chila turns soft.

steps.title: Heat the pan
steps.text: Heat a non-stick or well-seasoned iron tawa on medium flame and brush it with ¼ tsp oil. A few drops of water should sizzle when the pan is ready.

steps.title: Spread the chila
steps.text: Pour one ladle of batter in the centre and spread it gently in circles into a 6–7 inch round. Drizzle a few drops of oil around the edges.

steps.title: Cook the first side
steps.text: Cook on medium-low flame for 2–3 minutes, until the top looks set and the edges lift easily and turn golden.

steps.title: Flip & cook
steps.text: Flip with a flat spatula and cook the other side for 1–2 minutes, pressing lightly, until golden spots appear.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with mint-coriander chutney or curd. Make the remaining chilas the same way, adding only a few drops of oil each time.

tips: Rest the batter for 10 minutes; it makes the chila softer and easier to flip.
Keep the flame medium-low so the centre cooks before the outside browns.
serving_ideas: mint-coriander chutney, plain curd or raita, and a cucumber-tomato salad.
Best time: breakfast, or an early evening meal.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh. Plain batter (without vegetables) keeps in the fridge in an airtight box for up to 12 hours.

recipes.description: Egg-topped dosa with a potato masala filling.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Wash the idli and soak for 5–6 hours. Separately wash and soak the urad dal with the methi seeds for 4–5 hours.

steps.title: Grind
steps.text: Grind the urad dal with ice-cold water until light, fluffy and doubled in volume. Grind the soaked grain to a smooth paste. Mix both with clean hands.

steps.title: Ferment
steps.text: Add salt, cover and keep in a warm place for 8–12 hours (overnight) until the batter rises and smells mildly sour.

steps.title: Prepare the filling
steps.text: Heat oil, crackle mustard seeds and urad dal, add curry leaves, ginger, green chillies and onion and sauté until soft. Add turmeric, the potatoes, salt and 3 tbsp water, mash lightly and mix in coriander.

steps.title: Heat the tawa
steps.text: Heat a cast-iron or non-stick tawa on medium-high flame. Sprinkle water; it should sizzle and evaporate. Wipe with an oiled cloth or half an onion.

steps.title: Spread the dosa
steps.text: Pour a ladle of batter in the centre and spread it in quick outward circles into a thin round.

steps.title: Add the topping
steps.text: Spread 2 tbsp beaten egg over the dosa and cook until set.

steps.title: Crisp it up
steps.text: Drizzle ½ tsp oil or ghee over the dosa and cook on medium flame for 1–2 minutes until the base turns golden and crisp.

steps.title: Fill & fold
steps.text: Place 2–3 tbsp of filling in the centre, fold the dosa over and lift onto a plate.

steps.title: Repeat
steps.text: Wipe the tawa with a damp cloth between dosas to cool it slightly so the batter spreads evenly.

tips: In cold weather, ferment the batter in a switched-off oven with the light on.
Use non-iodised salt for better fermentation.
serving_ideas: coconut chutney and sambar.
Best time: breakfast or dinner.
recipes.storage: fermented batter keeps in the fridge for 3–4 days. Cooked dosas are best eaten fresh.

recipes.description: Whole green moong chila with spinach, rich in fibre and iron.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Wash the whole green moong and spinach 2–3 times and soak in plenty of water for 6–8 hours. Drain well.

steps.title: Grind the batter
steps.text: Grind the soaked dal with ginger, green chillies and cumin, adding water little by little, to a smooth, thick batter. It should coat the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Add hing and salt and mix in the onion and coriander leaves. The batter does not need fermentation and can be used right away.

steps.title: Heat the pan
steps.text: Heat a non-stick or iron tawa on medium flame and grease it lightly with oil.

steps.title: Spread the chila
steps.text: Pour a ladle of batter and spread it quickly into a thin round. Drizzle a few drops of oil around the edges.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Cook on medium flame for 2–3 minutes until the base is golden and crisp, then flip and cook the other side for 1 minute.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with green chutney or tomato chutney. Repeat with the remaining batter.

tips: Do not add too much water while grinding; a thick batter gives crisp chilas.
Soaking can be done overnight for a quicker morning.
serving_ideas: mint-coriander chutney, plain curd or raita, and a cucumber-tomato salad.
Best time: breakfast, or an early evening meal.
recipes.storage: Batter keeps in the fridge for up to 24 hours; stir and adjust with a little water before use.

recipes.description: Pesarattu with spinach blended in.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Wash the whole green moong, rice and spinach well and soak together for 6–8 hours.

steps.title: Grind
steps.text: Drain and grind with the ginger and green chilli and spices to a slightly coarse, thick batter, adding water as needed.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Add salt and mix well. This batter needs no fermentation.

steps.title: Heat the tawa
steps.text: Heat a cast-iron or non-stick tawa on medium flame and grease it lightly.

steps.title: Spread
steps.text: Pour a ladle of batter and spread into a medium-thick round. Sprinkle the topping over it and press lightly.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Drizzle oil around the edges and cook for 2–3 minutes until golden, then flip and cook for 1–2 minutes more.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot. Repeat with the remaining batter.

tips: Grind the batter slightly coarse for a crisp texture.
serving_ideas: coconut chutney, avial or a little jaggery and butter (traditional).

recipes.storage: batter keeps in the fridge for up to 2 days.

recipes.description: An instant dosa from four flours.

steps.title: Mix the flours
steps.text: In a large bowl, combine the jowar, bajra, ragi and rice flour and curd with salt.

steps.title: Make a thin batter
steps.text: Add water gradually, whisking constantly, to make a thin, flowing batter without lumps — much thinner than regular dosa batter.

steps.title: Add flavourings & rest
steps.text: Stir in the onion, green chilli, curry leaves and coriander leaves. Rest for 20 minutes; the flour absorbs water, so thin it again before cooking.

steps.title: Heat the tawa
steps.text: Heat a cast-iron or non-stick tawa on medium-high flame and grease it lightly.

steps.title: Pour the dosa
steps.text: Stir the batter from the bottom and pour it from a height, starting at the edges and filling the gaps. Do not spread it with the ladle.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Drizzle ½ tsp oil and cook on medium flame for 3–4 minutes until the dosa turns golden and crisp and leaves the pan easily.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Fold and serve immediately; instant dosas lose their crispness as they cool. Stir the batter before each dosa.

tips: These dosas are cooked on one side only; flipping is not needed.
If the dosa sticks, the pan is not hot enough or needs a little more oil.
serving_ideas: coconut chutney and sambar.
Best time: breakfast or dinner.
recipes.storage: best made fresh. Leftover batter keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

steps.text: Heat oil, crackle mustard seeds and urad dal, add curry leaves, ginger, green chillies and onion and sauté until soft. Add turmeric, the potatoes, salt and 3 tbsp water, mash lightly and mix in coriander.

steps.title: Heat the tawa
steps.text: Heat a cast-iron or non-stick tawa on medium-high flame. Sprinkle water; it should sizzle and evaporate. Wipe with an oiled cloth or half an onion.

steps.title: Spread the dosa
steps.text: Pour a ladle of batter in the centre and spread it in quick outward circles into a thin round.

steps.title: Crisp it up
steps.text: Drizzle ½ tsp oil or ghee over the dosa and cook on medium flame for 1–2 minutes until the base turns golden and crisp.

steps.title: Fill & fold
steps.text: Place 2–3 tbsp of filling in the centre, fold the dosa over and lift onto a plate.

steps.title: Repeat
steps.text: Wipe the tawa with a damp cloth between dosas to cool it slightly so the batter spreads evenly.

serving_ideas: coconut chutney and sambar.

recipes.description: Little millet uttapam with vegetables.

steps.title: Prepare the batter
steps.text: Soak the little millet for 5 hours and the urad dal with methi seeds for 4 hours. Grind separately, mix, add salt and ferment overnight.

steps.title: Thicken
steps.text: Uttapam batter should be thicker than dosa batter; do not thin it.

steps.title: Chop the topping
steps.text: Finely chop the onion, carrot and coriander leaves and mix them together.

steps.title: Heat the tawa
steps.text: Heat a tawa on medium flame and grease it lightly.

steps.title: Spread
steps.text: Pour a ladle of batter and spread it gently into a thick 5–6 inch round.

steps.title: Add the topping
steps.text: Sprinkle 2 tbsp of the topping evenly and press it in gently with the back of the ladle.

steps.title: Cook covered
steps.text: Drizzle oil around the edges, cover and cook on medium-low flame for 3 minutes until the base is golden.

steps.title: Flip
steps.text: Flip and cook the topping side for 1–2 minutes until lightly browned.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with chutney and sambar.

tips: Cooking covered on low heat makes the uttapam soft and fully cooked inside.
Press the topping into the batter so it does not fall off when flipped.
serving_ideas: coconut chutney, tomato chutney and sambar.
Best time: breakfast or a light dinner.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh.

recipes.description: A quick red lentil dosa, rich in protein.

steps.text: Wash the masoor dal and spinach 2–3 times and soak in plenty of water for 2 hours. Drain well.

steps.title: Grind the batter
steps.text: Grind the soaked dal with ginger, green chillies and cumin, adding water little by little, to a smooth, thick batter. It should coat the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Add hing and salt and mix in the onion and coriander leaves. The batter does not need fermentation and can be used right away.

steps.title: Heat the pan
steps.text: Heat a non-stick or iron tawa on medium flame and grease it lightly with oil.

steps.title: Spread the chila

steps.title: Cook

steps.title: Prepare the batter
steps.text: Take the besan, rava / suji and curd in a bowl; it should be thick, like idli batter.

steps.title: Add the flavourings
steps.text: Mix in the methi, onion, green chilli and fruit salt and salt.

steps.title: Heat the appe pan
steps.text: Heat a paniyaram (appe) pan on medium flame and add a few drops of oil to each cavity.

steps.title: Fill
steps.text: Pour batter into each cavity until three-quarters full.

steps.title: Cook covered
steps.text: Cover and cook on medium-low flame for 3–4 minutes until the base turns golden.

steps.title: Turn
steps.text: Turn each appe with a skewer or spoon handle, add a drop of oil and cook the other side for 2–3 minutes.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with coconut or tomato chutney.

tips: Keep the flame medium-low so the appe cooks through without burning.
Leftover idli or dosa batter is perfect for appe.
serving_ideas: coconut chutney or tomato chutney.
Great for tiffin boxes and evening snacks.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh; keeps in a tiffin for 4–5 hours.

recipes.description: Idlis with fresh methi leaves.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Wash and soak the idli for 5–6 hours. Separately soak the urad dal with methi seeds for 4 hours.

steps.title: Grind the dal
steps.text: Grind the urad dal with ice-cold water, a little at a time, to a light, fluffy, smooth batter.

steps.title: Grind the grain
steps.text: Grind the soaked grain to a slightly coarse, semolina-like batter. Mix both batters well with your hand.

steps.title: Ferment
steps.text: Add salt, cover and leave in a warm place for 8–12 hours until it doubles and smells pleasantly sour.

steps.title: Add flavour
steps.text: Fold the chopped methi into the batter.

steps.title: Prepare the steamer
steps.text: Boil 2 cups water in an idli steamer or pressure cooker (without the whistle). Grease the idli moulds lightly.

steps.title: Fill the moulds
steps.text: Gently stir the batter without knocking out the air and pour into the moulds until three-quarters full.

steps.title: Steam
steps.text: Steam on medium-high flame for 10–12 minutes. A toothpick inserted in the centre should come out clean.

steps.title: Rest & demould
steps.text: Rest for 2 minutes, then scoop out the idlis with a wet spoon and serve hot.

tips: Use a 4:1 ratio of idli rice to urad dal for soft idlis.
Do not over-stir fermented batter; it loses the air that makes idlis fluffy.
serving_ideas: sambar and coconut or tomato chutney.
Best time: breakfast; also great for tiffin boxes.
recipes.storage: batter keeps in the fridge for 3–4 days; steamed idlis keep for 1 day and can be re-steamed.

recipes.description: An oats and besan chila with fresh methi, high in fibre and gentle on blood sugar.

steps.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps.text: Finely chop the onion and green chilli and grate the ginger. Small, even pieces keep the chila thin and help it cook evenly.

steps.title: Make the batter
steps.text: In a mixing bowl, combine the rolled oats, besan and methi with turmeric, ajwain, chilli powder and salt. Add water a little at a time and whisk to a smooth, lump-free batter that flows like dosa batter.

steps.title: Add vegetables & rest
steps.text: Fold in the chopped vegetables, ginger and coriander. Rest the batter for 15 minutes so it thickens slightly and the chila turns soft.

steps.title: Heat the pan
steps.text: Heat a non-stick or well-seasoned iron tawa on medium flame and brush it with ¼ tsp oil. A few drops of water should sizzle when the pan is ready.

steps.title: Spread the chila
steps.text: Pour one ladle of batter in the centre and spread it gently in circles into a 6–7 inch round. Drizzle a few drops of oil around the edges.

steps.title: Cook the first side
steps.text: Cook on medium-low flame for 2–3 minutes, until the top looks set and the edges lift easily and turn golden.

steps.title: Flip & cook
steps.text: Flip with a flat spatula and cook the other side for 1–2 minutes, pressing lightly, until golden spots appear.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with mint-coriander chutney or curd. Make the remaining chilas the same way, adding only a few drops of oil each time.

tips: Rest the batter for 10 minutes; it makes the chila softer and easier to flip.
Keep the flame medium-low so the centre cooks before the outside browns.
serving_ideas: mint-coriander chutney, plain curd or raita, and a cucumber-tomato salad.
Best time: breakfast, or an early evening meal.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh. Plain batter (without vegetables) keeps in the fridge in an airtight box for up to 12 hours.

recipes.description: Instant rava idlis with fresh methi.

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Dry-roast the rava / suji on low flame for 3–4 minutes until aromatic. Cool.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat oil, crackle mustard seeds, add urad dal, chana dal, cashews, curry leaves, green chilli and ginger and fry until golden. Add this to the roasted base.

steps.title: Mix the batter
steps.text: Add curd, salt and enough water to make a thick, idli-like batter. Stir in the methi.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Cover and rest for 15–20 minutes so the grains soften and swell.

steps.title: Prepare the steamer
steps.text: Boil water in the steamer and grease the idli moulds.

steps.title: Add fruit salt
steps.text: Just before steaming, add the Eno with 1 tsp water and stir gently in one direction; the batter will turn frothy.

steps.title: Steam
steps.text: Fill the moulds immediately and steam for 10–12 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Rest 2 minutes, demould and serve hot.

tips: Steam immediately after adding Eno; the bubbles fade if the batter waits.
Use fresh, slightly sour curd for the best taste.
serving_ideas: sambar and coconut or tomato chutney.
Best time: breakfast; also great for tiffin boxes.
recipes.storage: best eaten the same day; re-steam leftovers for 3 minutes.

steps.text: In a large bowl, combine the little millet, rava / suji and rice flour and curd with salt.

steps.title: Make a thin batter
steps.text: Add water gradually, whisking constantly, to make a thin, flowing batter without lumps — much thinner than regular dosa batter.

steps.text: Stir in the onion, green chilli, curry leaves and coriander leaves. Rest for 20 minutes; the flour absorbs water, so thin it again before cooking.

steps.text: Heat a cast-iron or non-stick tawa on medium-high flame and grease it lightly.

steps.text: Fold and serve immediately; instant dosas lose their crispness as they cool. Stir the batter before each dosa.

serving_ideas: coconut chutney and sambar.

recipes.description: A protein-rich instant dosa from ground moong dal.

steps.title: Mix the flours
steps.text: In a large bowl, combine the moong dal with salt.

steps.title: Make a thin batter
steps.text: Add water gradually, whisking constantly, to make a thin, flowing batter without lumps.

steps.title: Add flavourings & rest
steps.text: Stir in the onion, green chilli, curry leaves and coriander leaves. Rest for 20 minutes; the flour absorbs water, so thin it again before cooking.

steps.title: Heat the tawa
steps.text: Heat a cast-iron or non-stick tawa on medium-high flame and grease it lightly.

steps.title: Spread the dosa
steps.text: Pour a ladle of batter and spread it gently into a round.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Drizzle ½ tsp oil and cook on medium flame for 3–4 minutes until the dosa turns golden and crisp and leaves the pan easily.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Fold and serve immediately; instant dosas lose their crispness as they cool. Stir the batter before each dosa.

tips: These dosas are cooked on one side only; flipping is not needed.

serving_ideas: coconut chutney and sambar.
Best time: breakfast or dinner.
recipes.storage: best made fresh. Leftover batter keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

recipes.description: A protein-packed dosa from moong and masoor dal.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Wash the moong dal, masoor dal and rice well and soak together for 3 hours.

steps.title: Grind
steps.text: Drain and grind with the ginger, green chilli and curry leaves and spices to a slightly coarse, thick batter, adding water as needed.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Add salt and mix well. This batter needs no fermentation.

steps.title: Heat the tawa
steps.text: Heat a cast-iron or non-stick tawa on medium flame and grease it lightly.

steps.title: Spread
steps.text: Pour a ladle of batter and spread into a medium-thick round.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Drizzle oil around the edges and cook for 2–3 minutes until golden, then flip and cook for 1–2 minutes more.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot. Repeat with the remaining batter.

tips: Grind the batter slightly coarse for a crisp texture.
serving_ideas: coconut chutney, avial or a little jaggery and butter (traditional).

recipes.storage: batter keeps in the fridge for up to 2 days.

recipes.description: Moong dal chila with fresh fenugreek leaves.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Wash the moong dal 2–3 times and soak in plenty of water for 4 hours. Drain well.

steps.title: Grind the batter
steps.text: Grind the soaked dal with ginger, green chillies and cumin, adding water little by little, to a smooth, thick batter. It should coat the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Add hing and salt and mix in the methi and onion. The batter does not need fermentation and can be used right away.

steps.title: Heat the pan

steps.title: Spread the chila

steps.title: Cook

tips: Do not add too much water while grinding; a thick batter gives crisp chilas.

recipes.description: A crunchy besan chila with chopped sprouts.

steps.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps.text: Finely chop the onion and green chilli and grate the ginger. Small, even pieces keep the chila thin and help it cook evenly.

steps.title: Make the batter
steps.text: In a mixing bowl, combine the besan and moong sprouts with turmeric, ajwain, chilli powder and salt. Add water a little at a time and whisk to a smooth, lump-free batter that flows like dosa batter.

steps.title: Add vegetables & rest
steps.text: Fold in the chopped vegetables, ginger and coriander. Rest the batter for 10 minutes so it thickens slightly and the chila turns soft.

steps.title: Heat the pan
steps.text: Heat a non-stick or well-seasoned iron tawa on medium flame and brush it with ¼ tsp oil. A few drops of water should sizzle when the pan is ready.

steps.title: Spread the chila
steps.text: Pour one ladle of batter in the centre and spread it gently in circles into a 6–7 inch round. Drizzle a few drops of oil around the edges.

steps.title: Cook the first side
steps.text: Cook on medium-low flame for 2–3 minutes, until the top looks set and the edges lift easily and turn golden.

steps.title: Flip & cook
steps.text: Flip with a flat spatula and cook the other side for 1–2 minutes, pressing lightly, until golden spots appear.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with mint-coriander chutney or curd. Make the remaining chilas the same way, adding only a few drops of oil each time.

tips: Rest the batter for 10 minutes; it makes the chila softer and easier to flip.
Keep the flame medium-low so the centre cooks before the outside browns.
serving_ideas: mint-coriander chutney, plain curd or raita, and a cucumber-tomato salad.
Best time: breakfast, or an early evening meal.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh. Plain batter (without vegetables) keeps in the fridge in an airtight box for up to 12 hours.

recipes.description: A nutrient-dense dosa with moringa leaves in the batter.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Wash the idli and soak for 5–6 hours. Separately wash and soak the urad dal with the methi seeds for 4–5 hours.

steps.title: Grind
steps.text: Grind the urad dal with ice-cold water until light, fluffy and doubled in volume. Grind the soaked grain to a smooth paste. Mix both with clean hands.

steps.title: Ferment
steps.text: Add salt, cover and keep in a warm place for 8–12 hours (overnight) until the batter rises and smells mildly sour.

steps.title: Flavour the batter
steps.text: Chop the moringa leaves finely and stir them into the batter.

steps.title: Heat the tawa
steps.text: Heat a cast-iron or non-stick tawa on medium-high flame. Sprinkle water; it should sizzle and evaporate. Wipe with an oiled cloth or half an onion.

steps.title: Spread the dosa
steps.text: Pour a ladle of batter in the centre and spread it in quick outward circles into a thin round.

steps.title: Crisp it up
steps.text: Drizzle ½ tsp oil or ghee over the dosa and cook on medium flame for 1–2 minutes until the base turns golden and crisp.

steps.title: Fold & serve
steps.text: Fold the dosa in half or roll it up and serve immediately.

steps.title: Repeat
steps.text: Wipe the tawa with a damp cloth between dosas to cool it slightly so the batter spreads evenly.

tips: In cold weather, ferment the batter in a switched-off oven with the light on.
Use non-iodised salt for better fermentation.
serving_ideas: coconut chutney and sambar.
Best time: breakfast or dinner.
recipes.storage: fermented batter keeps in the fridge for 3–4 days. Cooked dosas are best eaten fresh.

recipes.description: Soft idlis from rice and two millets.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Wash and soak the idli, foxtail millet and little millet for 5–6 hours. Separately soak the urad dal with methi seeds for 4 hours.

steps.title: Grind the dal
steps.text: Grind the urad dal with ice-cold water, a little at a time, to a light, fluffy, smooth batter.

steps.title: Grind the grain
steps.text: Grind the soaked grain to a slightly coarse, semolina-like batter. Mix both batters well with your hand.

steps.title: Ferment
steps.text: Add salt, cover and leave in a warm place for 8–12 hours until it doubles and smells pleasantly sour.

steps.title: Prepare the steamer
steps.text: Boil 2 cups water in an idli steamer or pressure cooker (without the whistle). Grease the idli moulds lightly.

steps.title: Fill the moulds
steps.text: Gently stir the batter without knocking out the air and pour into the moulds until three-quarters full.

steps.title: Steam
steps.text: Steam on medium-high flame for 10–12 minutes. A toothpick inserted in the centre should come out clean.

steps.title: Rest & demould
steps.text: Rest for 2 minutes, then scoop out the idlis with a wet spoon and serve hot.

tips: Use a 4:1 ratio of idli rice to urad dal for soft idlis.
Do not over-stir fermented batter; it loses the air that makes idlis fluffy.
serving_ideas: sambar and coconut or tomato chutney.
Best time: breakfast; also great for tiffin boxes.
recipes.storage: batter keeps in the fridge for 3–4 days; steamed idlis keep for 1 day and can be re-steamed.

recipes.description: Uttapam topped with mushrooms.

steps.title: Prepare the batter
steps.text: Soak the idli for 5 hours and the urad dal with methi seeds for 4 hours. Grind separately, mix, add salt and ferment overnight.

steps.title: Thicken
steps.text: Uttapam batter should be thicker than dosa batter; do not thin it.

steps.title: Chop the topping
steps.text: Finely chop the mushrooms, onion and capsicum and mix them together.

steps.title: Heat the tawa
steps.text: Heat a tawa on medium flame and grease it lightly.

steps.title: Spread
steps.text: Pour a ladle of batter and spread it gently into a thick 5–6 inch round.

steps.title: Add the topping
steps.text: Sprinkle 2 tbsp of the topping evenly and press it in gently with the back of the ladle.

steps.title: Cook covered
steps.text: Drizzle oil around the edges, cover and cook on medium-low flame for 3 minutes until the base is golden.

steps.title: Flip
steps.text: Flip and cook the topping side for 1–2 minutes until lightly browned.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with chutney and sambar.

tips: Cooking covered on low heat makes the uttapam soft and fully cooked inside.
Press the topping into the batter so it does not fall off when flipped.
serving_ideas: coconut chutney, tomato chutney and sambar.

steps.text: Take the rava / suji and curd in a bowl; it should be thick, like idli batter.

steps.text: Mix in the spinach, onion, green chilli and fruit salt and salt.

steps.text: Heat a paniyaram (appe) pan on medium flame and add a few drops of oil to each cavity.

steps.text: Heat oil, crackle mustard seeds, add urad dal, chana dal, cashews, curry leaves, green chilli and ginger and fry until golden. Add this to the roasted base.

steps.title: Mix the batter
steps.text: Add curd, salt and enough water to make a thick, idli-like batter. Stir in the spinach.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Cover and rest for 15–20 minutes so the grains soften and swell.

steps.text: Boil water in the steamer and grease the idli moulds.

recipes.description: Instant semolina chila filled with spiced paneer.

recipes.description: Instant rava idlis with green peas.

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Dry-roast the rava / suji on low flame for 3–4 minutes until aromatic. Cool.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat oil, crackle mustard seeds, add urad dal, chana dal, cashews, curry leaves, green chilli and ginger and fry until golden. Add this to the roasted base.

steps.title: Mix the batter
steps.text: Add curd, salt and enough water to make a thick, idli-like batter. Stir in the green peas.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Cover and rest for 15–20 minutes so the grains soften and swell.

steps.title: Prepare the steamer
steps.text: Boil water in the steamer and grease the idli moulds.

steps.title: Add fruit salt
steps.text: Just before steaming, add the Eno with 1 tsp water and stir gently in one direction; the batter will turn frothy.

steps.title: Steam
steps.text: Fill the moulds immediately and steam for 10–12 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Rest 2 minutes, demould and serve hot.

tips: Steam immediately after adding Eno; the bubbles fade if the batter waits.
Use fresh, slightly sour curd for the best taste.
serving_ideas: sambar and coconut or tomato chutney.
Best time: breakfast; also great for tiffin boxes.
recipes.storage: best eaten the same day; re-steam leftovers for 3 minutes.

recipes.description: Onion uttapam sprinkled with spicy podi.

steps.title: Prepare the batter
steps.text: Soak the idli for 5 hours and the urad dal with methi seeds for 4 hours. Grind separately, mix, add salt and ferment overnight.

steps.title: Thicken
steps.text: Uttapam batter should be thicker than dosa batter; do not thin it.

steps.title: Chop the topping
steps.text: Finely chop the onion and coriander leaves and mix them together.

steps.title: Heat the tawa
steps.text: Heat a tawa on medium flame and grease it lightly.

steps.title: Spread
steps.text: Pour a ladle of batter and spread it gently into a thick 5–6 inch round.

steps.title: Add the topping
steps.text: Sprinkle 2 tbsp of the topping evenly and press it in gently with the back of the ladle.

steps.title: Cook covered
steps.text: Drizzle oil around the edges, cover and cook on medium-low flame for 3 minutes until the base is golden.

steps.title: Flip
steps.text: Flip and cook the topping side for 1–2 minutes until lightly browned.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with chutney and sambar.

tips: Cooking covered on low heat makes the uttapam soft and fully cooked inside.
Press the topping into the batter so it does not fall off when flipped.
serving_ideas: coconut chutney, tomato chutney and sambar.
Best time: breakfast or a light dinner.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh.

recipes.description: A soft orange dosa with pumpkin purée.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Wash the idli and soak for 5–6 hours. Separately wash and soak the urad dal with the methi seeds for 4–5 hours.

steps.title: Grind
steps.text: Grind the urad dal with ice-cold water until light, fluffy and doubled in volume. Grind the soaked grain to a smooth paste. Mix both with clean hands.

steps.title: Ferment
steps.text: Add salt, cover and keep in a warm place for 8–12 hours (overnight) until the batter rises and smells mildly sour.

steps.title: Flavour the batter
steps.text: Blend the steamed pumpkin and mix into the batter.

steps.title: Heat the tawa
steps.text: Heat a cast-iron or non-stick tawa on medium-high flame. Sprinkle water; it should sizzle and evaporate. Wipe with an oiled cloth or half an onion.

steps.title: Spread the dosa
steps.text: Pour a ladle of batter in the centre and spread it in quick outward circles into a thin round.

steps.title: Crisp it up
steps.text: Drizzle ½ tsp oil or ghee over the dosa and cook on medium flame for 1–2 minutes until the base turns golden and crisp.

steps.title: Fold & serve
steps.text: Fold the dosa in half or roll it up and serve immediately.

steps.title: Repeat
steps.text: Wipe the tawa with a damp cloth between dosas to cool it slightly so the batter spreads evenly.

tips: In cold weather, ferment the batter in a switched-off oven with the light on.
Use non-iodised salt for better fermentation.
serving_ideas: coconut chutney and sambar.
Best time: breakfast or dinner.
recipes.storage: fermented batter keeps in the fridge for 3–4 days. Cooked dosas are best eaten fresh.

recipes.description: An adai made with quinoa and mixed dals.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Wash the quinoa, toor / arhar dal, chana dal and moong dal well and soak together for 4–6 hours.

steps.title: Grind
steps.text: Drain and grind with the ginger, green chilli and curry leaves and spices to a slightly coarse, thick batter, adding water as needed.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Add salt and mix well. This batter needs no fermentation.

steps.title: Heat the tawa
steps.text: Heat a cast-iron or non-stick tawa on medium flame and grease it lightly.

steps.title: Spread
steps.text: Pour a ladle of batter and spread into a medium-thick round. Sprinkle the topping over it and press lightly.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Drizzle oil around the edges and cook for 2–3 minutes until golden, then flip and cook for 1–2 minutes more.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot. Repeat with the remaining batter.

tips: Grind the batter slightly coarse for a crisp texture.
serving_ideas: coconut chutney, avial or a little jaggery and butter (traditional).
Best time: breakfast or dinner.
recipes.storage: batter keeps in the fridge for up to 2 days.

recipes.description: Protein-rich quinoa appe.

steps.title: Prepare the batter
steps.text: Take the quinoa and rava / suji in a bowl; it should be thick, like idli batter.

steps.title: Add the flavourings
steps.text: Mix in the onion, carrot, green chilli and fruit salt and salt.

steps.title: Heat the appe pan
steps.text: Heat a paniyaram (appe) pan on medium flame and add a few drops of oil to each cavity.

steps.title: Fill
steps.text: Pour batter into each cavity until three-quarters full.

steps.title: Cook covered
steps.text: Cover and cook on medium-low flame for 3–4 minutes until the base turns golden.

steps.title: Turn
steps.text: Turn each appe with a skewer or spoon handle, add a drop of oil and cook the other side for 2–3 minutes.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with coconut or tomato chutney.

tips: Keep the flame medium-low so the appe cooks through without burning.
Leftover idli or dosa batter is perfect for appe.
serving_ideas: coconut chutney or tomato chutney.
Great for tiffin boxes and evening snacks.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh; keeps in a tiffin for 4–5 hours.

recipes.description: Uttapam topped with moong sprouts.

steps.title: Prepare the batter
steps.text: Soak the idli for 5 hours and the urad dal with methi seeds for 4 hours. Grind separately, mix, add salt and ferment overnight.

steps.title: Thicken
steps.text: Uttapam batter should be thicker than dosa batter; do not thin it.

steps.title: Chop the topping
steps.text: Finely chop the moong sprouts, onion, coriander leaves and green chilli and mix them together.

steps.title: Heat the tawa
steps.text: Heat a tawa on medium flame and grease it lightly.

steps.title: Spread
steps.text: Pour a ladle of batter and spread it gently into a thick 5–6 inch round.

steps.title: Add the topping
steps.text: Sprinkle 2 tbsp of the topping evenly and press it in gently with the back of the ladle.

steps.title: Cook covered
steps.text: Drizzle oil around the edges, cover and cook on medium-low flame for 3 minutes until the base is golden.

steps.title: Flip
steps.text: Flip and cook the topping side for 1–2 minutes until lightly browned.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with chutney and sambar.

tips: Cooking covered on low heat makes the uttapam soft and fully cooked inside.
Press the topping into the batter so it does not fall off when flipped.
serving_ideas: coconut chutney, tomato chutney and sambar.
Best time: breakfast or a light dinner.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh.

recipes.description: Soft, sweet banana appe, a kids’ favourite.

steps.title: Prepare the batter
steps.text: Take the whole-wheat flour and rava / suji in a bowl; it should be thick, like idli batter.

steps.title: Add the flavourings
steps.text: Mix in the banana, jaggery and grated coconut and salt.

steps.title: Heat the appe pan
steps.text: Heat a paniyaram (appe) pan on medium flame and add a few drops of oil to each cavity.

steps.title: Fill
steps.text: Pour batter into each cavity until three-quarters full.

steps.title: Cook covered
steps.text: Cover and cook on medium-low flame for 3–4 minutes until the base turns golden.

steps.title: Turn
steps.text: Turn each appe with a skewer or spoon handle, add a drop of oil and cook the other side for 2–3 minutes.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve warm as a snack.

tips: Keep the flame medium-low so the appe cooks through without burning.
Leftover idli or dosa batter is perfect for appe.
serving_ideas: coconut chutney or tomato chutney.
Great for tiffin boxes and evening snacks.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh; keeps in a tiffin for 4–5 hours.

recipes.description: Besan chila with grated sweet potato, mildly sweet and rich in beta-carotene.

steps.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps.text: Finely chop the onion and green chilli and grate the ginger. Small, even pieces keep the chila thin and help it cook evenly.

steps.title: Make the batter
steps.text: In a mixing bowl, combine the besan and sweet potato with turmeric, ajwain, chilli powder and salt. Add water a little at a time and whisk to a smooth, lump-free batter that flows like dosa batter.

steps.title: Add vegetables & rest
steps.text: Fold in the chopped vegetables, ginger and coriander. Rest the batter for 10 minutes so it thickens slightly and the chila turns soft.

steps.title: Heat the pan
steps.text: Heat a non-stick or well-seasoned iron tawa on medium flame and brush it with ¼ tsp oil. A few drops of water should sizzle when the pan is ready.

steps.title: Spread the chila
steps.text: Pour one ladle of batter in the centre and spread it gently in circles into a 6–7 inch round. Drizzle a few drops of oil around the edges.

steps.title: Cook the first side
steps.text: Cook on medium-low flame for 2–3 minutes, until the top looks set and the edges lift easily and turn golden.

steps.title: Flip & cook
steps.text: Flip with a flat spatula and cook the other side for 1–2 minutes, pressing lightly, until golden spots appear.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with mint-coriander chutney or curd. Make the remaining chilas the same way, adding only a few drops of oil each time.

tips: Rest the batter for 10 minutes; it makes the chila softer and easier to flip.
Keep the flame medium-low so the centre cooks before the outside browns.
serving_ideas: mint-coriander chutney, plain curd or raita, and a cucumber-tomato salad.

recipes.storage: best eaten fresh. Plain batter (without vegetables) keeps in the fridge in an airtight box for up to 12 hours.

recipes.description: A tangy orange dosa with tomato purée in the batter.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Wash the idli and soak for 5–6 hours. Separately wash and soak the urad dal with the methi seeds for 4–5 hours.

steps.title: Grind
steps.text: Grind the urad dal with ice-cold water until light, fluffy and doubled in volume. Grind the soaked grain to a smooth paste. Mix both with clean hands.

steps.title: Ferment
steps.text: Add salt, cover and keep in a warm place for 8–12 hours (overnight) until the batter rises and smells mildly sour.

steps.title: Flavour the batter
steps.text: Blend tomatoes and red chillies to a smooth purée and stir into the fermented batter.

steps.title: Heat the tawa
steps.text: Heat a cast-iron or non-stick tawa on medium-high flame. Sprinkle water; it should sizzle and evaporate. Wipe with an oiled cloth or half an onion.

steps.title: Spread the dosa
steps.text: Pour a ladle of batter in the centre and spread it in quick outward circles into a thin round.

steps.title: Crisp it up
steps.text: Drizzle ½ tsp oil or ghee over the dosa and cook on medium flame for 1–2 minutes until the base turns golden and crisp.

steps.title: Fold & serve
steps.text: Fold the dosa in half or roll it up and serve immediately.

steps.title: Repeat
steps.text: Wipe the tawa with a damp cloth between dosas to cool it slightly so the batter spreads evenly.

tips: In cold weather, ferment the batter in a switched-off oven with the light on.
Use non-iodised salt for better fermentation.
serving_ideas: coconut chutney and sambar.
Best time: breakfast or dinner.
recipes.storage: fermented batter keeps in the fridge for 3–4 days. Cooked dosas are best eaten fresh.

recipes.description: A soft, slightly spongy chila from masoor and urad dal.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Wash the masoor dal and urad dal 2–3 times and soak in plenty of water for 4 hours. Drain well.

steps.title: Grind the batter
steps.text: Grind the soaked dal with ginger, green chillies and cumin, adding water little by little, to a smooth, thick batter. It should coat the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Add hing and salt and mix in the onion and coriander leaves. The batter does not need fermentation and can be used right away.

steps.title: Heat the pan
steps.text: Heat a non-stick or iron tawa on medium flame and grease it lightly with oil.

steps.title: Spread the chila
steps.text: Pour a ladle of batter and spread it quickly into a thin round. Drizzle a few drops of oil around the edges.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Cook on medium flame for 2–3 minutes until the base is golden and crisp, then flip and cook the other side for 1 minute.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with green chutney or tomato chutney. Repeat with the remaining batter.

tips: Do not add too much water while grinding; a thick batter gives crisp chilas.
Soaking can be done overnight for a quicker morning.
serving_ideas: mint-coriander chutney, plain curd or raita, and a cucumber-tomato salad.
Best time: breakfast, or an early evening meal.
recipes.storage: Batter keeps in the fridge for up to 24 hours; stir and adjust with a little water before use.

recipes.description: Idlis studded with carrot, peas and beans.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Wash and soak the idli for 5–6 hours. Separately soak the urad dal with methi seeds for 4 hours.

steps.title: Grind the dal
steps.text: Grind the urad dal with ice-cold water, a little at a time, to a light, fluffy, smooth batter.

steps.title: Grind the grain
steps.text: Grind the soaked grain to a slightly coarse, semolina-like batter. Mix both batters well with your hand.

steps.title: Ferment
steps.text: Add salt, cover and leave in a warm place for 8–12 hours until it doubles and smells pleasantly sour.

steps.title: Add flavour
steps.text: Fold the vegetables and coriander into the batter.

steps.title: Prepare the steamer
steps.text: Boil 2 cups water in an idli steamer or pressure cooker (without the whistle). Grease the idli moulds lightly.

steps.title: Fill the moulds
steps.text: Gently stir the batter without knocking out the air and pour into the moulds until three-quarters full.

steps.title: Steam
steps.text: Steam on medium-high flame for 10–12 minutes. A toothpick inserted in the centre should come out clean.

steps.title: Rest & demould
steps.text: Rest for 2 minutes, then scoop out the idlis with a wet spoon and serve hot.

tips: Use a 4:1 ratio of idli rice to urad dal for soft idlis.
Do not over-stir fermented batter; it loses the air that makes idlis fluffy.
serving_ideas: sambar and coconut or tomato chutney.
Best time: breakfast; also great for tiffin boxes.
recipes.storage: batter keeps in the fridge for 3–4 days; steamed idlis keep for 1 day and can be re-steamed.

recipes.description: Rice flour rotti with fresh methi.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Take the rice flour with the methi, onion and green chilli and salt in a wide plate.

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: Add hot water little by little and mix with a spoon, then knead with the heel of your palm for 3–4 minutes into a smooth, crack-free dough. Millet dough has no gluten, so knead only one portion at a time.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Take a lemon-sized ball and pat it between your palms, or roll it between two sheets of butter paper, into a 6-inch round.

steps.title: Cook the first side
steps.text: Place on a hot tawa on medium flame. Spread a little water over the top with your fingers to prevent cracks.

steps.title: Flip
steps.text: When the bottom has light spots (about 1 minute), flip and cook the other side for 1 minute.

steps.title: Puff
steps.text: Roast directly on the flame with tongs, or press with a cloth on the tawa, until it puffs and both sides are cooked.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Apply a little ghee and serve hot.

tips: Knead each portion just before rolling; millet dough dries out quickly.
Patting with wet hands is easier than rolling for beginners.
serving_ideas: dal, sabzi, pithla or a garlic chutney, plus a little white butter or jaggery (traditional).
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: best eaten hot; it hardens as it cools.

recipes.description: A paratha stuffed with spiced potato and cauliflower.

steps.title: Knead the dough
steps.text: Mix the whole-wheat flour with salt and oil. Add water little by little and knead into a soft, smooth dough. Cover and rest for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare the stuffing
steps.text: Mix the mashed potato with the squeezed cauliflower and spices.

steps.title: Divide
steps.text: Divide the dough and the stuffing into 4 equal portions each. The stuffing should be dry; moisture makes parathas tear.

steps.title: Stuff
steps.text: Roll a dough ball into a 4-inch disc, place a portion of stuffing in the centre, gather the edges, pinch to seal and flatten gently.

steps.title: Roll
steps.text: Dust with flour and roll gently into a 6–7 inch paratha, applying even pressure so the stuffing does not break through.

steps.title: Cook the first side
steps.text: Place on a hot tawa over medium flame. Cook for 1 minute until small bubbles appear, then flip.

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Brush the cooked side with ½ tsp ghee or oil, flip again and press the edges with a spatula. Cook both sides until golden-brown spots appear.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with curd. Make the remaining parathas the same way.

tips: Seal the stuffing well and roll with light pressure to avoid tearing.
Use only ½ tsp ghee per side; dry-roasting first keeps the paratha light.
serving_ideas: plain curd or raita, a little white butter (optional) and pickle or green chutney.
Best time: breakfast or lunch.
recipes.storage: best eaten hot. Cooked parathas keep in a tiffin for 5–6 hours; the stuffing keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

steps.title: Roll

recipes.description: Soft rotis with bajra added to atta.

steps.text: Mix the whole-wheat flour and bajra with a pinch of salt. Add water little by little and knead into a soft, smooth dough.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Cover and rest for 20–30 minutes; rested dough makes softer rotis.

steps.title: Divide & roll
steps.text: Divide into 6 balls. Dust with flour and roll each into a thin, even 6-inch circle.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Place on a hot tawa. Flip when small bubbles appear (about 20 seconds).

steps.title: Cook the other side
steps.text: Cook until light brown spots form (about 40 seconds).

steps.title: Puff
steps.text: Place the roti directly on a medium flame with tongs; it will puff up fully. Flip once.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Apply a little ghee if you like, and keep in a cloth-lined box.

tips: Roll evenly; thick and thin patches stop the roti from puffing.

serving_ideas: any dal, sabzi or curry.

recipes.description: A light barnyard millet roti.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Take the barnyard millet and salt in a wide plate.

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: Add hot water little by little and mix with a spoon, then knead with the heel of your palm for 3–4 minutes into a smooth, crack-free dough. Millet dough has no gluten, so knead only one portion at a time.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Take a lemon-sized ball and pat it between your palms, or roll it between two sheets of butter paper, into a 6-inch round.

steps.title: Cook the first side
steps.text: Place on a hot tawa on medium flame. Spread a little water over the top with your fingers to prevent cracks.

steps.title: Flip
steps.text: When the bottom has light spots (about 1 minute), flip and cook the other side for 1 minute.

steps.title: Puff
steps.text: Roast directly on the flame with tongs, or press with a cloth on the tawa, until it puffs and both sides are cooked.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Apply a little ghee and serve hot.

tips: Knead each portion just before rolling; millet dough dries out quickly.
Patting with wet hands is easier than rolling for beginners.
serving_ideas: dal, sabzi, pithla or a garlic chutney, plus a little white butter or jaggery (traditional).
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: best eaten hot; it hardens as it cools.

recipes.description: Soft paratha with bathua greens kneaded into the dough.

steps.title: Prepare the add-ins
steps.text: Chop the bathua finely.

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: In a bowl, combine the whole-wheat flour with the bathua leaves, spices and salt. Add water gradually and knead into a soft dough. Rest for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Divide
steps.text: Divide the dough into 6 equal balls.

steps.title: Roll
steps.text: Dust a ball with flour and roll it into a thin 6-inch round.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Place on a hot tawa on medium flame. Flip when small bubbles appear and cook the other side for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Apply a few drops of oil, flip and press gently with a spatula. Cook until both sides have golden-brown spots.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Keep warm in a cloth-lined box and serve with curd, chutney or a sabzi.

tips: Rest the dough so it rolls thin without shrinking back.
serving_ideas: plain curd or raita, a little white butter (optional) and pickle or green chutney.
Best time: breakfast or lunch.
recipes.storage: keeps in an airtight box for 1 day at room temperature (theplas up to 3 days) and is ideal for travel.

recipes.description: Paratha stuffed with spiced mashed chickpeas.

steps.title: Knead the dough
steps.text: Mix the whole-wheat flour with salt and oil. Add water little by little and knead into a soft, smooth dough. Cover and rest for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare the stuffing
steps.text: Mash the drained chickpeas and mix with onion and spices.

steps.title: Divide
steps.text: Divide the dough and the stuffing into 4 equal portions each. The stuffing should be dry; moisture makes parathas tear.

steps.title: Stuff
steps.text: Roll a dough ball into a 4-inch disc, place a portion of stuffing in the centre, gather the edges, pinch to seal and flatten gently.

steps.title: Roll
steps.text: Dust with flour and roll gently into a 6–7 inch paratha, applying even pressure so the stuffing does not break through.

steps.title: Cook the first side
steps.text: Place on a hot tawa over medium flame. Cook for 1 minute until small bubbles appear, then flip.

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Brush the cooked side with ½ tsp ghee or oil, flip again and press the edges with a spatula. Cook both sides until golden-brown spots appear.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with curd. Make the remaining parathas the same way.

tips: Seal the stuffing well and roll with light pressure to avoid tearing.
Use only ½ tsp ghee per side; dry-roasting first keeps the paratha light.
serving_ideas: plain curd or raita, a little white butter (optional) and pickle or green chutney.
Best time: breakfast or lunch.
recipes.storage: best eaten hot. Cooked parathas keep in a tiffin for 5–6 hours; the stuffing keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

steps.text: Mix the whole-wheat flour and jowar with a pinch of salt. Add water little by little and knead into a soft, smooth dough.

steps.text: Cover and rest for 20–30 minutes; rested dough makes softer rotis.

steps.text: Divide into 6 balls. Dust with flour and roll each into a thin, even 6-inch circle.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Place on a hot tawa. Flip when small bubbles appear (about 20 seconds).

steps.title: Cook the other side
steps.text: Cook until light brown spots form (about 40 seconds).

steps.title: Puff
steps.text: Place the roti directly on a medium flame with tongs; it will puff up fully. Flip once.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Apply a little ghee if you like, and keep in a cloth-lined box.

tips: Roll evenly; thick and thin patches stop the roti from puffing.

recipes.storage: keeps soft in a cloth-lined box for 6–8 hours.

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: Add hot water little by little and mix with a spoon, then knead with the heel of your palm for 3–4 minutes into a smooth, crack-free dough. Millet dough has no gluten, so knead only one portion at a time.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Take a lemon-sized ball and pat it between your palms, or roll it between two sheets of butter paper, into a 6-inch round.

steps.title: Cook the first side
steps.text: Place on a hot tawa on medium flame. Spread a little water over the top with your fingers to prevent cracks.

steps.title: Flip
steps.text: When the bottom has light spots (about 1 minute), flip and cook the other side for 1 minute.

steps.title: Puff
steps.text: Roast directly on the flame with tongs, or press with a cloth on the tawa, until it puffs and both sides are cooked.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Apply a little ghee and serve hot.

tips: Knead each portion just before rolling; millet dough dries out quickly.
Patting with wet hands is easier than rolling for beginners.
serving_ideas: dal, sabzi, pithla or a garlic chutney, plus a little white butter or jaggery (traditional).
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: best eaten hot; it hardens as it cools.

recipes.description: Paratha stuffed with spiced cooked masoor dal.

steps.title: Knead the dough
steps.text: Mix the whole-wheat flour with salt and oil. Add water little by little and knead into a soft, smooth dough. Cover and rest for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare the stuffing
steps.text: Cook masoor dal with little water until thick and dry; mash and mix with spices.

steps.title: Divide
steps.text: Divide the dough and the stuffing into 4 equal portions each. The stuffing should be dry; moisture makes parathas tear.

steps.title: Stuff
steps.text: Roll a dough ball into a 4-inch disc, place a portion of stuffing in the centre, gather the edges, pinch to seal and flatten gently.

steps.title: Roll
steps.text: Dust with flour and roll gently into a 6–7 inch paratha, applying even pressure so the stuffing does not break through.

steps.title: Cook the first side
steps.text: Place on a hot tawa over medium flame. Cook for 1 minute until small bubbles appear, then flip.

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Brush the cooked side with ½ tsp ghee or oil, flip again and press the edges with a spatula. Cook both sides until golden-brown spots appear.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with curd. Make the remaining parathas the same way.

tips: Seal the stuffing well and roll with light pressure to avoid tearing.
Use only ½ tsp ghee per side; dry-roasting first keeps the paratha light.
serving_ideas: plain curd or raita, a little white butter (optional) and pickle or green chutney.
Best time: breakfast or lunch.
recipes.storage: best eaten hot. Cooked parathas keep in a tiffin for 5–6 hours; the stuffing keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

recipes.description: Fresh herby theplas.

steps.title: Prepare the add-ins
steps.text: Chop the herbs.

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: In a bowl, combine the whole-wheat flour and besan with the mint leaves, coriander leaves and curd, spices and salt. Add water gradually and knead into a soft dough. Rest for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Divide
steps.text: Divide the dough into 6 equal balls.

steps.title: Roll
steps.text: Dust a ball with flour and roll it into a thin 6-inch round.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Place on a hot tawa on medium flame. Flip when small bubbles appear and cook the other side for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Apply a few drops of oil, flip and press gently with a spatula. Cook until both sides have golden-brown spots.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Keep warm in a cloth-lined box and serve with curd, chutney or a sabzi.

tips: Rest the dough so it rolls thin without shrinking back.
serving_ideas: plain curd or raita, a little white butter (optional) and pickle or green chutney.
Best time: breakfast or lunch.
recipes.storage: keeps in an airtight box for 1 day at room temperature (theplas up to 3 days) and is ideal for travel.

recipes.description: Roti with quinoa flour for extra protein.

steps.title: Knead
steps.text: Mix the whole-wheat flour and quinoa with a pinch of salt. Add water little by little and knead into a soft, smooth dough.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Cover and rest for 20–30 minutes; rested dough makes softer rotis.

steps.title: Divide & roll
steps.text: Divide into 6 balls. Dust with flour and roll each into a thin, even 6-inch circle.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Place on a hot tawa. Flip when small bubbles appear (about 20 seconds).

steps.title: Cook the other side
steps.text: Cook until light brown spots form (about 40 seconds).

steps.title: Puff
steps.text: Place the roti directly on a medium flame with tongs; it will puff up fully. Flip once.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Apply a little ghee if you like, and keep in a cloth-lined box.

tips: Roll evenly; thick and thin patches stop the roti from puffing.
Knead the dough 10 minutes for the softest rotis.
serving_ideas: any dal, sabzi or curry.
Best time: lunch and dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps soft in a cloth-lined box for 6–8 hours.

steps.text: Place on a hot tawa on medium flame. Flip when small bubbles appear and cook the other side for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Apply a few drops of oil, flip and press gently with a spatula. Cook until both sides have golden-brown spots.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Keep warm in a cloth-lined box and serve with curd, chutney or a sabzi.

recipes.description: A protein-rich paratha stuffed with spiced moong sprouts.

steps.title: Knead the dough
steps.text: Mix the whole-wheat flour with salt and oil. Add water little by little and knead into a soft, smooth dough. Cover and rest for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare the stuffing
steps.text: Steam the sprouts for 5 minutes, mash coarsely and mix with onion and spices.

steps.title: Divide
steps.text: Divide the dough and the stuffing into 4 equal portions each. The stuffing should be dry; moisture makes parathas tear.

steps.title: Stuff
steps.text: Roll a dough ball into a 4-inch disc, place a portion of stuffing in the centre, gather the edges, pinch to seal and flatten gently.

steps.title: Roll
steps.text: Dust with flour and roll gently into a 6–7 inch paratha, applying even pressure so the stuffing does not break through.

steps.title: Cook the first side
steps.text: Place on a hot tawa over medium flame. Cook for 1 minute until small bubbles appear, then flip.

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Brush the cooked side with ½ tsp ghee or oil, flip again and press the edges with a spatula. Cook both sides until golden-brown spots appear.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with curd. Make the remaining parathas the same way.

tips: Seal the stuffing well and roll with light pressure to avoid tearing.
Use only ½ tsp ghee per side; dry-roasting first keeps the paratha light.
serving_ideas: plain curd or raita, a little white butter (optional) and pickle or green chutney.
Best time: breakfast or lunch.
recipes.storage: best eaten hot. Cooked parathas keep in a tiffin for 5–6 hours; the stuffing keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

recipes.description: Chia pudding topped with cinnamon apple.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: In a jar or bowl, stir the chia seeds into the toned milk with the honey until well combined.

steps.title: Rest briefly
steps.text: Leave for 10 minutes and stir again so the seeds or oats do not clump.

steps.title: Refrigerate
steps.text: Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight until thick and creamy.

steps.title: Loosen
steps.text: In the morning, stir well and add a splash of milk if it is too thick.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve chilled, topped with the apple and walnuts.

tips: Stir often and keep the flame low so the porridge does not catch at the bottom.
Porridge thickens as it cools; loosen it with a little warm milk or water.

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Dry-roast the bajra on low flame for 3–4 minutes, stirring, until aromatic.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Add the remaining water and bring to a gentle boil, stirring continuously so it does not stick.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Lower the flame and cook for 8 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy. Add the ajwain and dry ginger powder in the last 2 minutes.

steps.title: Sweeten
steps.text: Switch off the flame and stir in the jaggery. Adding jaggery off the heat stops milk from curdling.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Pour into bowls.

tips: Stir often and keep the flame low so the porridge does not catch at the bottom.

recipes.description: Poha with shredded cabbage.

steps.title: Rinse the poha
steps.text: Put the poha in a sieve and rinse under running water for 15–20 seconds, tossing gently. Drain and rest for 5 minutes to soften. Do not soak.

steps.title: Season the poha
steps.text: Sprinkle the turmeric, salt and sugar over the poha and fluff gently with a fork so they coat evenly.

steps.title: Roast the crunch
steps.text: Heat the oil in a kadhai and roast the peanuts on low flame until crunchy. Remove and keep aside.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: In the same oil, crackle the mustard seeds and cumin, then add curry leaves, green chilli and hing.

steps.title: Cook the vegetables
steps.text: Add the onion and cabbage and sauté on medium flame until the onion is soft and translucent and the vegetables are just tender (3–5 minutes).

steps.title: Add the poha
steps.text: Add the seasoned poha and mix gently. Cover and cook on low flame for 2–3 minutes so it steams through.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Switch off the flame and add the lemon juice and coriander leaves and the roasted crunch. Toss gently and serve hot.

tips: Use thick poha; thin poha turns mushy.
Add lemon juice only after switching off the flame, or it turns bitter.
serving_ideas: a cup of masala tea or buttermilk, and a fruit.
Best time: breakfast or evening snack.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh; it dries out when reheated.

recipes.description: Rava upma with sweet corn.

steps.title: Roast the grain
steps.text: Dry-roast the rava / suji on low flame for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until aromatic and lightly golden. Transfer to a plate.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat oil in a kadhai. Crackle the mustard seeds, then add the dals and cashews and fry until golden. Add curry leaves, green chilli, ginger and hing.

steps.title: Cook the vegetables
steps.text: Add the onion, sweet corn kernels and capsicum and sauté for 3–4 minutes until slightly soft.

steps.title: Boil the water
steps.text: Add 420 ml water and salt and bring to a rolling boil.

steps.title: Add the grain
steps.text: Lower the flame and add the rava / suji in a thin stream with one hand while stirring continuously with the other, so no lumps form.

steps.title: Cook covered
steps.text: Cover and cook on the lowest flame for 3–4 minutes until the water is absorbed and the grain is soft.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Add the ghee, lemon juice and coriander, fluff gently and serve hot.

tips: Roasting the grain well keeps the upma fluffy and non-sticky.
For a softer upma, add ¼ cup more water.
serving_ideas: coconut chutney, a cup of filter coffee or buttermilk.
Best time: breakfast or a light dinner.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh. Sprinkle a little water and reheat leftovers covered.

steps.text: Whisk the curd with the besan, turmeric, chilli powder and salt until completely smooth. Add the water and whisk again.

steps.text: Pour into a heavy pot and bring to a boil on medium flame, stirring continuously so the curd does not split.

steps.text: Once it boils, lower the flame and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it thickens slightly and the raw besan smell goes.

steps.text: Heat oil or ghee, crackle cumin, methi and mustard seeds, add dry red chillies, curry leaves and hing and pour over the kadhi.

tips: Use slightly sour curd for the best flavour.

steps.title: Prepare the tadka
steps.text: Heat ghee in a small pan, crackle the cumin, add garlic and fry until light golden, then add the dry red chilli and hing.

steps.title: Temper the dal
steps.text: Pour the sizzling tadka over the dal and cover immediately for 1 minute to trap the aroma.

steps.title: Serve
