recipes.description: Kadhi with carrot, beans and potato.

steps.title: Whisk
steps.text: Whisk the curd with the besan, turmeric, chilli powder and salt until completely smooth. Add the water and whisk again.

steps.title: Start cooking
steps.text: Pour into a heavy pot and bring to a boil on medium flame, stirring continuously so the curd does not split.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Once it boils, lower the flame and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it thickens slightly and the raw besan smell goes.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the carrot, french beans and potato and simmer until tender.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat oil or ghee, crackle cumin, methi and mustard seeds, add dry red chillies, curry leaves and hing and pour over the kadhi.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with coriander and serve hot.

tips: Use slightly sour curd for the best flavour.
Keep stirring until the kadhi comes to a boil to stop it from curdling.
serving_ideas: steamed rice, jeera rice or khichdi.
Best time: lunch.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

recipes.description: A light moong dal rasam.

steps.title: Cook the dal
steps.text: Pressure-cook the moong dal with 2 cups water for 3 whistles and mash; keep the dal water.

steps.title: Crush the spices
steps.text: Coarsely crush the pepper, cumin and garlic in a mortar.

steps.title: Boil the base
steps.text: In a pot, add the tamarind water, crushed tomatoes, turmeric, salt, jaggery, curry leaves, the crushed spices and rasam powder. Boil for 7–8 minutes until the raw smell goes.

steps.title: Add water & dal
steps.text: Add the remaining water and the dal. Heat until it turns frothy on top, then switch off. Do not boil it hard after this.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee, crackle mustard seeds, add dry red chillies, curry leaves and hing and pour over the rasam.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Add coriander, cover for 5 minutes, and serve hot with rice or as a soup.

tips: Switch off rasam as soon as it froths up; over-boiling makes it bitter.
Rasam tastes better after resting covered for 10 minutes.
serving_ideas: steamed rice with a little ghee, or sip it hot like a soup.
Best time: lunch or dinner; very soothing during colds.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

recipes.description: A hearty tomato rasam with dal and garlic.

steps.title: Cook the dal
steps.text: Pressure-cook the toor / arhar dal with 2 cups water for 3 whistles and mash; keep the dal water.

steps.title: Crush the spices
steps.text: Coarsely crush the pepper, cumin and garlic in a mortar.

steps.title: Boil the base
steps.text: In a pot, add the tamarind water, crushed tomatoes, turmeric, salt, jaggery, curry leaves, the crushed spices and rasam powder along with the garlic. Boil for 7–8 minutes until the raw smell goes.

steps.title: Add water & dal
steps.text: Add the remaining water and the dal. Heat until it turns frothy on top, then switch off. Do not boil it hard after this.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee, crackle mustard seeds, add dry red chillies, curry leaves and hing and pour over the rasam.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Add coriander, cover for 5 minutes, and serve hot with rice or as a soup.

tips: Switch off rasam as soon as it froths up; over-boiling makes it bitter.
Rasam tastes better after resting covered for 10 minutes.
serving_ideas: steamed rice with a little ghee, or sip it hot like a soup.
Best time: lunch or dinner; very soothing during colds.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

recipes.description: A tangy kadhi with tomato.

steps.title: Whisk
steps.text: Whisk the curd with the besan, turmeric, chilli powder and salt until completely smooth. Add the water and whisk again.

steps.title: Start cooking
steps.text: Pour into a heavy pot and bring to a boil on medium flame, stirring continuously so the curd does not split.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Once it boils, lower the flame and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it thickens slightly and the raw besan smell goes.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the tomato and simmer until tender.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat oil or ghee, crackle cumin, methi and mustard seeds, add dry red chillies, curry leaves and hing and pour over the kadhi.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with coriander and serve hot.

tips: Use slightly sour curd for the best flavour.
Keep stirring until the kadhi comes to a boil to stop it from curdling.
serving_ideas: steamed rice, jeera rice or khichdi.
Best time: lunch.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

recipes.description: Bengali-style chickpeas with coconut bits.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Wash the kabuli chana well and soak in plenty of water for 8 hours or overnight.

steps.title: Pressure-cook
steps.text: Drain, add fresh water and salt and pressure-cook for 5–6 whistles until soft enough to mash between your fingers. Keep the cooking water.

steps.title: Make the masala
steps.text: Heat mustard oil until it smokes lightly, then lower the flame. Add cumin, bay leaf and dry red chilli, then onion, and sauté until golden. Add ginger, tomato and the powdered spices and cook until the oil separates.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Add the cooked kabuli chana with enough cooking water to make a gravy. Mash a few pieces against the side of the pan to thicken it.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Cover and simmer on low flame for 15 minutes so the kabuli chana absorb the masala.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Add the grated coconut and coriander leaves, check the salt and serve hot.

tips: Brown the onions slowly; this gives the gravy its depth without cream.
Use the legume cooking water in the gravy; it holds flavour and nutrients.
serving_ideas: steamed rice, jeera rice, phulka or bhakri, with onion-cucumber salad.
Best time: lunch.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2–3 days and tastes even better the next day. Freezes well for a month.

recipes.description: Potatoes with tangy pickle spices.

steps.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps.text: Wash, peel if needed and cut the potato into even, bite-sized pieces so they cook evenly.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat mustard oil until it smokes lightly, lower the flame and add fennel, kalonji, methi and mustard seeds (the pickle spices), then hing and green chilli.

steps.title: Add the spices
steps.text: Lower the flame and add the turmeric and powdered spices with 1 tbsp water so they do not burn. Stir for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the potato and salt and toss well to coat with the masala.

steps.title: Cook uncovered
steps.text: Cook on medium flame for 6 minutes, stirring gently now and then, until tender and lightly browned. Do not cover.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Uncover, raise the flame for 1 minute to dry any moisture, then add the coriander leaves and mix gently.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with phulka, paratha or dal-rice.

tips: Cut vegetables to the same size so they cook evenly.
Cook on low heat with the lid on; the vegetables steam in their own moisture and need very little oil.
serving_ideas: phulka, paratha or bhakri, with dal and curd.
Best time: lunch or dinner; also great in tiffin boxes.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1–2 days.

steps.text: Heat mustard oil until it smokes lightly, lower the flame and add fennel, kalonji, methi and mustard seeds (the pickle spices), then hing and green chilli.

steps.title: Add the spices
steps.text: Lower the flame and add the turmeric and powdered spices with 1 tbsp water so they do not burn. Stir for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the mushrooms and salt and toss well to coat with the masala.

steps.title: Cook uncovered
steps.text: Cook on medium flame for 8 minutes, stirring gently now and then, until tender and lightly browned. Do not cover.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Uncover, raise the flame for 1 minute to dry any moisture, then add the coriander leaves and mix gently.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with phulka, paratha or dal-rice.

tips: Cut vegetables to the same size so they cook evenly.
Cook on low heat with the lid on; the vegetables steam in their own moisture and need very little oil.
serving_ideas: phulka, paratha or bhakri, with dal and curd.
Best time: lunch or dinner; also great in tiffin boxes.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1–2 days.

steps.text: Heat coconut oil, crackle the mustard seeds, then add dry red chillies, curry leaves and crushed shallots and sauté for 1 minute. Coarsely crush the coconut with cumin, garlic, green chilli and turmeric (do not make a paste).

steps.title: Add the spices
steps.text: Lower the flame and add the crushed coconut mixture with 1 tbsp water so they do not burn. Stir for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the moringa and eggs and salt and toss well to coat with the masala.

steps.title: Cook covered
steps.text: Cover and cook on low flame for 5 minutes, stirring every few minutes. Sprinkle a little water only if it starts to stick.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Uncover, raise the flame for 1 minute to dry any moisture and mix gently.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with phulka, paratha or dal-rice.

tips: Cut vegetables to the same size so they cook evenly.
Cook on low heat with the lid on; the vegetables steam in their own moisture and need very little oil.
serving_ideas: phulka, paratha or bhakri, with dal and curd.
Best time: lunch or dinner; also great in tiffin boxes.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1–2 days.

recipes.description: Capsicums stuffed with spicy soya keema.

steps.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps.text: Cut the tops off and deseed.

steps.title: Make the stuffing
steps.text: Mix the soya granules, onion and tomato with all the powdered spices and salt. Sprinkle a few drops of water if needed so it just holds together.

steps.title: Stuff
steps.text: Fill each slit vegetable with the masala, pressing it in firmly. Keep any leftover masala.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat oil in a wide pan, crackle the cumin and add hing.

steps.title: Arrange
steps.text: Place the stuffed vegetables in a single layer and sprinkle over the leftover masala.

steps.title: Cook covered
steps.text: Cover and cook on low flame for 15 minutes, turning gently every 4–5 minutes, until tender and evenly browned.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with phulka or as a side with dal-rice.

tips: Cook on low heat so the vegetable cooks through before the masala burns.
Turn gently with tongs so the stuffing stays in.
serving_ideas: phulka, paratha or dal-rice.
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

recipes.description: Spring onion greens with roasted besan, Maharashtrian style.

steps.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps.text: Wash, peel if needed and cut the spring onion and besan into even, bite-sized pieces so they cook evenly.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat oil in a kadhai, crackle the cumin, then add hing, green chilli and ginger and sauté for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Add the spices
steps.text: Lower the flame and add the turmeric and powdered spices with 1 tbsp water so they do not burn. Stir for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the spring onion and besan and salt and toss well to coat with the masala.

steps.title: Cook uncovered
steps.text: Cook on medium flame for 6 minutes, stirring gently now and then, until tender and lightly browned. Do not cover.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Uncover, raise the flame for 1 minute to dry any moisture, then add the coriander leaves and mix gently.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with phulka, paratha or dal-rice.

tips: Cut vegetables to the same size so they cook evenly.
Cook on low heat with the lid on; the vegetables steam in their own moisture and need very little oil.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat oil in a wide pan, crackle the cumin and add hing.

steps.title: Arrange
steps.text: Place the stuffed vegetables in a single layer and sprinkle over the leftover masala.

steps.text: Cover and cook on low flame for 10 minutes, turning gently every 4–5 minutes, until tender and evenly browned.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with phulka or as a side with dal-rice.

recipes.description: Small brinjals in a pickle-spice gravy.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Wash and cut the brinjal into bite-sized pieces.

steps.title: Make the gravy
steps.text: Heat mustard oil until it smokes lightly, lower the flame and add the pickle spices (fennel, kalonji, methi, mustard). Sauté the onion until golden, add ginger, garlic and tomato and cook until thick. Lower the flame and stir in the whisked curd.

steps.title: Adjust
steps.text: Add water as needed for a medium-thick gravy, add salt and bring to a gentle boil.

steps.title: Add the main ingredients
steps.text: Add the brinjal and stir gently to coat with the gravy.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Cover and simmer on low flame for 12 minutes until everything is cooked and the flavours blend.

steps.title: Finish & serve
steps.text: Add the coriander leaves and serve hot.

tips: Cook the masala until oil separates; this removes the raw taste and gives a rich gravy with less fat.
Add paneer or soft vegetables at the end so they stay soft and hold their shape.
serving_ideas: phulka, multigrain roti, jeera rice or brown rice.
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2 days. Reheat gently, adding a splash of water.

recipes.description: Pulao made with barnyard millet.

steps.title: Rinse & soak
steps.text: Wash the barnyard millet 3–4 times until the water runs clear and soak for 30 minutes. Drain.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee and oil in a heavy pot or cooker. Add the whole spices and fry for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the onion and sauté until light golden, then ginger, garlic and green chilli.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the carrot, french beans and green peas and sauté for 2–3 minutes.

steps.title: Add the barnyard millet
steps.text: Add the drained grain and stir gently for 1–2 minutes to coat it with ghee.

steps.title: Add water
steps.text: Add 440 ml hot water and salt; taste the water, it should be slightly salty.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Cover and cook on the lowest flame for 12–15 minutes (or 1 whistle in a pressure cooker) until the water is absorbed and the grains are tender.

steps.title: Rest & fluff
steps.text: Rest covered for 5–10 minutes, then fluff gently with a fork. Garnish and serve.

tips: Rest the rice for 5 minutes after cooking; the grains firm up and stay separate.
Use a heavy-bottomed pot and the lowest flame so the bottom does not burn.
serving_ideas: raita, a green salad and papad (roasted).
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day. Reheat with a sprinkle of water.

recipes.description: Barnyard millet and moong khichdi.

steps.title: Wash & soak
steps.text: Wash the barnyard millet and moong dal together until the water runs clear and soak for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee in a pressure cooker, crackle the cumin, add hing, ginger and green chilli.

steps.title: Add vegetables
steps.text: Add the carrot and green peas and sauté for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Add grains & water
steps.text: Add the drained grains, turmeric, salt and 720 ml water. Stir well.

steps.title: Pressure-cook
steps.text: Cook for 3–4 whistles on medium flame. Let the pressure release naturally.

steps.title: Adjust
steps.text: Open, mash lightly and add hot water if you like a softer, porridge-like consistency.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with a spoon of ghee, curd and roasted papad.

tips: A softer, mushier khichdi is easier to digest when you are unwell.
Add a little extra ghee on top just before serving for aroma.
serving_ideas: curd, kadhi or raita, roasted papad and a pickle (in moderation).
Best time: dinner; ideal when unwell.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh; keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: Wash and cook the rice with water and salt until each grain is soft but separate. Spread on a plate to cool completely.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat the oil and crackle the mustard seeds, then add the urad dal, chana dal, dry red chillies, curry leaves, hing and peanuts and fry until the dals and nuts turn golden.

steps.text: Sauté the beetroot until soft and add the spice powder.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Add the cooled rice and gently fold everything together without mashing the grains.

steps.title: Rest & serve
steps.text: Rest for 10 minutes so the flavours soak in. Garnish and serve warm or at room temperature.

tips: Use cooled, day-old or fully cooled rice so the grains stay separate.

recipes.description: Fried rice with broccoli.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: Cook the basmati rice until just done, spread on a plate and cool completely (day-old rice is ideal).

steps.title: Heat the wok
steps.text: Heat oil in a wok on the highest flame until it just starts to smoke.

steps.title: Aromatics
steps.text: Add garlic, ginger and the white part of the spring onions and stir-fry for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Stir-fry
steps.text: Add the vegetables and broccoli and toss on high heat for 2–3 minutes; they should stay crunchy.

steps.title: Add rice
steps.text: Add the cold rice, soy sauce, vinegar, pepper and a little salt. Toss on high heat for 2 minutes, breaking up any lumps.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Add the spring onion greens, toss once and serve immediately.

tips: Use cold rice and a very hot wok so the rice does not turn mushy.
Low-sodium soy sauce keeps the salt in check.
serving_ideas: a bowl of clear soup or a light Indo-Chinese gravy.
Best time: lunch or dinner.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Mix the carrot, french beans, green peas, cauliflower and paneer with the marinade ingredients and rest for at least 30 minutes.

steps.title: Caramelise the onions
steps.text: Heat oil and half the ghee in a heavy pot and fry the sliced onions on medium flame, stirring, until deep golden (12–15 minutes). Remove half for layering.

steps.title: Cook the base
steps.text: Add the marinated carrot, french beans, green peas, cauliflower and paneer to the remaining onions and cook on medium flame until almost done and the masala is thick.

steps.title: Par-boil the rice
steps.text: Boil the water with salt and whole spices. Add the drained rice and cook for 5–6 minutes until 70% done (the grain should still have a bite). Drain.

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: Spread the rice over the base. Top with fried onions, mint, coriander, garam masala, saffron soaked in warm milk and the remaining ghee.

steps.title: Dum
steps.text: Cover tightly (seal with foil or dough) and cook on the lowest flame for 25 minutes, or place the pot on a hot tawa.

steps.title: Rest & serve
steps.text: Rest for 10 minutes, then gently mix from the side and serve with raita.

tips: Par-boil the rice only 70%; it finishes cooking on dum.
Use a heavy pot or place it on a tawa so the bottom layer does not burn.
serving_ideas: onion-cucumber raita and a fresh salad.
Best time: lunch or festive meals.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1–2 days; sprinkle water and reheat covered.

recipes.description: Biryani with chickpeas and potato.

steps.title: Soak the rice
steps.text: Wash the basmati rice gently 3–4 times and soak for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Mix the kabuli chana and potato with the marinade ingredients and rest for at least 30 minutes.

steps.title: Caramelise the onions
steps.text: Heat oil and half the ghee in a heavy pot and fry the sliced onions on medium flame, stirring, until deep golden (12–15 minutes). Remove half for layering.

steps.title: Cook the base
steps.text: Add the marinated kabuli chana and potato to the remaining onions and cook on medium flame until almost done and the masala is thick.

steps.title: Par-boil the rice
steps.text: Boil the water with salt and whole spices. Add the drained rice and cook for 5–6 minutes until 70% done (the grain should still have a bite). Drain.

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: Spread the rice over the base. Top with fried onions, mint, coriander, garam masala, saffron soaked in warm milk and the remaining ghee.

steps.title: Dum
steps.text: Cover tightly (seal with foil or dough) and cook on the lowest flame for 15 minutes, or place the pot on a hot tawa.

steps.title: Rest & serve
steps.text: Rest for 10 minutes, then gently mix from the side and serve with raita.

tips: Par-boil the rice only 70%; it finishes cooking on dum.
Use a heavy pot or place it on a tawa so the bottom layer does not burn.
serving_ideas: onion-cucumber raita and a fresh salad.
Best time: lunch or festive meals.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1–2 days; sprinkle water and reheat covered.

recipes.description: Khichdi with chana dal.

steps.title: Wash & soak
steps.text: Wash the rice and chana dal together until the water runs clear and soak for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee in a pressure cooker, crackle the cumin, add hing, ginger and green chilli.

steps.title: Add vegetables
steps.text: Add the tomato and carrot and sauté for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Add grains & water
steps.text: Add the drained grains, turmeric, salt and 720 ml water. Stir well.

steps.title: Pressure-cook
steps.text: Cook for 4–5 whistles on medium flame. Let the pressure release naturally.

steps.title: Adjust
steps.text: Open, mash lightly and add hot water if you like a softer, porridge-like consistency.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with a spoon of ghee, curd and roasted papad.

tips: A softer, mushier khichdi is easier to digest when you are unwell.
Add a little extra ghee on top just before serving for aroma.
serving_ideas: curd, kadhi or raita, roasted papad and a pickle (in moderation).
Best time: dinner; ideal when unwell.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh; keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: Cook the basmati rice until just done, spread on a plate and cool completely (day-old rice is ideal).

steps.title: Heat the wok
steps.text: Heat oil in a wok on the highest flame until it just starts to smoke.

steps.title: Aromatics
steps.text: Add garlic, ginger and the white part of the spring onions and stir-fry for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Stir-fry
steps.text: Add the vegetables and chicken and tomato and toss on high heat for 2–3 minutes; they should stay crunchy.

steps.title: Add rice
steps.text: Add the cold rice, soy sauce, vinegar, pepper and a little salt. Toss on high heat for 2 minutes, breaking up any lumps.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Add the spring onion greens, toss once and serve immediately.

tips: Use cold rice and a very hot wok so the rice does not turn mushy.
Low-sodium soy sauce keeps the salt in check.
serving_ideas: a bowl of clear soup or a light Indo-Chinese gravy.
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh; keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

steps.text: Heat oil and half the ghee in a heavy pot and fry the sliced onions on medium flame, stirring, until deep golden (12–15 minutes). Remove half for layering.

steps.text: Add the marinated chicken, potato and eggs to the remaining onions and cook on medium flame until almost done and the masala is thick.

steps.text: Boil the water with salt and whole spices. Add the drained rice and cook for 5–6 minutes until 70% done (the grain should still have a bite). Drain.

recipes.description: A protein-rich biryani made with quinoa.

steps.title: Soak the rice
steps.text: Wash the quinoa gently 3–4 times and soak for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Mix the carrot, french beans, green peas and cauliflower with the marinade ingredients and rest for at least 30 minutes.

steps.title: Caramelise the onions
steps.text: Heat oil and half the ghee in a heavy pot and fry the sliced onions on medium flame, stirring, until deep golden (12–15 minutes). Remove half for layering.

steps.title: Cook the base
steps.text: Add the marinated carrot, french beans, green peas and cauliflower to the remaining onions and cook on medium flame until almost done and the masala is thick.

steps.title: Par-boil the rice
steps.text: Boil the water with salt and whole spices. Add the drained rice and cook for 5–6 minutes until 70% done (the grain should still have a bite). Drain.

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: Spread the rice over the base. Top with fried onions, mint, coriander, garam masala, saffron soaked in warm milk and the remaining ghee.

steps.title: Dum
steps.text: Cover tightly (seal with foil or dough) and cook on the lowest flame for 15 minutes, or place the pot on a hot tawa.

steps.title: Rest & serve
steps.text: Rest for 10 minutes, then gently mix from the side and serve with raita.

tips: Par-boil the rice only 70%; it finishes cooking on dum.
Use a heavy pot or place it on a tawa so the bottom layer does not burn.
serving_ideas: onion-cucumber raita and a fresh salad.
Best time: lunch or festive meals.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1–2 days; sprinkle water and reheat covered.

steps.title: Rinse & soak
steps.text: Wash the basmati rice 3–4 times until the water runs clear and soak for 20 minutes. Drain.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee and oil in a heavy pot or cooker. Add the whole spices and fry for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the onion and sauté until light golden, then ginger, garlic and green chilli.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the spinach and sweet corn kernels and sauté for 2–3 minutes.

steps.text: Add the drained grain and stir gently for 1–2 minutes to coat it with ghee.

recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day. Reheat with a sprinkle of water.

recipes.description: Sweet corn with pomegranate.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Wash all the produce well. Chop the sweet corn kernels, pomegranate seeds, onion and mint leaves into small, even pieces.

steps.title: Make the dressing
steps.text: In a small bowl, whisk together the lemon juice and chaat masala until well combined.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Put the salad ingredients in a large bowl, pour the dressing over and toss gently with two spoons.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Let the salad sit for 5 minutes so the flavours mingle (not longer, or the vegetables release water).

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve immediately, or keep the dressing separate until serving if packing for later.

tips: Add salt and dressing just before eating so the salad stays crunchy.
Chill the vegetables beforehand for a refreshing salad.

recipes.description: A cooling ash gourd soup.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Wash and roughly chop the ash gourd.

steps.title: Sauté
steps.text: Heat oil in a pot and sauté the garlic, ginger and onion for 2–3 minutes until soft and fragrant.

steps.title: Add vegetables
steps.text: Add the ash gourd and moong dal and sauté for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Pressure-cook
steps.text: Add the water and salt and pressure-cook for 2–3 whistles until everything is very soft.

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: Cool slightly and blend until smooth. Strain if you like a silky soup.

steps.title: Reheat
steps.text: Return to the pot, adjust the thickness with hot water and bring to a gentle boil.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Add pepper and check the salt.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Pour into bowls, garnish with the coriander leaves and lemon juice and serve hot.

tips: Thicken soups with a little blended potato, oats or dal instead of cornflour or cream.
Add lemon juice only after switching off the heat.
serving_ideas: a slice of whole-wheat toast or a small salad.
Best time: as a starter or a light dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2 days; can be frozen for 1 month (without cream).

recipes.description: A creamy avocado-mint dip.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Wash and roughly chop the ripe avocado, mint leaves, green chilli and garlic.

steps.title: Grind
steps.text: Put everything in a mixer jar and grind to a smooth (or slightly coarse) paste, adding water a spoon at a time.

steps.title: Taste
steps.text: Check the salt, sourness and heat and adjust.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Transfer to a bowl and serve fresh.

tips: Grind with a little ice-cold water to keep green chutneys bright.
A squeeze of lemon helps green chutneys keep their colour.
serving_ideas: dosa, idli, chila, paratha, sandwiches or as a dip for snacks.
Use 1–2 tbsp per serving.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2–3 days.

steps.text: Sauté onion and red chillies in oil until golden.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Let the mixture cool completely before grinding.

steps.title: Grind
steps.text: Put everything in a mixer jar and grind to a smooth (or slightly coarse) paste, adding water a spoon at a time.

steps.title: Taste
steps.text: Check the salt, sourness and heat and adjust.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Transfer to a bowl and serve fresh.

tips: Grind with a little ice-cold water to keep green chutneys bright.
A squeeze of lemon helps green chutneys keep their colour.
serving_ideas: dosa, idli, chila, paratha, sandwiches or as a dip for snacks.
Use 1–2 tbsp per serving.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2–3 days.

recipes.description: Soya chunks tikka with pickle spices.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Cut the soya chunks, capsicum and onion into even 1½-inch pieces.

steps.title: Make the marinade
steps.text: Whisk hung curd with roasted besan, ginger-garlic, spices, lemon juice, mustard oil and salt into a thick paste.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Coat everything well and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes (up to 4 hours).

steps.title: Skewer
steps.text: Thread onto skewers (soak wooden ones in water for 20 minutes first), alternating with capsicum and onion.

steps.title: Grill
steps.text: Grill in an oven, air fryer or on a grill pan at 200°C for 12–15 minutes, turning once, until charred at the edges. Brush with a few drops of oil halfway.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Sprinkle chaat masala and lemon juice and serve hot with onion rings and mint chutney.

tips: Use thick hung curd so the marinade clings and does not drip.
Roasted besan in the marinade helps it stick and adds a smoky flavour.
serving_ideas: mint chutney and an onion-cucumber salad.
Best time: starter or a high-protein snack.
recipes.storage: marinated pieces keep in the fridge for 1 day; grill just before serving.

recipes.description: Crisp brinjal fries.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Wash, dry and slice the brinjal as listed.

steps.title: Coat
steps.text: Mix the coating ingredients into a thick batter (or dry rub) and toss the brinjal so every piece is coated.

steps.title: Preheat
steps.text: Preheat the air fryer to 190°C for 3 minutes and brush the basket with oil.

steps.title: Arrange
steps.text: Place the pieces in a single layer without overlapping. Spray or brush lightly with oil.

steps.title: Air-fry
steps.text: Cook for 12–15 minutes, shaking or turning halfway, until golden and crisp.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with green chutney.

tips: Do not overcrowd the basket; crispness needs hot air around every piece.
No air fryer? Bake at 210°C for 18–20 minutes, turning once.
serving_ideas: green chutney or hung curd dip, and a cup of tea or buttermilk.
Best time: evening snack or a starter.
recipes.storage: best eaten hot and fresh.

recipes.description: Colocasia patties with ajwain.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Boil, steam or chop the arbi, green chilli, ginger and coriander leaves as listed and let them cool.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Combine everything in a bowl and mash well. The mixture should hold its shape when pressed; add a little more rice flour if it is too soft.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Grease your palms and shape into 8 round, flat tikkis about ½ inch thick.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Refrigerate for 15 minutes so they hold firm while cooking.

steps.title: Pan-roast
steps.text: Heat a non-stick tawa, brush with oil and cook the tikkis on medium flame for 3–4 minutes per side until golden and crisp.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with green chutney or hung curd dip.

tips: Chilling the tikkis before cooking stops them from breaking.
Use a non-stick pan and a light brush of oil; there is no need to deep-fry.
serving_ideas: green chutney or hung curd dip, and a cup of tea or buttermilk.
Best time: evening snack or a starter.
Stuff in a whole-wheat wrap with salad for a quick meal.
recipes.storage: uncooked tikkis keep in the fridge for 1 day or can be frozen for 1 month.

recipes.description: Pink instant rava dhokla.

steps.title: Make the batter
steps.text: Mix the rava / suji, curd, beetroot and ginger and salt with enough water to make a smooth, thick, pourable batter.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Cover and rest the batter for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare the steamer
steps.text: Boil water in a steamer or large pot with a stand. Grease a 7-inch tin or plate with oil.

steps.title: Add the leavening
steps.text: Just before steaming, add the fruit salt with 1 tsp water and stir gently in one direction until frothy.

steps.title: Steam
steps.text: Pour into the greased tin immediately and steam on medium-high flame for 15 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the centre comes out clean.

steps.title: Cool & cut
steps.text: Rest for 5 minutes, then cut into squares or diamonds.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat oil, crackle the mustard seeds and sesame, add curry leaves, green chillies and hing. Add water and lemon juice and pour evenly over the pieces.

steps.title: Garnish & serve
steps.text: Sprinkle with coriander and coconut and serve.

tips: Do not open the steamer for the first 10 minutes; the batter can collapse.
Pour the tempering water slowly so the pieces stay soft and moist.
serving_ideas: green chutney or hung curd dip, and a cup of tea or buttermilk.
Best time: evening snack or a starter.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day; best at room temperature.

recipes.description: Broccoli in a creamy tikka marinade.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Cut the broccoli, capsicum and onion into even 1½-inch pieces.

steps.title: Make the marinade
steps.text: Whisk hung curd with roasted besan, ginger-garlic, spices, lemon juice, mustard oil and salt into a thick paste.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Coat everything well and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes (up to 4 hours).

steps.title: Skewer
steps.text: Thread onto skewers (soak wooden ones in water for 20 minutes first), alternating with capsicum and onion.

steps.title: Grill
steps.text: Grill in an oven, air fryer or on a grill pan at 200°C for 12–15 minutes, turning once, until charred at the edges. Brush with a few drops of oil halfway.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Sprinkle chaat masala and lemon juice and serve hot with onion rings and mint chutney.

tips: Use thick hung curd so the marinade clings and does not drip.
Roasted besan in the marinade helps it stick and adds a smoky flavour.
serving_ideas: mint chutney and an onion-cucumber salad.
Best time: starter or a high-protein snack.
recipes.storage: marinated pieces keep in the fridge for 1 day; grill just before serving.

recipes.description: Crisp broccoli and potato tikkis.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Boil, steam or chop the broccoli, potato, paneer, green chilli, ginger and coriander leaves as listed and let them cool.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Combine everything in a bowl and mash well. The mixture should hold its shape when pressed; add a little more rolled oats if it is too soft.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Grease your palms and shape into 8 round, flat tikkis about ½ inch thick.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Refrigerate for 15 minutes so they hold firm while cooking.

steps.title: Pan-roast
steps.text: Heat a non-stick tawa, brush with oil and cook the tikkis on medium flame for 3–4 minutes per side until golden and crisp.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with green chutney or hung curd dip.

tips: Chilling the tikkis before cooking stops them from breaking.
Use a non-stick pan and a light brush of oil; there is no need to deep-fry.
serving_ideas: green chutney or hung curd dip, and a cup of tea or buttermilk.
Best time: evening snack or a starter.
Stuff in a whole-wheat wrap with salad for a quick meal.
recipes.storage: uncooked tikkis keep in the fridge for 1 day or can be frozen for 1 month.

recipes.description: Steamed carrot muthia.

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: Mix the whole-wheat flour, besan, rava / suji and carrot with ginger, chilli, spices, sesame, lemon juice, sugar, salt, soda and oil. Knead into a soft dough without water (or just a few drops).

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Grease your palms and shape into 4–5 cylindrical rolls about 1 inch thick.

steps.title: Steam
steps.text: Steam the rolls on a greased plate for 20–25 minutes, until a knife comes out clean.

steps.title: Cool & slice
steps.text: Cool for 10 minutes and slice into ½-inch rounds.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat oil, crackle mustard and sesame, add curry leaves and hing, then the muthia slices.

steps.title: Crisp
steps.text: Toss on medium flame for 4–5 minutes until lightly crisp.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with coriander and serve with green chutney and tea.

tips: Do not add water; the vegetables release enough moisture.
Steamed muthia keep in the fridge for 2 days; temper just before serving.
serving_ideas: green chutney or hung curd dip, and a cup of tea or buttermilk.
Best time: evening snack or a starter.
recipes.storage: steamed rolls keep in the fridge for 2 days.

recipes.description: Tangy chaat masala makhana.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Measure out the makhana.

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Heat the ghee in a wide pan on low flame. Add the makhana and roast, stirring often, for 10 minutes until crisp and crunchy.

steps.title: Test
steps.text: Cool one piece for a few seconds and bite; it should break with a crunch.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Switch off the flame and sprinkle the chaat masala, amchur and black salt. Toss well.

steps.title: Cool & store
steps.text: Cool completely before storing in an airtight jar.

tips: Roast on low heat; high heat browns the outside while the inside stays chewy.
Store only after cooling completely, or it turns soggy.
serving_ideas: a cup of tea, green tea or buttermilk.
A perfect office or travel snack.
recipes.storage: keeps crisp in an airtight jar for 1–2 weeks.

recipes.description: Chana dal sundal.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Soak 2 hours and cook until just soft, not mushy.

steps.title: Drain
steps.text: Drain well; keep the water for soups or dal.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat coconut oil, crackle mustard seeds, add urad dal, dry red chillies, curry leaves, hing, green chilli and ginger.

steps.title: Toss
steps.text: Add the cooked chana dal and salt and toss for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Switch off, add the grated coconut, lemon juice and coriander and mix.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve warm as an evening snack.

tips: Cook the legumes until soft but still whole; mushy legumes make a sticky sundal.
serving_ideas: a cup of tea or buttermilk.
Best time: evening snack; a traditional Navratri offering.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

steps.text: Mix the rolled oats, besan, rava / suji and lauki with ginger, chilli, spices, sesame, lemon juice, sugar, salt, soda and oil. Knead into a soft dough without water (or just a few drops).

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Grease your palms and shape into 4–5 cylindrical rolls about 1 inch thick.

steps.title: Steam
steps.text: Steam the rolls on a greased plate for 20–25 minutes, until a knife comes out clean.

steps.title: Cool & slice
steps.text: Cool for 10 minutes and slice into ½-inch rounds.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat oil, crackle mustard and sesame, add curry leaves and hing, then the muthia slices.

steps.title: Crisp
steps.text: Toss on medium flame for 4–5 minutes until lightly crisp.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with coriander and serve with green chutney and tea.

tips: Do not add water; the vegetables release enough moisture.
Steamed muthia keep in the fridge for 2 days; temper just before serving.
serving_ideas: green chutney or hung curd dip, and a cup of tea or buttermilk.
Best time: evening snack or a starter.
recipes.storage: steamed rolls keep in the fridge for 2 days.

recipes.description: Black-eyed bean chaat.

steps.title: Prepare the base
steps.text: Keep the lobia ready (cooked and cooled where needed).

steps.title: Chop the toppings
steps.text: Finely chop the onion, tomato, coriander leaves and green chilli.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: In a bowl, combine the base and toppings.

steps.title: Dress
steps.text: Add lemon juice, chaat masala, roasted cumin, chilli powder and salt. Toss well.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve immediately so it stays crunchy.

tips: Mix chaat just before eating; it turns soggy if it waits.
serving_ideas: enjoy on its own as an evening snack.
Use chutneys sparingly; they add sugar and salt.
recipes.storage: best eaten immediately.

recipes.description: Almonds roasted with a light spice coating.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Measure out the almonds.

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Heat the ghee in a wide pan on low flame. Add the almonds and roast, stirring often, for 8 minutes until crisp and crunchy.

steps.title: Test
steps.text: Cool one piece for a few seconds and bite; it should break with a crunch.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Switch off the flame and sprinkle the kashmiri red chilli powder and chaat masala. Toss well.

steps.title: Cool & store
steps.text: Cool completely before storing in an airtight jar.

tips: Roast on low heat; high heat browns the outside while the inside stays chewy.
Store only after cooling completely, or it turns soggy.
serving_ideas: a cup of tea, green tea or buttermilk.
A perfect office or travel snack.
recipes.storage: keeps crisp in an airtight jar for 1–2 weeks.

recipes.description: Protein-rich red lentil dhokla.

steps.title: Make the batter
steps.text: Grind the soaked masoor dal with ginger and chilli to a thick batter.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Cover and rest the batter for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare the steamer
steps.text: Boil water in a steamer or large pot with a stand. Grease a 7-inch tin or plate with oil.

steps.title: Add the leavening
steps.text: Just before steaming, add the fruit salt with 1 tsp water and stir gently in one direction until frothy.

steps.title: Steam
steps.text: Pour into the greased tin immediately and steam on medium-high flame for 15 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the centre comes out clean.

steps.title: Cool & cut
steps.text: Rest for 5 minutes, then cut into squares or diamonds.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat oil, crackle the mustard seeds and sesame, add curry leaves, green chillies and hing. Add water and lemon juice and pour evenly over the pieces.

steps.title: Garnish & serve
steps.text: Sprinkle with coriander and coconut and serve.

tips: Do not open the steamer for the first 10 minutes; the batter can collapse.
Pour the tempering water slowly so the pieces stay soft and moist.
serving_ideas: green chutney or hung curd dip, and a cup of tea or buttermilk.
Best time: evening snack or a starter.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day; best at room temperature.

recipes.description: Moth bean sundal with coconut.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Soak 6 hours and pressure-cook for 1–2 whistles.

steps.title: Drain
steps.text: Drain well; keep the water for soups or dal.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat coconut oil, crackle mustard seeds, add urad dal, dry red chillies, curry leaves, hing, green chilli and ginger.

steps.title: Toss
steps.text: Add the cooked moth beans and salt and toss for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Switch off, add the grated coconut, lemon juice and coriander and mix.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve warm as an evening snack.

tips: Cook the legumes until soft but still whole; mushy legumes make a sticky sundal.

recipes.description: Creamy, mild mushroom tikka.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Cut the mushrooms, capsicum and onion into even 1½-inch pieces.

steps.title: Make the marinade
steps.text: Whisk hung curd with roasted besan, ginger-garlic, spices, lemon juice, mustard oil and salt into a thick paste.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Coat everything well and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes (up to 4 hours).

steps.title: Skewer
steps.text: Thread onto skewers (soak wooden ones in water for 20 minutes first), alternating with capsicum and onion.

steps.title: Grill
steps.text: Grill in an oven, air fryer or on a grill pan at 200°C for 12–15 minutes, turning once, until charred at the edges. Brush with a few drops of oil halfway.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Sprinkle chaat masala and lemon juice and serve hot with onion rings and mint chutney.

tips: Use thick hung curd so the marinade clings and does not drip.
Roasted besan in the marinade helps it stick and adds a smoky flavour.
serving_ideas: mint chutney and an onion-cucumber salad.
Best time: starter or a high-protein snack.
recipes.storage: marinated pieces keep in the fridge for 1 day; grill just before serving.

steps.text: Coat everything well and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes (up to 4 hours).

steps.title: Skewer
steps.text: Thread onto skewers (soak wooden ones in water for 20 minutes first), alternating with capsicum and onion.

steps.title: Grill
steps.text: Grill in an oven, air fryer or on a grill pan at 200°C for 12–15 minutes, turning once, until charred at the edges. Brush with a few drops of oil halfway.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Sprinkle chaat masala and lemon juice and serve hot with onion rings and mint chutney.

tips: Use thick hung curd so the marinade clings and does not drip.
Roasted besan in the marinade helps it stick and adds a smoky flavour.
serving_ideas: mint chutney and an onion-cucumber salad.
Best time: starter or a high-protein snack.
recipes.storage: marinated pieces keep in the fridge for 1 day; grill just before serving.

recipes.description: White peas sundal, a Navratri favourite.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Soak overnight and pressure-cook for 5 whistles.

steps.title: Drain
steps.text: Drain well; keep the water for soups or dal.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat coconut oil, crackle mustard seeds, add urad dal, dry red chillies, curry leaves, hing, green chilli and ginger.

steps.title: Toss
steps.text: Add the cooked dried white peas and salt and toss for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Switch off, add the grated coconut, lemon juice and coriander and mix.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve warm as an evening snack.

tips: Cook the legumes until soft but still whole; mushy legumes make a sticky sundal.
serving_ideas: a cup of tea or buttermilk.
Best time: evening snack; a traditional Navratri offering.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

recipes.description: Coastal prawn cutlets.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Boil, steam or chop the prawns, potato, onion, ginger, garlic, green chilli and coriander leaves as listed and let them cool.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Combine everything in a bowl and mash well. The mixture should hold its shape when pressed; add a little more rolled oats if it is too soft.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Grease your palms and shape into 8 round, flat tikkis about ½ inch thick.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Refrigerate for 15 minutes so they hold firm while cooking.

steps.title: Pan-roast
steps.text: Heat a non-stick tawa, brush with oil and cook the tikkis on medium flame for 3–4 minutes per side until golden and crisp.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with green chutney or hung curd dip.

tips: Chilling the tikkis before cooking stops them from breaking.
Use a non-stick pan and a light brush of oil; there is no need to deep-fry.

Best time: evening snack or a starter.

recipes.description: A light murmura and peanut mix.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Measure out the murmura, peanuts, roasted chana and curry leaves.

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Heat the ghee in a wide pan on low flame. Add the murmura, peanuts, roasted chana and curry leaves and roast, stirring often, for 6 minutes until crisp and crunchy.

steps.title: Test
steps.text: Cool one piece for a few seconds and bite; it should break with a crunch.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Switch off the flame and sprinkle the turmeric powder. Toss well.

steps.title: Cool & store
steps.text: Cool completely before storing in an airtight jar.

tips: Roast on low heat; high heat browns the outside while the inside stays chewy.
Store only after cooling completely, or it turns soggy.
serving_ideas: a cup of tea, green tea or buttermilk.
A perfect office or travel snack.
recipes.storage: keeps crisp in an airtight jar for 1–2 weeks.

recipes.description: Calcium-rich ragi dhokla.

steps.title: Make the batter
steps.text: Mix the ragi, rava / suji, curd, ginger and green chilli and salt with enough water to make a smooth, thick, pourable batter.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Cover and rest the batter for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare the steamer
steps.text: Boil water in a steamer or large pot with a stand. Grease a 7-inch tin or plate with oil.

steps.title: Add the leavening
steps.text: Just before steaming, add the fruit salt with 1 tsp water and stir gently in one direction until frothy.

steps.title: Steam
steps.text: Pour into the greased tin immediately and steam on medium-high flame for 15 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the centre comes out clean.

steps.title: Cool & cut
steps.text: Rest for 5 minutes, then cut into squares or diamonds.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat oil, crackle the mustard seeds and sesame, add curry leaves, green chillies and hing. Add water and lemon juice and pour evenly over the pieces.

steps.title: Garnish & serve
steps.text: Sprinkle with coriander and coconut and serve.

tips: Do not open the steamer for the first 10 minutes; the batter can collapse.
Pour the tempering water slowly so the pieces stay soft and moist.
serving_ideas: green chutney or hung curd dip, and a cup of tea or buttermilk.
Best time: evening snack or a starter.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day; best at room temperature.

recipes.description: Ragi and methi steamed muthia.

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: Mix the ragi, besan, rava / suji and methi with ginger, chilli, spices, sesame, lemon juice, sugar, salt, soda and oil. Knead into a soft dough without water (or just a few drops).

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Grease your palms and shape into 4–5 cylindrical rolls about 1 inch thick.

steps.title: Steam
steps.text: Steam the rolls on a greased plate for 20–25 minutes, until a knife comes out clean.

steps.title: Cool & slice
steps.text: Cool for 10 minutes and slice into ½-inch rounds.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat oil, crackle mustard and sesame, add curry leaves and hing, then the muthia slices.

steps.title: Crisp
steps.text: Toss on medium flame for 4–5 minutes until lightly crisp.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with coriander and serve with green chutney and tea.

tips: Do not add water; the vegetables release enough moisture.
Steamed muthia keep in the fridge for 2 days; temper just before serving.
serving_ideas: green chutney or hung curd dip, and a cup of tea or buttermilk.
Best time: evening snack or a starter.
recipes.storage: steamed rolls keep in the fridge for 2 days.

steps.text: Switch off the flame and sprinkle the tandoori masala and chaat masala. Toss well.

recipes.description: Assorted vegetables in a tandoori marinade.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Cut the cauliflower, capsicum, onion, mushrooms and baby corn, capsicum and onion into even 1½-inch pieces.

steps.title: Make the marinade
steps.text: Whisk hung curd with roasted besan, ginger-garlic, spices, lemon juice, mustard oil and salt into a thick paste.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Coat everything well and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes (up to 4 hours).

steps.title: Skewer
steps.text: Thread onto skewers (soak wooden ones in water for 20 minutes first), alternating with capsicum and onion.

steps.title: Grill
steps.text: Grill in an oven, air fryer or on a grill pan at 200°C for 12–15 minutes, turning once, until charred at the edges. Brush with a few drops of oil halfway.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Sprinkle chaat masala and lemon juice and serve hot with onion rings and mint chutney.

tips: Use thick hung curd so the marinade clings and does not drip.
Roasted besan in the marinade helps it stick and adds a smoky flavour.
serving_ideas: mint chutney and an onion-cucumber salad.
Best time: starter or a high-protein snack.
recipes.storage: marinated pieces keep in the fridge for 1 day; grill just before serving.

recipes.description: Chicken tikka with pickle spices.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Clean the chicken, pat dry and make deep slits so the marinade penetrates.

steps.title: First marinade
steps.text: Rub with lemon juice, salt and chilli and rest for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Second marinade
steps.text: Mix the remaining marinade ingredients into a thick paste, coat well and refrigerate for at least 2 hours (overnight is best).

steps.title: Preheat
steps.text: Preheat the oven or air fryer to 200°C.

steps.title: Grill
steps.text: Grill for 15–20 minutes, turning once and brushing with a few drops of oil, until charred at the edges and cooked through.

steps.title: Rest & serve

tips: Hung curd marinade keeps the meat juicy without frying.

recipes.description: Spicy Andhra-style chicken curry.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Wash and drain the chicken. Mix with the marinade ingredients and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes (overnight is best).

steps.title: Make the masala
steps.text: Sauté curry leaves, onion and chillies until golden, add ginger-garlic, tomato and spices, then poppy seed paste.

steps.title: Add the chicken
steps.text: Add the marinated chicken and cook on high flame for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until it changes colour and is coated in masala.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Add water as needed, cover and simmer on low flame for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is tender and cooked through.

steps.title: Check
steps.text: The chicken is done when the juices run clear and there is no pink near the bone.

steps.title: Finish & serve
steps.text: Add the coriander leaves and serve hot.

tips: Use skinless chicken to cut saturated fat.
Simmer gently; boiling hard makes chicken tough.
serving_ideas: phulka, jeera rice or brown rice, with a salad and curd.
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2 days; freezes for 1 month.

recipes.description: Spicy Andhra-style fish fry.

steps.title: Clean
steps.text: Wash the fish fillets, pat completely dry and make shallow slits.

steps.title: Make the masala
steps.text: Mix the masala ingredients into a thick paste with lemon juice (no water).

steps.title: Coat
steps.text: Rub the paste all over the fish, into the slits, and rest for 20–30 minutes.

steps.title: Heat the pan
steps.text: Heat a non-stick or cast-iron tawa on medium flame and brush with oil.

steps.title: Shallow-fry
steps.text: Place the fish and cook for 3–4 minutes per side, drizzling a little oil around, until crisp and cooked through.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with onion rings and lemon wedges.

tips: Pat the fish completely dry; moisture stops it from crisping.
Flip only once to keep the pieces whole.
serving_ideas: onion rings, lemon wedges and rice with dal or rasam.
Best time: lunch.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh.

recipes.description: Bihari fish curry with mustard and tomato.

steps.title: Clean & season
steps.text: Wash the fish fillets well, pat dry and rub with turmeric, chilli and salt. Rest for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Sear (optional)
steps.text: Lightly sear the pieces in a non-stick pan with a few drops of oil for 1 minute per side; this helps them hold their shape.

steps.title: Make the curry
steps.text: Heat mustard oil, add kalonji, sauté onion and garlic, add tomato, mustard paste and spices.

steps.title: Boil
steps.text: Add water as needed, check the salt and bring to a gentle boil.

steps.title: Add the fish
steps.text: Slide in the pieces in a single layer. Simmer for 8 minutes without stirring; swirl the pan gently instead.

steps.title: Rest & serve
steps.text: Switch off, cover and rest for 10 minutes so the flavours develop. Serve hot.

tips: Do not stir after adding the fish; swirl the pan so the pieces stay whole.
Fish cooks fast; it is done when it flakes easily.
serving_ideas: steamed rice or red rice, with a vegetable side.
Best time: lunch.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day. Reheat gently.

recipes.description: Fish tikka in a green herb marinade.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Clean the fish fillets, pat dry and make deep slits so the marinade penetrates.

steps.title: First marinade
steps.text: Rub with lemon juice, salt and chilli and rest for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Second marinade
steps.text: Mix the remaining marinade ingredients into a thick paste, coat well and refrigerate for at least 2 hours (overnight is best).

steps.title: Preheat
steps.text: Preheat the oven or air fryer to 200°C.

steps.title: Grill
steps.text: Grill for 10–15 minutes, turning once and brushing with a few drops of oil, until charred at the edges and cooked through.

steps.title: Rest & serve

tips: Hung curd marinade keeps the meat juicy without frying.

serving_ideas: mint chutney, onion rings and a green salad.
Best time: a high-protein starter or dinner.
recipes.storage: marinated meat keeps in the fridge for 1 day; cooked tikka keeps 1 day.

steps.text: Cook on medium-low flame for 12 minutes, stirring often, until the liquid is absorbed and the halwa thickens.

recipes.description: Water chestnut flour halwa.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Prepare the singhara as listed.

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Heat the ghee and roast the singhara on low flame, stirring constantly, until golden and aromatic.

steps.title: Add the liquid
steps.text: Add the toned milk (it will splutter, so pour carefully) and stir continuously.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Cook on medium-low flame for 6 minutes, stirring often, until the liquid is absorbed and the halwa thickens.

steps.title: Sweeten
steps.text: Add the jaggery and cardamom and cook for 3–4 minutes until the halwa leaves the sides of the pan.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with the almonds and cashews and serve warm.

tips: Halwa needs patient stirring on low heat; do not rush it.
This lighter version uses less ghee and jaggery instead of sugar.
serving_ideas: enjoy a small portion after a meal, or with a cup of tea.
Keep sweets to a small bowl or 1–2 pieces.

recipes.description: Creamy kheer with crushed sweet corn.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Wash or roast the sweet corn kernels as listed.

steps.title: Boil the toned milk
steps.text: Bring the toned milk to a boil in a heavy-bottomed pan, stirring so it does not stick.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Add the sweet corn kernels and simmer on low flame for 15 minutes, stirring often and scraping the sides, until soft and creamy.

steps.title: Flavour
steps.text: Add the cardamom and saffron and simmer for 2 more minutes.

steps.title: Sweeten
steps.text: Switch off the flame and let it cool for 5 minutes, then stir in the jaggery. Adding jaggery off the heat keeps the milk from curdling.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with the almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled.

tips: Use a heavy-bottomed pan and stir often so the milk does not burn.
Kheer thickens as it cools; add a little warm milk to loosen it.
serving_ideas: enjoy a small portion after a meal, or with a cup of tea.
Keep sweets to a small bowl or 1–2 pieces.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

recipes.description: A barnyard millet dosa with a peppery mushroom filling.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Wash the barnyard millet and soak for 5–6 hours. Separately wash and soak the urad dal with the methi seeds for 4–5 hours.

steps.title: Grind
steps.text: Grind the urad dal with ice-cold water until light, fluffy and doubled in volume. Grind the soaked grain to a smooth paste. Mix both with clean hands.

steps.title: Ferment
steps.text: Add salt, cover and keep in a warm place for 8–12 hours (overnight) until the batter rises and smells mildly sour.

steps.title: Prepare the filling
steps.text: Sauté garlic, onion and mushrooms on high heat until dry; season with pepper.

steps.title: Heat the tawa
steps.text: Heat a cast-iron or non-stick tawa on medium-high flame. Sprinkle water; it should sizzle and evaporate. Wipe with an oiled cloth or half an onion.

steps.title: Spread the dosa
steps.text: Pour a ladle of batter in the centre and spread it in quick outward circles into a thin round.

steps.title: Crisp it up
steps.text: Drizzle ½ tsp oil or ghee over the dosa and cook on medium flame for 1–2 minutes until the base turns golden and crisp.

steps.title: Fill & fold
steps.text: Place 2–3 tbsp of filling in the centre, fold the dosa over and lift onto a plate.

steps.title: Repeat
steps.text: Wipe the tawa with a damp cloth between dosas to cool it slightly so the batter spreads evenly.

tips: In cold weather, ferment the batter in a switched-off oven with the light on.
Use non-iodised salt for better fermentation.
serving_ideas: coconut chutney and sambar.
Best time: breakfast or dinner.
recipes.storage: fermented batter keeps in the fridge for 3–4 days. Cooked dosas are best eaten fresh.

recipes.description: Green barnyard millet idlis with spinach.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Wash and soak the barnyard millet for 5–6 hours. Separately soak the urad dal with methi seeds for 4 hours.

steps.title: Grind the dal
steps.text: Grind the urad dal with ice-cold water, a little at a time, to a light, fluffy, smooth batter.

steps.title: Grind the grain
steps.text: Grind the soaked grain to a slightly coarse, semolina-like batter. Mix both batters well with your hand.

steps.title: Ferment
steps.text: Add salt, cover and leave in a warm place for 8–12 hours until it doubles and smells pleasantly sour.

steps.title: Add flavour
steps.text: Fold the spinach purée into the batter.

steps.title: Prepare the steamer
steps.text: Boil 2 cups water in an idli steamer or pressure cooker (without the whistle). Grease the idli moulds lightly.

steps.title: Fill the moulds
steps.text: Gently stir the batter without knocking out the air and pour into the moulds until three-quarters full.

steps.title: Steam
steps.text: Steam on medium-high flame for 10–12 minutes. A toothpick inserted in the centre should come out clean.

steps.title: Rest & demould
steps.text: Rest for 2 minutes, then scoop out the idlis with a wet spoon and serve hot.

tips: Use a 4:1 ratio of idli rice to urad dal for soft idlis.
Do not over-stir fermented batter; it loses the air that makes idlis fluffy.
serving_ideas: sambar and coconut or tomato chutney.
Best time: breakfast; also great for tiffin boxes.
recipes.storage: batter keeps in the fridge for 3–4 days; steamed idlis keep for 1 day and can be re-steamed.

recipes.description: A wholesome bajra chila with beetroot, quick to make and full of fibre.

steps.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps.text: Finely chop the onion and green chilli and grate the ginger. Small, even pieces keep the chila thin and help it cook evenly.

steps.title: Make the batter
steps.text: In a mixing bowl, combine the bajra, besan and beetroot with turmeric, ajwain, chilli powder and salt. Add water a little at a time and whisk to a smooth, lump-free batter that flows like dosa batter.

steps.title: Add vegetables & rest
steps.text: Fold in the chopped vegetables, ginger and coriander. Rest the batter for 10 minutes so it thickens slightly and the chila turns soft.

steps.title: Heat the pan
steps.text: Heat a non-stick or well-seasoned iron tawa on medium flame and brush it with ¼ tsp oil. A few drops of water should sizzle when the pan is ready.

steps.title: Spread the chila
steps.text: Pour one ladle of batter in the centre and spread it gently in circles into a 6–7 inch round. Drizzle a few drops of oil around the edges.

steps.title: Cook the first side
steps.text: Cook on medium-low flame for 2–3 minutes, until the top looks set and the edges lift easily and turn golden.

steps.title: Flip & cook
steps.text: Flip with a flat spatula and cook the other side for 1–2 minutes, pressing lightly, until golden spots appear.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with mint-coriander chutney or curd. Make the remaining chilas the same way, adding only a few drops of oil each time.

tips: Rest the batter for 10 minutes; it makes the chila softer and easier to flip.
Keep the flame medium-low so the centre cooks before the outside browns.
serving_ideas: mint-coriander chutney, plain curd or raita, and a cucumber-tomato salad.
Best time: breakfast, or an early evening meal.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh. Plain batter (without vegetables) keeps in the fridge in an airtight box for up to 12 hours.

recipes.description: A protein-rich chana dal chila with beetroot, no fermentation needed.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Wash the chana dal and beetroot 2–3 times and soak in plenty of water for 5 hours. Drain well.

steps.title: Grind the batter
steps.text: Grind the soaked dal with ginger, green chillies and cumin, adding water little by little, to a smooth, thick batter. It should coat the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Add hing and salt and mix in the onion and coriander leaves. The batter does not need fermentation and can be used right away.

steps.title: Heat the pan
steps.text: Heat a non-stick or iron tawa on medium flame and grease it lightly with oil.

steps.title: Spread the chila
steps.text: Pour a ladle of batter and spread it quickly into a thin round. Drizzle a few drops of oil around the edges.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Cook on medium flame for 2–3 minutes until the base is golden and crisp, then flip and cook the other side for 1 minute.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with green chutney or tomato chutney. Repeat with the remaining batter.

tips: Do not add too much water while grinding; a thick batter gives crisp chilas.
Soaking can be done overnight for a quicker morning.
serving_ideas: mint-coriander chutney, plain curd or raita, and a cucumber-tomato salad.
Best time: breakfast, or an early evening meal.
recipes.storage: Batter keeps in the fridge for up to 24 hours; stir and adjust with a little water before use.

recipes.description: Instant dalia idlis with beetroot.

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Dry-roast the dalia and rava / suji on low flame for 3–4 minutes until aromatic. Cool.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat oil, crackle mustard seeds, add urad dal, chana dal, cashews, curry leaves, green chilli and ginger and fry until golden. Add this to the roasted base.

steps.title: Mix the batter
steps.text: Add curd, salt and enough water to make a thick, idli-like batter. Stir in the beetroot.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Cover and rest for 15–20 minutes so the grains soften and swell.

steps.title: Prepare the steamer
steps.text: Boil water in the steamer and grease the idli moulds.

steps.title: Add fruit salt
steps.text: Just before steaming, add the Eno with 1 tsp water and stir gently in one direction; the batter will turn frothy.

steps.title: Steam
steps.text: Fill the moulds immediately and steam for 10–12 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Rest 2 minutes, demould and serve hot.

tips: Steam immediately after adding Eno; the bubbles fade if the batter waits.
Use fresh, slightly sour curd for the best taste.
serving_ideas: sambar and coconut or tomato chutney.
Best time: breakfast; also great for tiffin boxes.
recipes.storage: best eaten the same day; re-steam leftovers for 3 minutes.

recipes.description: A protein-rich mixed dal chila with beetroot, no fermentation needed.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Wash the moong dal, masoor dal, chana dal and beetroot 2–3 times and soak in plenty of water for 4 hours. Drain well.

steps.title: Grind the batter
steps.text: Grind the soaked dal with ginger, green chillies and cumin, adding water little by little, to a smooth, thick batter. It should coat the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Add hing and salt and mix in the onion and coriander leaves. The batter does not need fermentation and can be used right away.

steps.title: Heat the pan
steps.text: Heat a non-stick or iron tawa on medium flame and grease it lightly with oil.

steps.title: Spread the chila
steps.text: Pour a ladle of batter and spread it quickly into a thin round. Drizzle a few drops of oil around the edges.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Cook on medium flame for 2–3 minutes until the base is golden and crisp, then flip and cook the other side for 1 minute.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with green chutney or tomato chutney. Repeat with the remaining batter.

tips: Do not add too much water while grinding; a thick batter gives crisp chilas.
Soaking can be done overnight for a quicker morning.
serving_ideas: mint-coriander chutney, plain curd or raita, and a cucumber-tomato salad.
Best time: breakfast, or an early evening meal.
recipes.storage: Batter keeps in the fridge for up to 24 hours; stir and adjust with a little water before use.

recipes.description: Instant oats idlis with beetroot.

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Dry-roast the rolled oats and rava / suji on low flame for 3–4 minutes until aromatic. Cool.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat oil, crackle mustard seeds, add urad dal, chana dal, cashews, curry leaves, green chilli and ginger and fry until golden. Add this to the roasted base.

steps.title: Mix the batter
steps.text: Add curd, salt and enough water to make a thick, idli-like batter. Stir in the beetroot.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Cover and rest for 15–20 minutes so the grains soften and swell.

steps.title: Prepare the steamer
steps.text: Boil water in the steamer and grease the idli moulds.

steps.title: Add fruit salt
steps.text: Just before steaming, add the Eno with 1 tsp water and stir gently in one direction; the batter will turn frothy.

steps.title: Steam
steps.text: Fill the moulds immediately and steam for 10–12 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Rest 2 minutes, demould and serve hot.

tips: Steam immediately after adding Eno; the bubbles fade if the batter waits.
Use fresh, slightly sour curd for the best taste.
serving_ideas: sambar and coconut or tomato chutney.
Best time: breakfast; also great for tiffin boxes.
recipes.storage: best eaten the same day; re-steam leftovers for 3 minutes.

recipes.description: A thick brown rice uttapam topped with carrot peas.

steps.title: Prepare the batter
steps.text: Soak the brown rice for 5 hours and the urad dal with methi seeds for 4 hours. Grind separately, mix, add salt and ferment overnight.

steps.title: Thicken
steps.text: Uttapam batter should be thicker than dosa batter; do not thin it.

steps.title: Chop the topping
steps.text: Finely chop the carrot, green peas and coriander leaves and mix them together.

steps.title: Heat the tawa
steps.text: Heat a tawa on medium flame and grease it lightly.

steps.title: Spread
steps.text: Pour a ladle of batter and spread it gently into a thick 5–6 inch round.

steps.title: Add the topping
steps.text: Sprinkle 2 tbsp of the topping evenly and press it in gently with the back of the ladle.

steps.title: Cook covered
steps.text: Drizzle oil around the edges, cover and cook on medium-low flame for 3 minutes until the base is golden.

steps.title: Flip
steps.text: Flip and cook the topping side for 1–2 minutes until lightly browned.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with chutney and sambar.

tips: Cooking covered on low heat makes the uttapam soft and fully cooked inside.
Press the topping into the batter so it does not fall off when flipped.
serving_ideas: coconut chutney, tomato chutney and sambar.
Best time: breakfast or a light dinner.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh.

recipes.description: A brown rice dosa with a peppery mushroom filling.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Wash the brown rice and soak for 5–6 hours. Separately wash and soak the urad dal with the methi seeds for 4–5 hours.

steps.title: Grind
steps.text: Grind the urad dal with ice-cold water until light, fluffy and doubled in volume. Grind the soaked grain to a smooth paste. Mix both with clean hands.

steps.title: Ferment

recipes.description: Green brown rice idlis with spinach.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Wash and soak the brown rice for 5–6 hours. Separately soak the urad dal with methi seeds for 4 hours.

steps.title: Grind the dal
steps.text: Grind the urad dal with ice-cold water, a little at a time, to a light, fluffy, smooth batter.

steps.title: Grind the grain
steps.text: Grind the soaked grain to a slightly coarse, semolina-like batter. Mix both batters well with your hand.

steps.title: Ferment
steps.text: Add salt, cover and leave in a warm place for 8–12 hours until it doubles and smells pleasantly sour.

steps.title: Add flavour
steps.text: Fold the spinach purée into the batter.

steps.title: Prepare the steamer
steps.text: Boil 2 cups water in an idli steamer or pressure cooker (without the whistle). Grease the idli moulds lightly.

steps.title: Fill the moulds
steps.text: Gently stir the batter without knocking out the air and pour into the moulds until three-quarters full.

steps.title: Steam
steps.text: Steam on medium-high flame for 10–12 minutes. A toothpick inserted in the centre should come out clean.

steps.title: Rest & demould
steps.text: Rest for 2 minutes, then scoop out the idlis with a wet spoon and serve hot.

tips: Use a 4:1 ratio of idli rice to urad dal for soft idlis.
Do not over-stir fermented batter; it loses the air that makes idlis fluffy.
serving_ideas: sambar and coconut or tomato chutney.
Best time: breakfast; also great for tiffin boxes.
recipes.storage: batter keeps in the fridge for 3–4 days; steamed idlis keep for 1 day and can be re-steamed.

recipes.description: A wholesome bajra chila with cabbage, quick to make and full of fibre.

steps.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps.text: Finely chop the onion and green chilli and grate the ginger. Small, even pieces keep the chila thin and help it cook evenly.

steps.title: Make the batter
steps.text: In a mixing bowl, combine the bajra, besan and cabbage with turmeric, ajwain, chilli powder and salt. Add water a little at a time and whisk to a smooth, lump-free batter that flows like dosa batter.

steps.title: Add vegetables & rest
steps.text: Fold in the chopped vegetables, ginger and coriander. Rest the batter for 10 minutes so it thickens slightly and the chila turns soft.

steps.title: Heat the pan
steps.text: Heat a non-stick or well-seasoned iron tawa on medium flame and brush it with ¼ tsp oil. A few drops of water should sizzle when the pan is ready.

steps.title: Spread the chila
steps.text: Pour one ladle of batter in the centre and spread it gently in circles into a 6–7 inch round. Drizzle a few drops of oil around the edges.

steps.title: Cook the first side
steps.text: Cook on medium-low flame for 2–3 minutes, until the top looks set and the edges lift easily and turn golden.

steps.title: Flip & cook
steps.text: Flip with a flat spatula and cook the other side for 1–2 minutes, pressing lightly, until golden spots appear.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with mint-coriander chutney or curd. Make the remaining chilas the same way, adding only a few drops of oil each time.

tips: Rest the batter for 10 minutes; it makes the chila softer and easier to flip.
Keep the flame medium-low so the centre cooks before the outside browns.
serving_ideas: mint-coriander chutney, plain curd or raita, and a cucumber-tomato salad.
Best time: breakfast, or an early evening meal.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh. Plain batter (without vegetables) keeps in the fridge in an airtight box for up to 12 hours.

recipes.description: A protein-rich chana dal chila with cabbage, no fermentation needed.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Wash the chana dal 2–3 times and soak in plenty of water for 5 hours. Drain well.

steps.title: Grind the batter
steps.text: Grind the soaked dal with ginger, green chillies and cumin, adding water little by little, to a smooth, thick batter. It should coat the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Add hing and salt and mix in the cabbage and onion. The batter does not need fermentation and can be used right away.

steps.title: Heat the pan
steps.text: Heat a non-stick or iron tawa on medium flame and grease it lightly with oil.

steps.title: Spread the chila
steps.text: Pour a ladle of batter and spread it quickly into a thin round. Drizzle a few drops of oil around the edges.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Cook on medium flame for 2–3 minutes until the base is golden and crisp, then flip and cook the other side for 1 minute.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with green chutney or tomato chutney. Repeat with the remaining batter.

tips: Do not add too much water while grinding; a thick batter gives crisp chilas.
Soaking can be done overnight for a quicker morning.
serving_ideas: mint-coriander chutney, plain curd or raita, and a cucumber-tomato salad.
Best time: breakfast, or an early evening meal.
recipes.storage: Batter keeps in the fridge for up to 24 hours; stir and adjust with a little water before use.

steps.text: Take the moong dal in a bowl; it should be thick, like idli batter.

steps.title: Add the flavourings
steps.text: Mix in the cabbage, onion, green chilli and fruit salt and salt.

steps.text: Heat a paniyaram (appe) pan on medium flame and add a few drops of oil to each cavity.
