recipes.description: A light, peppery drumstick leaf pepper rasam.

steps.title: Prepare the base
steps.text: Soak the tamarind in warm water for 10 minutes and extract the juice.

steps.title: Crush the spices
steps.text: Coarsely crush the pepper, cumin and garlic in a mortar.

steps.title: Boil the base
steps.text: In a pot, add the tamarind water, crushed tomatoes, turmeric, salt, jaggery, curry leaves, the crushed spices and rasam powder along with the moringa and black peppercorns. Boil for 7–8 minutes until the raw smell goes.

steps.title: Add water
steps.text: Add the remaining water. Heat until it turns frothy on top, then switch off. Do not boil it hard after this.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee, crackle mustard seeds, add dry red chillies, curry leaves and hing and pour over the rasam.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Add coriander, cover for 5 minutes, and serve hot with rice or as a soup.

tips: Switch off rasam as soon as it froths up; over-boiling makes it bitter.
Rasam tastes better after resting covered for 10 minutes.
serving_ideas: steamed rice with a little ghee, or sip it hot like a soup.
Best time: lunch or dinner; very soothing during colds.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

recipes.description: A light, peppery ginger lemon rasam.

steps.title: Cook the dal
steps.text: Pressure-cook the moong dal with 2 cups water for 3 whistles and mash; keep the dal water.

steps.title: Crush the spices
steps.text: Coarsely crush the pepper, cumin and garlic in a mortar.

steps.title: Boil the base
steps.text: In a pot, add the tamarind water, crushed tomatoes, turmeric, salt, jaggery, curry leaves, the crushed spices and rasam powder along with the ginger. Boil for 7–8 minutes until the raw smell goes.

steps.title: Add water & dal
steps.text: Add the remaining water and the dal. Heat until it turns frothy on top, then switch off. Do not boil it hard after this.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee, crackle mustard seeds, add dry red chillies, curry leaves and hing and pour over the rasam.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Add coriander, cover for 5 minutes, and serve hot with rice or as a soup.

tips: Switch off rasam as soon as it froths up; over-boiling makes it bitter.
Rasam tastes better after resting covered for 10 minutes.
serving_ideas: steamed rice with a little ghee, or sip it hot like a soup.
Best time: lunch or dinner; very soothing during colds.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

recipes.description: Curd-besan kadhi with gwar.

steps.title: Whisk
steps.text: Whisk the curd with the besan, turmeric, chilli powder and salt until completely smooth. Add the water and whisk again.

steps.title: Start cooking
steps.text: Pour into a heavy pot and bring to a boil on medium flame, stirring continuously so the curd does not split.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Once it boils, lower the flame and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it thickens slightly and the raw besan smell goes.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the gwar phali and simmer until tender.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat oil or ghee, crackle cumin, methi and mustard seeds, add dry red chillies, curry leaves and hing and pour over the kadhi.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with coriander and serve hot.

tips: Use slightly sour curd for the best flavour.
Keep stirring until the kadhi comes to a boil to stop it from curdling.
serving_ideas: steamed rice, jeera rice or khichdi.
Best time: lunch.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

recipes.description: South Indian sambar with kovakkai (ivy gourd).

steps.title: Cook the dal
steps.text: Wash the toor / arhar dal and pressure-cook with water and turmeric for 3–4 whistles until soft. Mash well.

steps.title: Soak the tamarind
steps.text: Soak the tamarind in ½ cup warm water for 10 minutes and squeeze out the pulp.

steps.title: Cook the vegetables
steps.text: In a pot, boil the kundru, onion and tomato with 1¼ cups water and salt for 7–8 minutes until tender but not mushy.

steps.title: Add tamarind & spices
steps.text: Add the tamarind extract, sambar powder and jaggery and simmer for 5 minutes until the raw smell of tamarind goes.

steps.title: Add the dal
steps.text: Add the mashed dal, adjust the consistency with hot water and simmer for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat oil, crackle mustard and methi seeds, add dry red chillies, curry leaves and hing, and pour over the sambar.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with coriander and serve hot.

tips: Simmer the sambar after adding dal; boiling hard makes it lose its aroma.
Freshly ground sambar powder makes a big difference to flavour.
serving_ideas: steamed rice, idli, dosa or vada.
Best time: breakfast, lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2 days. Dal thickens when cold; add hot water while reheating.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee, crackle mustard seeds, add dry red chillies, curry leaves and hing and pour over the rasam.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Add coriander, cover for 5 minutes, and serve hot with rice or as a soup.

tips: Switch off rasam as soon as it froths up; over-boiling makes it bitter.
Rasam tastes better after resting covered for 10 minutes.
serving_ideas: steamed rice with a little ghee, or sip it hot like a soup.
Best time: lunch or dinner; very soothing during colds.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

recipes.description: Toor dal cooked with moringa leaf leaves, rich in iron and folate.

steps.title: Wash & soak
steps.text: Wash the toor / arhar dal 3–4 times until the water runs clear and soak for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Pressure-cook
steps.text: Cook the dal with the water, turmeric and salt for 3–4 whistles on medium flame, until completely soft. Let the pressure release naturally.

steps.title: Mash
steps.text: Open the cooker and whisk the dal lightly until creamy. Add hot water to get the consistency you like and simmer for 3–4 minutes.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the moringa leaf leaves to the cooked dal and simmer for 4–5 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare the tadka
steps.text: Heat oil, crackle mustard seeds and cumin, then add dry red chillies, curry leaves, crushed garlic and hing.

steps.title: Temper the dal
steps.text: Pour the sizzling tadka over the dal and cover immediately for 1 minute to trap the aroma.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with coriander and serve hot.

tips: Soaking dal makes it cook faster and easier to digest.
Add the tadka just before serving for the best aroma.
serving_ideas: phulka, jeera rice or brown rice, with a salad.
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2 days. Dal thickens when cold; add hot water while reheating.

steps.title: Prepare the base
steps.text: Soak the tamarind in warm water for 10 minutes and extract the juice.

steps.title: Crush the spices
steps.text: Coarsely crush the pepper, cumin and garlic in a mortar.

steps.title: Boil the base
steps.text: In a pot, add the tamarind water, crushed tomatoes, turmeric, salt, jaggery, curry leaves, the crushed spices and rasam powder along with the garlic and black peppercorns. Boil for 7–8 minutes until the raw smell goes.

steps.title: Add water

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee, crackle mustard seeds, add dry red chillies, curry leaves and hing and pour over the rasam.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Add coriander, cover for 5 minutes, and serve hot with rice or as a soup.

tips: Switch off rasam as soon as it froths up; over-boiling makes it bitter.
Rasam tastes better after resting covered for 10 minutes.
serving_ideas: steamed rice with a little ghee, or sip it hot like a soup.
Best time: lunch or dinner; very soothing during colds.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

steps.title: Boil the base
steps.text: In a pot, add the tamarind water, crushed tomatoes, turmeric, salt, jaggery, curry leaves, the crushed spices and rasam powder along with the pomegranate seeds. Boil for 7–8 minutes until the raw smell goes.

steps.title: Add water & dal

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee, crackle mustard seeds, add dry red chillies, curry leaves and hing and pour over the rasam.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Add coriander, cover for 5 minutes, and serve hot with rice or as a soup.

tips: Switch off rasam as soon as it froths up; over-boiling makes it bitter.
Rasam tastes better after resting covered for 10 minutes.
serving_ideas: steamed rice with a little ghee, or sip it hot like a soup.

recipes.description: South Indian sambar with pumpkin brinjal.

steps.title: Cook the dal
steps.text: Wash the toor / arhar dal and pressure-cook with water and turmeric for 3–4 whistles until soft. Mash well.

steps.title: Soak the tamarind
steps.text: Soak the tamarind in ½ cup warm water for 10 minutes and squeeze out the pulp.

steps.title: Cook the vegetables
steps.text: In a pot, boil the pumpkin, brinjal, onion and tomato with 1¼ cups water and salt for 7–8 minutes until tender but not mushy.

steps.title: Add tamarind & spices
steps.text: Add the tamarind extract, sambar powder and jaggery and simmer for 5 minutes until the raw smell of tamarind goes.

steps.title: Add the dal
steps.text: Add the mashed dal, adjust the consistency with hot water and simmer for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat oil, crackle mustard and methi seeds, add dry red chillies, curry leaves and hing, and pour over the sambar.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with coriander and serve hot.

tips: Simmer the sambar after adding dal; boiling hard makes it lose its aroma.
Freshly ground sambar powder makes a big difference to flavour.
serving_ideas: steamed rice, idli, dosa or vada.
Best time: breakfast, lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2 days. Dal thickens when cold; add hot water while reheating.

steps.title: Mash
steps.text: Open the cooker and whisk the dal lightly until creamy. Add hot water to get the consistency you like and simmer for 3–4 minutes.

recipes.description: Curd-besan kadhi with sweet potato.

steps.title: Whisk
steps.text: Whisk the curd with the besan, turmeric, chilli powder and salt until completely smooth. Add the water and whisk again.

steps.title: Start cooking
steps.text: Pour into a heavy pot and bring to a boil on medium flame, stirring continuously so the curd does not split.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Once it boils, lower the flame and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it thickens slightly and the raw besan smell goes.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the sweet potato and simmer until tender.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat oil or ghee, crackle cumin, methi and mustard seeds, add dry red chillies, curry leaves and hing and pour over the kadhi.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with coriander and serve hot.

tips: Use slightly sour curd for the best flavour.
Keep stirring until the kadhi comes to a boil to stop it from curdling.
serving_ideas: steamed rice, jeera rice or khichdi.
Best time: lunch.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

recipes.description: A light, peppery thakkali milagu rasam.

steps.title: Prepare the base
steps.text: Soak the tamarind in warm water for 10 minutes and extract the juice.

steps.title: Crush the spices
steps.text: Coarsely crush the pepper, cumin and garlic in a mortar.

steps.title: Boil the base
steps.text: In a pot, add the tamarind water, crushed tomatoes, turmeric, salt, jaggery, curry leaves, the crushed spices and rasam powder along with the black peppercorns. Boil for 7–8 minutes until the raw smell goes.

steps.title: Add water
steps.text: Add the remaining water. Heat until it turns frothy on top, then switch off. Do not boil it hard after this.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee, crackle mustard seeds, add dry red chillies, curry leaves and hing and pour over the rasam.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Add coriander, cover for 5 minutes, and serve hot with rice or as a soup.

tips: Switch off rasam as soon as it froths up; over-boiling makes it bitter.
Rasam tastes better after resting covered for 10 minutes.
serving_ideas: steamed rice with a little ghee, or sip it hot like a soup.
Best time: lunch or dinner; very soothing during colds.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

recipes.description: Chole cooked with baingan in a homestyle masala.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Wash the kabuli chana well and soak in plenty of water for 8 hours or overnight.

steps.title: Pressure-cook
steps.text: Drain, add fresh water and salt and pressure-cook for 5–6 whistles until soft enough to mash between your fingers. Keep the cooking water.

steps.title: Make the masala
steps.text: Heat oil, add cumin and bay leaf. Add onion and sauté on medium flame for 8–10 minutes until deep golden. Add ginger, garlic and green chilli and cook 1 minute. Add the tomato purée and powdered spices and cook until the masala thickens and oil separates (6–8 minutes).

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the brinjal and cook covered 8 minutes.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Add the cooked kabuli chana with enough cooking water to make a gravy. Mash a few pieces against the side of the pan to thicken it.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Cover and simmer on low flame for 15 minutes so the kabuli chana absorb the masala.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Add the coriander leaves and lemon juice, check the salt and serve hot.

tips: Brown the onions slowly; this gives the gravy its depth without cream.
Use the legume cooking water in the gravy; it holds flavour and nutrients.
serving_ideas: steamed rice, jeera rice, phulka or bhakri, with onion-cucumber salad.
Best time: lunch.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2–3 days and tastes even better the next day. Freezes well for a month.

steps.text: Drain, add fresh water and salt and pressure-cook for 3 whistles until soft enough to mash between your fingers. Keep the cooking water.

steps.title: Make the masala
steps.text: Heat oil, add cumin and bay leaf. Add onion and sauté on medium flame for 8–10 minutes until deep golden. Add ginger, garlic and green chilli and cook 1 minute. Add the tomato purée and powdered spices and cook until the masala thickens and oil separates (6–8 minutes).

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the methi and cook 4 minutes.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Add the cooked lobia with enough cooking water to make a gravy. Mash a few pieces against the side of the pan to thicken it.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Cover and simmer on low flame for 15 minutes so the lobia absorb the masala.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Add the coriander leaves and lemon juice, check the salt and serve hot.

tips: Brown the onions slowly; this gives the gravy its depth without cream.
Use the legume cooking water in the gravy; it holds flavour and nutrients.
serving_ideas: steamed rice, jeera rice, phulka or bhakri, with onion-cucumber salad.
Best time: lunch.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2–3 days and tastes even better the next day. Freezes well for a month.

recipes.description: Arbi cooked with tangy pickle spices and mustard oil.

steps.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps.text: Wash, peel if needed and cut the arbi into even, bite-sized pieces so they cook evenly.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat mustard oil until it smokes lightly, lower the flame and add fennel, kalonji, methi and mustard seeds (the pickle spices), then hing and green chilli.

steps.title: Add the spices
steps.text: Lower the flame and add the turmeric and powdered spices with 1 tbsp water so they do not burn. Stir for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the arbi and salt and toss well to coat with the masala.

steps.title: Cook covered
steps.text: Cover and cook on low flame for 8 minutes, stirring every few minutes. Sprinkle a little water only if it starts to stick.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Uncover, raise the flame for 1 minute to dry any moisture, then add the coriander leaves and mix gently.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with phulka, paratha or dal-rice.

tips: Cut vegetables to the same size so they cook evenly.
Cook on low heat with the lid on; the vegetables steam in their own moisture and need very little oil.
serving_ideas: phulka, paratha or bhakri, with dal and curd.
Best time: lunch or dinner; also great in tiffin boxes.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1–2 days.

recipes.description: Kachcha Kela tossed with cumin, ginger and green chilli, simple and light.

steps.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps.text: Wash, peel if needed and cut the raw banana into even, bite-sized pieces so they cook evenly.

steps.text: Heat oil in a kadhai, crackle the cumin, then add hing, green chilli and ginger and sauté for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Add the spices
steps.text: Lower the flame and add the turmeric and powdered spices with 1 tbsp water so they do not burn. Stir for 30 seconds.

recipes.description: Chana in a tangy gravy flavoured with pickle spices and mustard oil.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Wash and cut the kabuli chana into bite-sized pieces.

steps.title: Make the gravy
steps.text: Heat mustard oil until it smokes lightly, lower the flame and add the pickle spices (fennel, kalonji, methi, mustard). Sauté the onion until golden, add ginger, garlic and tomato and cook until thick. Lower the flame and stir in the whisked curd.

steps.title: Adjust
steps.text: Add water as needed for a medium-thick gravy, add salt and bring to a gentle boil.

steps.title: Add the main ingredients
steps.text: Add the kabuli chana and stir gently to coat with the gravy.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Cover and simmer on low flame for 8 minutes until everything is cooked and the flavours blend.

steps.title: Finish & serve
steps.text: Add the coriander leaves and serve hot.

tips: Cook the masala until oil separates; this removes the raw taste and gives a rich gravy with less fat.
Add paneer or soft vegetables at the end so they stay soft and hold their shape.
serving_ideas: phulka, multigrain roti, jeera rice or brown rice.
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2 days. Reheat gently, adding a splash of water.

recipes.description: A one-pot khichdi of barnyard and green moong dal.

steps.title: Wash & soak
steps.text: Wash the barnyard millet and whole green moong together until the water runs clear and soak for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee in a pressure cooker, crackle the cumin, add hing, ginger and green chilli.

steps.title: Add vegetables
steps.text: Add the carrot, green peas and tomato and sauté for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Add grains & water
steps.text: Add the drained grains, turmeric, salt and 720 ml water. Stir well.

steps.title: Pressure-cook
steps.text: Cook for 3–4 whistles on medium flame. Let the pressure release naturally.

steps.title: Adjust
steps.text: Open, mash lightly and add hot water if you like a softer, porridge-like consistency.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with a spoon of ghee, curd and roasted papad.

tips: A softer, mushier khichdi is easier to digest when you are unwell.
Add a little extra ghee on top just before serving for aroma.
serving_ideas: curd, kadhi or raita, roasted papad and a pickle (in moderation).
Best time: dinner; ideal when unwell.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh; keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

recipes.description: Barnyard Millet pulao with beetroot and whole spices.

steps.title: Rinse & soak
steps.text: Wash the barnyard millet 3–4 times until the water runs clear and soak for 30 minutes. Drain.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee and oil in a heavy pot or cooker. Add the whole spices and fry for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the onion and sauté until light golden, then ginger, garlic and green chilli.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the beetroot and sauté for 2–3 minutes.

steps.title: Add the barnyard millet
steps.text: Add the drained grain and stir gently for 1–2 minutes to coat it with ghee.

steps.title: Add water
steps.text: Add 440 ml hot water and salt; taste the water, it should be slightly salty.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Cover and cook on the lowest flame for 12–15 minutes (or 1 whistle in a pressure cooker) until the water is absorbed and the grains are tender.

steps.title: Rest & fluff
steps.text: Rest covered for 5–10 minutes, then fluff gently with a fork. Garnish and serve.

tips: Rest the rice for 5 minutes after cooking; the grains firm up and stay separate.
Use a heavy-bottomed pot and the lowest flame so the bottom does not burn.
serving_ideas: raita, a green salad and papad (roasted).
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day. Reheat with a sprinkle of water.

recipes.description: A one-pot khichdi of barnyard and toor dal.

steps.title: Wash & soak
steps.text: Wash the barnyard millet and toor / arhar dal together until the water runs clear and soak for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee in a pressure cooker, crackle the cumin, add hing, ginger and green chilli.

steps.title: Add vegetables
steps.text: Add the carrot, green peas and tomato and sauté for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Add grains & water
steps.text: Add the drained grains, turmeric, salt and 720 ml water. Stir well.

steps.title: Pressure-cook
steps.text: Cook for 3–4 whistles on medium flame. Let the pressure release naturally.

steps.title: Adjust
steps.text: Open, mash lightly and add hot water if you like a softer, porridge-like consistency.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with a spoon of ghee, curd and roasted papad.

tips: A softer, mushier khichdi is easier to digest when you are unwell.
Add a little extra ghee on top just before serving for aroma.
serving_ideas: curd, kadhi or raita, roasted papad and a pickle (in moderation).
Best time: dinner; ideal when unwell.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh; keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the soya chunks and green peas and sauté for 2–3 minutes.

steps.title: Add the basmati rice
steps.text: Add the drained grain and stir gently for 1–2 minutes to coat it with ghee.

steps.title: Add water
steps.text: Add 400 ml hot water and salt; taste the water, it should be slightly salty.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Cover and cook on the lowest flame for 12–15 minutes (or 1 whistle in a pressure cooker) until the water is absorbed and the grains are tender.

steps.title: Rest & fluff
steps.text: Rest covered for 5–10 minutes, then fluff gently with a fork. Garnish and serve.

tips: Rest the rice for 5 minutes after cooking; the grains firm up and stay separate.
Use a heavy-bottomed pot and the lowest flame so the bottom does not burn.
serving_ideas: raita, a green salad and papad (roasted).
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day. Reheat with a sprinkle of water.

recipes.description: A one-pot khichdi of brown rice and green moong dal.

steps.title: Wash & soak
steps.text: Wash the brown rice and whole green moong together until the water runs clear and soak for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee in a pressure cooker, crackle the cumin, add hing, ginger and green chilli.

steps.title: Add vegetables
steps.text: Add the carrot, green peas and tomato and sauté for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Add grains & water
steps.text: Add the drained grains, turmeric, salt and 720 ml water. Stir well.

steps.title: Pressure-cook
steps.text: Cook for 3–4 whistles on medium flame. Let the pressure release naturally.

steps.title: Adjust
steps.text: Open, mash lightly and add hot water if you like a softer, porridge-like consistency.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with a spoon of ghee, curd and roasted papad.

tips: A softer, mushier khichdi is easier to digest when you are unwell.
Add a little extra ghee on top just before serving for aroma.
serving_ideas: curd, kadhi or raita, roasted papad and a pickle (in moderation).
Best time: dinner; ideal when unwell.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh; keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

recipes.description: Barnyard Millet flavoured South Indian coconut-rice style.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: Wash and cook the barnyard millet with water and salt until each grain is soft but separate. Spread on a plate to cool completely.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat the oil and crackle the mustard seeds, then add the urad dal, chana dal, dry red chillies, curry leaves, hing and peanuts and fry until the dals and nuts turn golden.

steps.title: Toast the coconut
steps.text: Sauté the coconut for 2 minutes until fragrant.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Add the cooled rice and gently fold everything together without mashing the grains.

steps.title: Rest & serve
steps.text: Rest for 10 minutes so the flavours soak in. Garnish and serve warm or at room temperature.

tips: Use cooled, day-old or fully cooled rice so the grains stay separate.
serving_ideas: curd or raita, a poriyal and roasted papad.
Best time: lunch and lunch boxes; ideal for travel.
recipes.storage: keeps for 6–8 hours at room temperature (great for travel) or 1 day in the fridge.

recipes.description: Fragrant layered biryani with corn paneer.

steps.title: Soak the rice
steps.text: Wash the basmati rice gently 3–4 times and soak for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Mix the sweet corn kernels and paneer with the marinade ingredients and rest for at least 30 minutes.

steps.title: Caramelise the onions
steps.text: Heat oil and half the ghee in a heavy pot and fry the sliced onions on medium flame, stirring, until deep golden (12–15 minutes). Remove half for layering.

steps.title: Cook the base
steps.text: Add the marinated sweet corn kernels and paneer to the remaining onions and cook on medium flame until almost done and the masala is thick.

steps.title: Par-boil the rice
steps.text: Boil the water with salt and whole spices. Add the drained rice and cook for 5–6 minutes until 70% done (the grain should still have a bite). Drain.

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: Spread the rice over the base. Top with fried onions, mint, coriander, garam masala, saffron soaked in warm milk and the remaining ghee.

steps.title: Dum
steps.text: Cover tightly (seal with foil or dough) and cook on the lowest flame for 15 minutes, or place the pot on a hot tawa.

steps.title: Rest & serve
steps.text: Rest for 10 minutes, then gently mix from the side and serve with raita.

tips: Par-boil the rice only 70%; it finishes cooking on dum.
Use a heavy pot or place it on a tawa so the bottom layer does not burn.
serving_ideas: onion-cucumber raita and a fresh salad.
Best time: lunch or festive meals.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1–2 days; sprinkle water and reheat covered.

steps.text: Heat the oil and crackle the mustard seeds, then add the urad dal, chana dal, dry red chillies, curry leaves, hing and peanuts and fry until the dals and nuts turn golden.

steps.title: Mash
steps.text: Mix the cooled grain with curd, milk and salt.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Add the cooled rice and gently fold everything together without mashing the grains.

steps.title: Rest & serve
steps.text: Rest for 10 minutes so the flavours soak in. Garnish and serve warm or at room temperature.

tips: Use cooled, day-old or fully cooled rice so the grains stay separate.
serving_ideas: curd or raita, a poriyal and roasted papad.
Best time: lunch and lunch boxes; ideal for travel.
recipes.storage: keeps for 6–8 hours at room temperature (great for travel) or 1 day in the fridge.

recipes.description: A one-pot khichdi of foxtail and green moong dal.

steps.title: Wash & soak
steps.text: Wash the foxtail millet and whole green moong together until the water runs clear and soak for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee in a pressure cooker, crackle the cumin, add hing, ginger and green chilli.

steps.title: Add vegetables
steps.text: Add the carrot, green peas and tomato and sauté for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Add grains & water
steps.text: Add the drained grains, turmeric, salt and 720 ml water. Stir well.

steps.title: Pressure-cook
steps.text: Cook for 3–4 whistles on medium flame. Let the pressure release naturally.

steps.title: Adjust
steps.text: Open, mash lightly and add hot water if you like a softer, porridge-like consistency.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with a spoon of ghee, curd and roasted papad.

tips: A softer, mushier khichdi is easier to digest when you are unwell.
Add a little extra ghee on top just before serving for aroma.
serving_ideas: curd, kadhi or raita, roasted papad and a pickle (in moderation).
Best time: dinner; ideal when unwell.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh; keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

recipes.description: Foxtail Millet pulao with beetroot and whole spices.

steps.title: Rinse & soak
steps.text: Wash the foxtail millet 3–4 times until the water runs clear and soak for 30 minutes. Drain.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee and oil in a heavy pot or cooker. Add the whole spices and fry for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the onion and sauté until light golden, then ginger, garlic and green chilli.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the beetroot and sauté for 2–3 minutes.

steps.title: Add the foxtail millet
steps.text: Add the drained grain and stir gently for 1–2 minutes to coat it with ghee.

steps.title: Add water
steps.text: Add 440 ml hot water and salt; taste the water, it should be slightly salty.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Cover and cook on the lowest flame for 12–15 minutes (or 1 whistle in a pressure cooker) until the water is absorbed and the grains are tender.

steps.title: Rest & fluff
steps.text: Rest covered for 5–10 minutes, then fluff gently with a fork. Garnish and serve.

tips: Rest the rice for 5 minutes after cooking; the grains firm up and stay separate.
Use a heavy-bottomed pot and the lowest flame so the bottom does not burn.
serving_ideas: raita, a green salad and papad (roasted).
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day. Reheat with a sprinkle of water.

recipes.description: Fragrant layered biryani with kala chana.

steps.title: Soak the rice
steps.text: Wash the basmati rice gently 3–4 times and soak for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Mix the kala chana with the marinade ingredients and rest for at least 30 minutes.

steps.title: Caramelise the onions
steps.text: Heat oil and half the ghee in a heavy pot and fry the sliced onions on medium flame, stirring, until deep golden (12–15 minutes). Remove half for layering.

steps.title: Cook the base
steps.text: Add the marinated kala chana to the remaining onions and cook on medium flame until almost done and the masala is thick.

steps.title: Par-boil the rice
steps.text: Boil the water with salt and whole spices. Add the drained rice and cook for 5–6 minutes until 70% done (the grain should still have a bite). Drain.

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: Spread the rice over the base. Top with fried onions, mint, coriander, garam masala, saffron soaked in warm milk and the remaining ghee.

steps.title: Dum
steps.text: Cover tightly (seal with foil or dough) and cook on the lowest flame for 15 minutes, or place the pot on a hot tawa.

steps.title: Rest & serve
steps.text: Rest for 10 minutes, then gently mix from the side and serve with raita.

tips: Par-boil the rice only 70%; it finishes cooking on dum.
Use a heavy pot or place it on a tawa so the bottom layer does not burn.
serving_ideas: onion-cucumber raita and a fresh salad.
Best time: lunch or festive meals.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1–2 days; sprinkle water and reheat covered.

recipes.description: A one-pot khichdi of kodo and green moong dal.

steps.title: Wash & soak
steps.text: Wash the kodo millet and whole green moong together until the water runs clear and soak for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee in a pressure cooker, crackle the cumin, add hing, ginger and green chilli.

steps.title: Add vegetables
steps.text: Add the carrot, green peas and tomato and sauté for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Add grains & water
steps.text: Add the drained grains, turmeric, salt and 720 ml water. Stir well.

steps.title: Pressure-cook
steps.text: Cook for 3–4 whistles on medium flame. Let the pressure release naturally.

steps.title: Adjust
steps.text: Open, mash lightly and add hot water if you like a softer, porridge-like consistency.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with a spoon of ghee, curd and roasted papad.

tips: A softer, mushier khichdi is easier to digest when you are unwell.
Add a little extra ghee on top just before serving for aroma.
serving_ideas: curd, kadhi or raita, roasted papad and a pickle (in moderation).
Best time: dinner; ideal when unwell.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh; keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

recipes.description: Kodo Millet pulao with beetroot and whole spices.

steps.title: Rinse & soak
steps.text: Wash the kodo millet 3–4 times until the water runs clear and soak for 30 minutes. Drain.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee and oil in a heavy pot or cooker. Add the whole spices and fry for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the onion and sauté until light golden, then ginger, garlic and green chilli.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the beetroot and sauté for 2–3 minutes.

steps.title: Add the kodo millet
steps.text: Add the drained grain and stir gently for 1–2 minutes to coat it with ghee.

steps.title: Add water
steps.text: Add 440 ml hot water and salt; taste the water, it should be slightly salty.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Cover and cook on the lowest flame for 12–15 minutes (or 1 whistle in a pressure cooker) until the water is absorbed and the grains are tender.

steps.title: Rest & fluff
steps.text: Rest covered for 5–10 minutes, then fluff gently with a fork. Garnish and serve.

tips: Rest the rice for 5 minutes after cooking; the grains firm up and stay separate.
Use a heavy-bottomed pot and the lowest flame so the bottom does not burn.
serving_ideas: raita, a green salad and papad (roasted).
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day. Reheat with a sprinkle of water.

recipes.description: Barnyard Millet flavoured South Indian lemon-rice style.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: Wash and cook the barnyard millet with water and salt until each grain is soft but separate. Spread on a plate to cool completely.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat the oil and crackle the mustard seeds, then add the urad dal, chana dal, dry red chillies, curry leaves, hing and peanuts and fry until the dals and nuts turn golden.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Add ginger, chilli and turmeric; switch off and add the lemon juice.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Add the cooled rice and gently fold everything together without mashing the grains.

steps.title: Rest & serve
steps.text: Rest for 10 minutes so the flavours soak in. Garnish and serve warm or at room temperature.

tips: Use cooled, day-old or fully cooled rice so the grains stay separate.
serving_ideas: curd or raita, a poriyal and roasted papad.
Best time: lunch and lunch boxes; ideal for travel.
recipes.storage: keeps for 6–8 hours at room temperature (great for travel) or 1 day in the fridge.

recipes.description: Little Millet pulao with chana and whole spices.

steps.title: Rinse & soak
steps.text: Wash the little millet 3–4 times until the water runs clear and soak for 30 minutes. Drain.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee and oil in a heavy pot or cooker. Add the whole spices and fry for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the onion and sauté until light golden, then ginger, garlic and green chilli.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the kabuli chana and sauté for 2–3 minutes.

steps.title: Add the little millet
steps.text: Add the drained grain and stir gently for 1–2 minutes to coat it with ghee.

steps.title: Add water
steps.text: Add 440 ml hot water and salt; taste the water, it should be slightly salty.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Cover and cook on the lowest flame for 12–15 minutes (or 1 whistle in a pressure cooker) until the water is absorbed and the grains are tender.

steps.title: Rest & fluff
steps.text: Rest covered for 5–10 minutes, then fluff gently with a fork. Garnish and serve.

tips: Rest the rice for 5 minutes after cooking; the grains firm up and stay separate.
Use a heavy-bottomed pot and the lowest flame so the bottom does not burn.
serving_ideas: raita, a green salad and papad (roasted).
Best time: lunch or dinner.

steps.text: Heat ghee in a pressure cooker, crackle the cumin, add hing, ginger and green chilli.

steps.text: Cook for 3–4 whistles on medium flame. Let the pressure release naturally.

steps.text: Open, mash lightly and add hot water if you like a softer, porridge-like consistency.

steps.text: Serve hot with a spoon of ghee, curd and roasted papad.

tips: A softer, mushier khichdi is easier to digest when you are unwell.
Add a little extra ghee on top just before serving for aroma.
serving_ideas: curd, kadhi or raita, roasted papad and a pickle (in moderation).
Best time: dinner; ideal when unwell.

recipes.description: Fragrant layered biryani with lobia.

steps.title: Soak the rice
steps.text: Wash the basmati rice gently 3–4 times and soak for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Mix the lobia with the marinade ingredients and rest for at least 30 minutes.

steps.title: Caramelise the onions
steps.text: Heat oil and half the ghee in a heavy pot and fry the sliced onions on medium flame, stirring, until deep golden (12–15 minutes). Remove half for layering.

steps.title: Cook the base
steps.text: Add the marinated lobia to the remaining onions and cook on medium flame until almost done and the masala is thick.

steps.title: Par-boil the rice
steps.text: Boil the water with salt and whole spices. Add the drained rice and cook for 5–6 minutes until 70% done (the grain should still have a bite). Drain.

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: Spread the rice over the base. Top with fried onions, mint, coriander, garam masala, saffron soaked in warm milk and the remaining ghee.

steps.title: Dum
steps.text: Cover tightly (seal with foil or dough) and cook on the lowest flame for 15 minutes, or place the pot on a hot tawa.

steps.title: Rest & serve
steps.text: Rest for 10 minutes, then gently mix from the side and serve with raita.

tips: Par-boil the rice only 70%; it finishes cooking on dum.
Use a heavy pot or place it on a tawa so the bottom layer does not burn.
serving_ideas: onion-cucumber raita and a fresh salad.
Best time: lunch or festive meals.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1–2 days; sprinkle water and reheat covered.

recipes.description: A one-pot khichdi of quinoa and toor dal.

steps.title: Wash & soak
steps.text: Wash the quinoa and toor / arhar dal together until the water runs clear and soak for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee in a pressure cooker, crackle the cumin, add hing, ginger and green chilli.

steps.title: Add vegetables
steps.text: Add the carrot, green peas and tomato and sauté for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Add grains & water
steps.text: Add the drained grains, turmeric, salt and 720 ml water. Stir well.

steps.title: Pressure-cook
steps.text: Cook for 3–4 whistles on medium flame. Let the pressure release naturally.

steps.title: Adjust
steps.text: Open, mash lightly and add hot water if you like a softer, porridge-like consistency.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with a spoon of ghee, curd and roasted papad.

tips: A softer, mushier khichdi is easier to digest when you are unwell.
Add a little extra ghee on top just before serving for aroma.
serving_ideas: curd, kadhi or raita, roasted papad and a pickle (in moderation).
Best time: dinner; ideal when unwell.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh; keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

recipes.description: Fragrant layered biryani with soya chunks.

steps.title: Soak the rice
steps.text: Wash the basmati rice gently 3–4 times and soak for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Mix the soya chunks and potato with the marinade ingredients and rest for at least 30 minutes.

steps.title: Caramelise the onions
steps.text: Heat oil and half the ghee in a heavy pot and fry the sliced onions on medium flame, stirring, until deep golden (12–15 minutes). Remove half for layering.

steps.title: Cook the base
steps.text: Add the marinated soya chunks and potato to the remaining onions and cook on medium flame until almost done and the masala is thick.

steps.title: Par-boil the rice
steps.text: Boil the water with salt and whole spices. Add the drained rice and cook for 5–6 minutes until 70% done (the grain should still have a bite). Drain.

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: Spread the rice over the base. Top with fried onions, mint, coriander, garam masala, saffron soaked in warm milk and the remaining ghee.

steps.title: Dum
steps.text: Cover tightly (seal with foil or dough) and cook on the lowest flame for 15 minutes, or place the pot on a hot tawa.

steps.title: Rest & serve
steps.text: Rest for 10 minutes, then gently mix from the side and serve with raita.

tips: Par-boil the rice only 70%; it finishes cooking on dum.
Use a heavy pot or place it on a tawa so the bottom layer does not burn.
serving_ideas: onion-cucumber raita and a fresh salad.
Best time: lunch or festive meals.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1–2 days; sprinkle water and reheat covered.

recipes.description: Barnyard Millet flavoured South Indian tamarind-rice style.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: Wash and cook the barnyard millet with water and salt until each grain is soft but separate. Spread on a plate to cool completely.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat the oil and crackle the mustard seeds, then add the urad dal, chana dal, dry red chillies, curry leaves, hing and peanuts and fry until the dals and nuts turn golden.

steps.title: Make the paste
steps.text: Simmer tamarind, jaggery and puliyogare powder until thick.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Add the cooled rice and gently fold everything together without mashing the grains.

steps.title: Rest & serve
steps.text: Rest for 10 minutes so the flavours soak in. Garnish and serve warm or at room temperature.

tips: Use cooled, day-old or fully cooled rice so the grains stay separate.
serving_ideas: curd or raita, a poriyal and roasted papad.
Best time: lunch and lunch boxes; ideal for travel.
recipes.storage: keeps for 6–8 hours at room temperature (great for travel) or 1 day in the fridge.

recipes.description: A cooling raita with beetroot mint.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Wash and finely chop or grate the beetroot and mint leaves.

steps.title: Whisk the curd
steps.text: Whisk the chilled curd until smooth. Add a few tablespoons of water or milk if it is very thick.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Fold in the beetroot and mint leaves.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Add roasted cumin powder, chilli powder and salt and mix.

steps.title: Chill & serve
steps.text: Refrigerate for 15 minutes and serve cold.

tips: Add salt just before serving to keep the raita from turning watery.
Use fresh, set curd for a thick raita.
serving_ideas: pulao, biryani, paratha or khichdi.
Raita adds probiotics and protein to any meal.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

recipes.description: A warming, wholesome beetroot tomato soup.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Wash and roughly chop the beetroot and tomato.

steps.title: Sauté
steps.text: Heat oil in a pot and sauté the garlic, ginger and onion for 2–3 minutes until soft and fragrant.

steps.title: Add vegetables
steps.text: Add the beetroot and tomato and sauté for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Add the water and salt, bring to a boil and simmer covered for 15 minutes until soft.

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: Cool slightly and blend until smooth. Strain if you like a silky soup.

steps.title: Reheat
steps.text: Return to the pot, adjust the thickness with hot water and bring to a gentle boil.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Add pepper and check the salt.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Pour into bowls, garnish with the coriander leaves and lemon juice and serve hot.

tips: Thicken soups with a little blended potato, oats or dal instead of cornflour or cream.
Add lemon juice only after switching off the heat.
serving_ideas: a slice of whole-wheat toast or a small salad.
Best time: as a starter or a light dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2 days; can be frozen for 1 month (without cream).

recipes.description: Achari Mushroom Tikka, grilled in an oven, air fryer or grill pan.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Cut the mushrooms, capsicum and onion into even 1½-inch pieces.

steps.title: Make the marinade
steps.text: Whisk hung curd with roasted besan, ginger-garlic, spices, lemon juice, mustard oil and salt into a thick paste.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Coat everything well and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes (up to 4 hours).

steps.title: Skewer
steps.text: Thread onto skewers (soak wooden ones in water for 20 minutes first), alternating with capsicum and onion.

steps.title: Grill

recipes.description: Air-fried Baby Corn Pakora with very little oil.

recipes.description: Pan-roasted beetroot paneer tikkis, crisp outside and soft inside.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Boil, steam or chop the beetroot, paneer, green chilli, ginger and coriander leaves as listed and let them cool.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Combine everything in a bowl and mash well. The mixture should hold its shape when pressed; add a little more rolled oats if it is too soft.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Grease your palms and shape into 8 round, flat tikkis about ½ inch thick.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Refrigerate for 15 minutes so they hold firm while cooking.

steps.title: Pan-roast
steps.text: Heat a non-stick tawa, brush with oil and cook the tikkis on medium flame for 3–4 minutes per side until golden and crisp.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with green chutney or hung curd dip.

tips: Chilling the tikkis before cooking stops them from breaking.
Use a non-stick pan and a light brush of oil; there is no need to deep-fry.
serving_ideas: green chutney or hung curd dip, and a cup of tea or buttermilk.
Best time: evening snack or a starter.
Stuff in a whole-wheat wrap with salad for a quick meal.
recipes.storage: uncooked tikkis keep in the fridge for 1 day or can be frozen for 1 month.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat coconut oil, crackle mustard seeds, add urad dal, dry red chillies, curry leaves, hing, green chilli and ginger.

steps.text: Add the cooked kala chana and sweet corn kernels and salt and toss for 2 minutes.

steps.text: Switch off, add the grated coconut, lemon juice and coriander and mix.

steps.text: Boil, steam or chop the moong dal, methi, green chilli, ginger and coriander leaves as listed and let them cool.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Combine everything in a bowl and mash well. The mixture should hold its shape when pressed; add a little more rice flour if it is too soft.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Grease your palms and shape into 8 round, flat tikkis about ½ inch thick.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Refrigerate for 15 minutes so they hold firm while cooking.

steps.title: Pan-roast
steps.text: Heat a non-stick tawa, brush with oil and cook the tikkis on medium flame for 3–4 minutes per side until golden and crisp.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with green chutney or hung curd dip.

tips: Chilling the tikkis before cooking stops them from breaking.
Use a non-stick pan and a light brush of oil; there is no need to deep-fry.
serving_ideas: green chutney or hung curd dip, and a cup of tea or buttermilk.
Best time: evening snack or a starter.
Stuff in a whole-wheat wrap with salad for a quick meal.
recipes.storage: uncooked tikkis keep in the fridge for 1 day or can be frozen for 1 month.

recipes.description: Soft, steamed methi rava dhokla, light and high in protein.

steps.title: Make the batter
steps.text: Mix the rava / suji, curd, methi and ginger and salt with enough water to make a smooth, thick, pourable batter.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Cover and rest the batter for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare the steamer
steps.text: Boil water in a steamer or large pot with a stand. Grease a 7-inch tin or plate with oil.

steps.title: Add the leavening
steps.text: Just before steaming, add the fruit salt with 1 tsp water and stir gently in one direction until frothy.

steps.title: Steam
steps.text: Pour into the greased tin immediately and steam on medium-high flame for 15 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the centre comes out clean.

steps.title: Cool & cut
steps.text: Rest for 5 minutes, then cut into squares or diamonds.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat oil, crackle the mustard seeds and sesame, add curry leaves, green chillies and hing. Add water and lemon juice and pour evenly over the pieces.

steps.title: Garnish & serve
steps.text: Sprinkle with coriander and coconut and serve.

tips: Do not open the steamer for the first 10 minutes; the batter can collapse.
Pour the tempering water slowly so the pieces stay soft and moist.
serving_ideas: green chutney or hung curd dip, and a cup of tea or buttermilk.
Best time: evening snack or a starter.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day; best at room temperature.

recipes.description: A tangy, protein-rich moong sprouts corn chaat.

steps.title: Prepare the base
steps.text: Keep the moong sprouts and sweet corn kernels ready (cooked and cooled where needed).

steps.title: Chop the toppings
steps.text: Finely chop the onion, tomato, coriander leaves and green chilli.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: In a bowl, combine the base and toppings.

steps.title: Dress
steps.text: Add lemon juice, chaat masala, roasted cumin, chilli powder and salt. Toss well.

steps.text: Serve immediately so it stays crunchy.

tips: Mix chaat just before eating; it turns soggy if it waits.

recipes.description: Mushroom Hariyali Tikka, grilled in an oven, air fryer or grill pan.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Cut the mushrooms, capsicum and onion into even 1½-inch pieces.

steps.title: Make the marinade
steps.text: Whisk hung curd with roasted besan, ginger-garlic, spices, lemon juice, mustard oil and salt into a thick paste.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Coat everything well and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes (up to 4 hours).

steps.title: Skewer
steps.text: Thread onto skewers (soak wooden ones in water for 20 minutes first), alternating with capsicum and onion.

steps.title: Grill
steps.text: Grill in an oven, air fryer or on a grill pan at 200°C for 12–15 minutes, turning once, until charred at the edges. Brush with a few drops of oil halfway.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Sprinkle chaat masala and lemon juice and serve hot with onion rings and mint chutney.

tips: Use thick hung curd so the marinade clings and does not drip.
Roasted besan in the marinade helps it stick and adds a smoky flavour.
serving_ideas: mint chutney and an onion-cucumber salad.
Best time: starter or a high-protein snack.
recipes.storage: marinated pieces keep in the fridge for 1 day; grill just before serving.

recipes.description: Rajma Corn Sundal, tempered with coconut and curry leaves.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Pressure-cook soaked rajma until soft; steam corn.

steps.title: Drain
steps.text: Drain well; keep the water for soups or dal.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat coconut oil, crackle mustard seeds, add urad dal, dry red chillies, curry leaves, hing, green chilli and ginger.

steps.title: Toss
steps.text: Add the cooked rajma and sweet corn kernels and salt and toss for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Switch off, add the grated coconut, lemon juice and coriander and mix.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve warm as an evening snack.

tips: Cook the legumes until soft but still whole; mushy legumes make a sticky sundal.
serving_ideas: a cup of tea or buttermilk.
Best time: evening snack; a traditional Navratri offering.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

recipes.description: Boiled eggs in a tangy gravy flavoured with pickle spices and mustard oil.

steps.title: Boil the eggs
steps.text: Boil the eggs for 10 minutes, cool in cold water and peel. Make shallow slits on each so the masala soaks in.

steps.title: Roast the eggs
steps.text: Toss the eggs in ½ tsp oil with a pinch of turmeric and chilli for 2 minutes until lightly golden. Set aside.

steps.title: Make the gravy
steps.text: Heat mustard oil until it smokes lightly, lower the flame and add the pickle spices (fennel, kalonji, methi, mustard). Sauté the onion until golden, add ginger, garlic and tomato and cook until thick. Lower the flame and stir in the whisked curd.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Add water to the consistency you like, add salt and simmer for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Add the eggs
steps.text: Add the eggs and simmer for 4–5 minutes so they absorb the flavours.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with coriander and serve hot.

tips: Slit the boiled eggs so the gravy flavours them all the way through.
serving_ideas: phulka, jeera rice or brown rice, with a salad and curd.
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

steps.text: Keep the chicken mince ready; no marinating is needed.

steps.title: Make the masala
steps.text: Heat oil, add the whole spices and fry for 30 seconds. Add the onion and sauté for 10–12 minutes until deep golden. Add ginger, garlic and chilli, then the tomato purée and powdered spices, and cook until the oil separates.

steps.text: Add the marinated chicken and cook on high flame for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until it changes colour and is coated in masala.

steps.text: The chicken is done when the juices run clear and there is no pink near the bone.

tips: Use skinless chicken to cut saturated fat.

recipes.description: Mutton in a mildly sweet, creamy fenugreek gravy made with milk instead of cream.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Wash the mutton, drain well and mix with the marinade. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight.

steps.title: Make the masala
steps.text: Boil the onion and cashews for 5 minutes and blend to a smooth paste. Heat oil, crackle cumin, add ginger, garlic and chilli, then the methi, and sauté for 3 minutes. Add the onion-cashew paste and cook for 4 minutes, then stir in the milk.

steps.title: Bhuno
steps.text: Add the marinated mutton and cook on high flame, stirring often, for 8–10 minutes until it is well coated and the masala starts to stick.

steps.title: Pressure-cook
steps.text: Add 1½ cups hot water and pressure-cook for 5–6 whistles on medium flame (or simmer covered for 1½ hours) until the mutton is tender.

steps.title: Reduce
steps.text: Open the cooker and simmer uncovered to the consistency you like.

steps.title: Finish & serve
steps.text: Skim off any surface fat, add the coriander leaves and serve hot.

tips: Choose lean cuts and trim visible fat to lower saturated fat.
Skim the fat that rises after cooking; it makes a big difference.
serving_ideas: phulka, jeera rice or brown rice, with a salad and curd.
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2 days; tastes better the next day. Freezes for 1 month.

recipes.description: Fish in a tangy gravy flavoured with pickle spices and mustard oil.

steps.title: Clean & season
steps.text: Wash the fish fillets well, pat dry and rub with turmeric, chilli and salt. Rest for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Sear (optional)
steps.text: Lightly sear the pieces in a non-stick pan with a few drops of oil for 1 minute per side; this helps them hold their shape.

steps.title: Make the curry
steps.text: Heat mustard oil until it smokes lightly, lower the flame and add the pickle spices (fennel, kalonji, methi, mustard). Sauté the onion until golden, add ginger, garlic and tomato and cook until thick. Lower the flame and stir in the whisked curd.

steps.title: Boil
steps.text: Add water as needed, check the salt and bring to a gentle boil.

steps.title: Add the fish
steps.text: Slide in the pieces in a single layer. Simmer for 8 minutes without stirring; swirl the pan gently instead.

steps.title: Rest & serve
steps.text: Switch off, cover and rest for 10 minutes so the flavours develop. Serve hot.

tips: Do not stir after adding the fish; swirl the pan so the pieces stay whole.
Fish cooks fast; it is done when it flakes easily.
serving_ideas: steamed rice or red rice, with a vegetable side.
Best time: lunch.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day. Reheat gently.

steps.text: Lightly sear the pieces in a non-stick pan with a few drops of oil for 1 minute per side; this helps them hold their shape.

steps.title: Make the curry
steps.text: Heat oil and butter, add the whole spices, ginger and garlic. Add tomatoes and soaked cashews and cook for 10 minutes until soft. Cool, blend to a very smooth purée and strain. Return to the pan with chilli powder and simmer for 5 minutes, then add milk and kasuri methi.

steps.title: Boil
steps.text: Add water as needed, check the salt and bring to a gentle boil.

steps.title: Add the fish
steps.text: Slide in the pieces in a single layer. Simmer for 8 minutes without stirring; swirl the pan gently instead.

steps.title: Rest & serve
steps.text: Switch off, cover and rest for 10 minutes so the flavours develop. Serve hot.

tips: Do not stir after adding the fish; swirl the pan so the pieces stay whole.
Fish cooks fast; it is done when it flakes easily.

recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day. Reheat gently.

recipes.description: Wholesome almond dates ladoos with no refined sugar.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Roast and chop the almonds; blend dates.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: In a large bowl, mix the almonds, dates and cardamom powder together well.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: While still warm, take a spoonful and press firmly between your palms into a round ladoo.

steps.title: Set
steps.text: Place on a plate and let them firm up for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Store
steps.text: Store in an airtight box.

tips: If the mixture does not bind, add 1–2 tsp warm ghee or a little more date paste.

recipes.description: A creamy apple oats kheer, lightly sweetened.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Wash or roast the rolled oats and apple as listed.

steps.title: Boil the toned milk
steps.text: Bring the toned milk to a boil in a heavy-bottomed pan, stirring so it does not stick.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Add the rolled oats and apple and simmer on low flame for 10 minutes, stirring often and scraping the sides, until soft and creamy.

steps.title: Flavour
steps.text: Add the cardamom and saffron and simmer for 2 more minutes.

steps.title: Sweeten
steps.text: Switch off the flame and let it cool for 5 minutes, then stir in the dates. Adding jaggery off the heat keeps the milk from curdling.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with the almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled.

tips: Use a heavy-bottomed pan and stir often so the milk does not burn.
Kheer thickens as it cools; add a little warm milk to loosen it.
serving_ideas: enjoy a small portion after a meal, or with a cup of tea.
Keep sweets to a small bowl or 1–2 pieces.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

steps.title: Add the liquid
steps.text: Add the toned milk (it will splutter, so pour carefully) and stir continuously.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Cook on medium-low flame for 20 minutes, stirring often, until the liquid is absorbed and the halwa thickens.

steps.title: Sweeten
steps.text: Add the jaggery and cardamom and cook for 3–4 minutes until the halwa leaves the sides of the pan.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with the almonds and cashews and serve warm.

tips: Halwa needs patient stirring on low heat; do not rush it.
This lighter version uses less ghee and jaggery instead of sugar.
serving_ideas: enjoy a small portion after a meal, or with a cup of tea.
Keep sweets to a small bowl or 1–2 pieces.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 3 days; warm before serving.

recipes.description: Wholesome quinoa peanut chikkis with no refined sugar.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Pop the quinoa in a dry pan; melt jaggery to hard-crack.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: In a large bowl, mix the quinoa, peanuts and jaggery together well.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: While still warm, take a spoonful and press firmly between your palms into a round ladoo.

steps.title: Set
steps.text: Place on a plate and let them firm up for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Store
steps.text: Store in an airtight box.

tips: If the mixture does not bind, add 1–2 tsp warm ghee or a little more date paste.
Make them small; one ladoo is a satisfying portion.
serving_ideas: one ladoo with a glass of milk, or as a pre-workout snack.
Great for children’s tiffin and for travel.
recipes.storage: keeps in an airtight box for 1–2 weeks (ladoos with fresh coconut: 5 days in the fridge).

recipes.description: A lighter ragi dates halwa made with less ghee.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Prepare the ragi as listed.

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Heat the ghee and roast the ragi on low flame, stirring constantly, until golden and aromatic.

steps.title: Add the liquid
steps.text: Add the toned milk (it will splutter, so pour carefully) and stir continuously.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Cook on medium-low flame for 10 minutes, stirring often, until the liquid is absorbed and the halwa thickens.

steps.title: Sweeten
steps.text: Add the dates and cardamom and cook for 3–4 minutes until the halwa leaves the sides of the pan.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with the almonds and cashews and serve warm.

tips: Halwa needs patient stirring on low heat; do not rush it.
This lighter version uses less ghee and jaggery instead of sugar.
serving_ideas: enjoy a small portion after a meal, or with a cup of tea.
Keep sweets to a small bowl or 1–2 pieces.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 3 days; warm before serving.

recipes.description: A creamy ragi dates kheer, lightly sweetened.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Wash or roast the ragi as listed.

steps.title: Boil the toned milk
steps.text: Bring the toned milk to a boil in a heavy-bottomed pan, stirring so it does not stick.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Add the ragi and simmer on low flame for 10 minutes, stirring often and scraping the sides, until soft and creamy.

steps.title: Flavour
steps.text: Add the cardamom and saffron and simmer for 2 more minutes.

steps.title: Sweeten
steps.text: Switch off the flame and let it cool for 5 minutes, then stir in the dates. Adding jaggery off the heat keeps the milk from curdling.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with the almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled.

tips: Use a heavy-bottomed pan and stir often so the milk does not burn.
Kheer thickens as it cools; add a little warm milk to loosen it.
serving_ideas: enjoy a small portion after a meal, or with a cup of tea.
Keep sweets to a small bowl or 1–2 pieces.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

recipes.description: A pink barnyard millet dosa with beetroot in the batter.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Wash the barnyard millet and soak for 5–6 hours. Separately wash and soak the urad dal with the methi seeds for 4–5 hours.

steps.title: Grind
steps.text: Grind the urad dal with ice-cold water until light, fluffy and doubled in volume. Grind the soaked grain to a smooth paste. Mix both with clean hands.

steps.title: Ferment
steps.text: Add salt, cover and keep in a warm place for 8–12 hours (overnight) until the batter rises and smells mildly sour.

steps.title: Flavour the batter
steps.text: Blend the beetroot and stir into the batter.

steps.title: Heat the tawa
steps.text: Heat a cast-iron or non-stick tawa on medium-high flame. Sprinkle water; it should sizzle and evaporate. Wipe with an oiled cloth or half an onion.

steps.title: Spread the dosa
steps.text: Pour a ladle of batter in the centre and spread it in quick outward circles into a thin round.

steps.title: Crisp it up
steps.text: Drizzle ½ tsp oil or ghee over the dosa and cook on medium flame for 1–2 minutes until the base turns golden and crisp.

steps.title: Fold & serve
steps.text: Fold the dosa in half or roll it up and serve immediately.

steps.title: Repeat
steps.text: Wipe the tawa with a damp cloth between dosas to cool it slightly so the batter spreads evenly.

tips: In cold weather, ferment the batter in a switched-off oven with the light on.
Use non-iodised salt for better fermentation.
serving_ideas: coconut chutney and sambar.
Best time: breakfast or dinner.
recipes.storage: fermented batter keeps in the fridge for 3–4 days. Cooked dosas are best eaten fresh.

recipes.description: Pink barnyard millet idlis with beetroot.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Wash and soak the barnyard millet for 5–6 hours. Separately soak the urad dal with methi seeds for 4 hours.

steps.title: Grind the dal
steps.text: Grind the urad dal with ice-cold water, a little at a time, to a light, fluffy, smooth batter.

steps.title: Grind the grain
steps.text: Grind the soaked grain to a slightly coarse, semolina-like batter. Mix both batters well with your hand.

steps.title: Ferment
steps.text: Add salt, cover and leave in a warm place for 8–12 hours until it doubles and smells pleasantly sour.

steps.title: Add flavour
steps.text: Fold the beetroot purée into the batter.

steps.title: Prepare the steamer
steps.text: Boil 2 cups water in an idli steamer or pressure cooker (without the whistle). Grease the idli moulds lightly.

steps.title: Fill the moulds
steps.text: Gently stir the batter without knocking out the air and pour into the moulds until three-quarters full.

steps.title: Steam
steps.text: Steam on medium-high flame for 10–12 minutes. A toothpick inserted in the centre should come out clean.

steps.title: Rest & demould
steps.text: Rest for 2 minutes, then scoop out the idlis with a wet spoon and serve hot.

tips: Use a 4:1 ratio of idli rice to urad dal for soft idlis.
Do not over-stir fermented batter; it loses the air that makes idlis fluffy.
serving_ideas: sambar and coconut or tomato chutney.
Best time: breakfast; also great for tiffin boxes.
recipes.storage: batter keeps in the fridge for 3–4 days; steamed idlis keep for 1 day and can be re-steamed.

recipes.description: A thick barnyard millet uttapam topped with beetroot onion.

steps.title: Prepare the batter
steps.text: Soak the barnyard millet for 5 hours and the urad dal with methi seeds for 4 hours. Grind separately, mix, add salt and ferment overnight.

steps.title: Thicken
steps.text: Uttapam batter should be thicker than dosa batter; do not thin it.

steps.title: Chop the topping
steps.text: Finely chop the beetroot, onion and coriander leaves and mix them together.

steps.title: Heat the tawa
steps.text: Heat a tawa on medium flame and grease it lightly.

steps.title: Spread
steps.text: Pour a ladle of batter and spread it gently into a thick 5–6 inch round.

steps.title: Add the topping
steps.text: Sprinkle 2 tbsp of the topping evenly and press it in gently with the back of the ladle.

steps.title: Cook covered
steps.text: Drizzle oil around the edges, cover and cook on medium-low flame for 3 minutes until the base is golden.

steps.title: Flip
steps.text: Flip and cook the topping side for 1–2 minutes until lightly browned.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with chutney and sambar.

tips: Cooking covered on low heat makes the uttapam soft and fully cooked inside.
Press the topping into the batter so it does not fall off when flipped.
serving_ideas: coconut chutney, tomato chutney and sambar.
Best time: breakfast or a light dinner.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh.

steps.text: Wash the barnyard millet and soak for 5–6 hours. Separately wash and soak the urad dal with the methi seeds for 4–5 hours.

steps.title: Grind
steps.text: Grind the urad dal with ice-cold water until light, fluffy and doubled in volume. Grind the soaked grain to a smooth paste. Mix both with clean hands.

steps.title: Ferment
steps.text: Add salt, cover and keep in a warm place for 8–12 hours (overnight) until the batter rises and smells mildly sour.

steps.title: Heat the tawa
steps.text: Heat a cast-iron or non-stick tawa on medium-high flame. Sprinkle water; it should sizzle and evaporate. Wipe with an oiled cloth or half an onion.

steps.title: Spread the dosa
steps.text: Pour a ladle of batter in the centre and spread it in quick outward circles into a thin round.

steps.title: Add the topping
steps.text: Spread 2–3 tbsp of the egg mixture on the dosa and cook until set.

steps.title: Crisp it up
steps.text: Drizzle ½ tsp oil or ghee over the dosa and cook on medium flame for 1–2 minutes until the base turns golden and crisp.

steps.title: Fold & serve
steps.text: Fold the dosa in half or roll it up and serve immediately.

steps.title: Repeat
steps.text: Wipe the tawa with a damp cloth between dosas to cool it slightly so the batter spreads evenly.

tips: In cold weather, ferment the batter in a switched-off oven with the light on.
Use non-iodised salt for better fermentation.
serving_ideas: coconut chutney and sambar.
Best time: breakfast or dinner.
recipes.storage: fermented batter keeps in the fridge for 3–4 days. Cooked dosas are best eaten fresh.

recipes.description: Barnyard Millet idlis with fresh methi.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Wash and soak the barnyard millet for 5–6 hours. Separately soak the urad dal with methi seeds for 4 hours.

steps.title: Grind the dal
steps.text: Grind the urad dal with ice-cold water, a little at a time, to a light, fluffy, smooth batter.

steps.title: Grind the grain
steps.text: Grind the soaked grain to a slightly coarse, semolina-like batter. Mix both batters well with your hand.

steps.title: Ferment
steps.text: Add salt, cover and leave in a warm place for 8–12 hours until it doubles and smells pleasantly sour.

steps.title: Add flavour
steps.text: Fold the methi into the batter.

steps.title: Prepare the steamer
steps.text: Boil 2 cups water in an idli steamer or pressure cooker (without the whistle). Grease the idli moulds lightly.

steps.title: Fill the moulds
steps.text: Gently stir the batter without knocking out the air and pour into the moulds until three-quarters full.

steps.title: Steam
steps.text: Steam on medium-high flame for 10–12 minutes. A toothpick inserted in the centre should come out clean.

steps.title: Rest & demould
steps.text: Rest for 2 minutes, then scoop out the idlis with a wet spoon and serve hot.

tips: Use a 4:1 ratio of idli rice to urad dal for soft idlis.
Do not over-stir fermented batter; it loses the air that makes idlis fluffy.
serving_ideas: sambar and coconut or tomato chutney.
Best time: breakfast; also great for tiffin boxes.
recipes.storage: batter keeps in the fridge for 3–4 days; steamed idlis keep for 1 day and can be re-steamed.

recipes.description: A thick barnyard millet uttapam topped with mushroom onion.

steps.title: Prepare the batter
steps.text: Soak the barnyard millet for 5 hours and the urad dal with methi seeds for 4 hours. Grind separately, mix, add salt and ferment overnight.

steps.title: Thicken
steps.text: Uttapam batter should be thicker than dosa batter; do not thin it.

steps.title: Chop the topping
steps.text: Finely chop the mushrooms, onion and capsicum and mix them together.

steps.title: Heat the tawa
steps.text: Heat a tawa on medium flame and grease it lightly.

steps.title: Spread
steps.text: Pour a ladle of batter and spread it gently into a thick 5–6 inch round.

steps.title: Add the topping
steps.text: Sprinkle 2 tbsp of the topping evenly and press it in gently with the back of the ladle.

steps.title: Cook covered
steps.text: Drizzle oil around the edges, cover and cook on medium-low flame for 3 minutes until the base is golden.

steps.title: Flip
steps.text: Flip and cook the topping side for 1–2 minutes until lightly browned.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with chutney and sambar.

tips: Cooking covered on low heat makes the uttapam soft and fully cooked inside.
Press the topping into the batter so it does not fall off when flipped.
serving_ideas: coconut chutney, tomato chutney and sambar.
Best time: breakfast or a light dinner.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh.

recipes.description: A wholesome bajra chila with bathua, quick to make and rich in fibre.

steps.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps.text: Finely chop the onion and green chilli and grate the ginger. Small, even pieces keep the chila thin and help it cook evenly.

steps.title: Make the batter
steps.text: In a mixing bowl, combine the bajra, besan and bathua leaves with turmeric, ajwain, chilli powder and salt. Add water a little at a time and whisk to a smooth, lump-free batter that flows like dosa batter.

steps.title: Add vegetables & rest
steps.text: Fold in the chopped vegetables, ginger and coriander. Rest the batter for 10 minutes so it thickens slightly and the chila turns soft.

steps.title: Heat the pan
steps.text: Heat a non-stick or well-seasoned iron tawa on medium flame and brush it with ¼ tsp oil. A few drops of water should sizzle when the pan is ready.

steps.title: Spread the chila
steps.text: Pour one ladle of batter in the centre and spread it gently in circles into a 6–7 inch round. Drizzle a few drops of oil around the edges.

steps.title: Cook the first side
steps.text: Cook on medium-low flame for 2–3 minutes, until the top looks set and the edges lift easily and turn golden.

steps.title: Flip & cook
steps.text: Flip with a flat spatula and cook the other side for 1–2 minutes, pressing lightly, until golden spots appear.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with mint-coriander chutney or curd. Make the remaining chilas the same way, adding only a few drops of oil each time.

tips: Rest the batter for 10 minutes; it makes the chila softer and easier to flip.
Keep the flame medium-low so the centre cooks before the outside browns.
serving_ideas: mint-coriander chutney, plain curd or raita, and a cucumber-tomato salad.
Best time: breakfast, or an early evening meal.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh. Plain batter (without vegetables) keeps in the fridge in an airtight box for up to 12 hours.

recipes.description: A protein-rich chana dal chila with bathua, no fermentation needed.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Wash the chana dal 2–3 times and soak in plenty of water for 5 hours. Drain well.

steps.title: Grind the batter
steps.text: Grind the soaked dal with ginger, green chillies and cumin, adding water little by little, to a smooth, thick batter. It should coat the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Add hing and salt and mix in the bathua leaves and onion. The batter does not need fermentation and can be used right away.

steps.title: Heat the pan
steps.text: Heat a non-stick or iron tawa on medium flame and grease it lightly with oil.

steps.title: Spread the chila
steps.text: Pour a ladle of batter and spread it quickly into a thin round. Drizzle a few drops of oil around the edges.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Cook on medium flame for 2–3 minutes until the base is golden and crisp, then flip and cook the other side for 1 minute.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with green chutney or tomato chutney. Repeat with the remaining batter.

tips: Do not add too much water while grinding; a thick batter gives crisp chilas.
Soaking can be done overnight for a quicker morning.
serving_ideas: mint-coriander chutney, plain curd or raita, and a cucumber-tomato salad.
Best time: breakfast, or an early evening meal.
recipes.storage: Batter keeps in the fridge for up to 24 hours; stir and adjust with a little water before use.

steps.text: In a mixing bowl, combine the makki, besan and bathua leaves with turmeric, ajwain, chilli powder and salt. Add water a little at a time and whisk to a smooth, lump-free batter that flows like dosa batter.

steps.title: Add vegetables & rest
steps.text: Fold in the chopped vegetables, ginger and coriander. Rest the batter for 10 minutes so it thickens slightly and the chila turns soft.

steps.title: Heat the pan
steps.text: Heat a non-stick or well-seasoned iron tawa on medium flame and brush it with ¼ tsp oil. A few drops of water should sizzle when the pan is ready.

steps.title: Spread the chila
steps.text: Pour one ladle of batter in the centre and spread it gently in circles into a 6–7 inch round. Drizzle a few drops of oil around the edges.

steps.title: Cook the first side
steps.text: Cook on medium-low flame for 2–3 minutes, until the top looks set and the edges lift easily and turn golden.

steps.title: Flip & cook
steps.text: Flip with a flat spatula and cook the other side for 1–2 minutes, pressing lightly, until golden spots appear.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with mint-coriander chutney or curd. Make the remaining chilas the same way, adding only a few drops of oil each time.

tips: Rest the batter for 10 minutes; it makes the chila softer and easier to flip.
Keep the flame medium-low so the centre cooks before the outside browns.
serving_ideas: mint-coriander chutney, plain curd or raita, and a cucumber-tomato salad.
Best time: breakfast, or an early evening meal.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh. Plain batter (without vegetables) keeps in the fridge in an airtight box for up to 12 hours.

recipes.description: A protein-rich masoor chila with bathua, no fermentation needed.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Wash the masoor dal 2–3 times and soak in plenty of water for 2 hours. Drain well.

steps.title: Grind the batter
steps.text: Grind the soaked dal with ginger, green chillies and cumin, adding water little by little, to a smooth, thick batter. It should coat the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Add hing and salt and mix in the bathua leaves and onion. The batter does not need fermentation and can be used right away.

steps.title: Heat the pan
steps.text: Heat a non-stick or iron tawa on medium flame and grease it lightly with oil.

steps.title: Spread the chila
steps.text: Pour a ladle of batter and spread it quickly into a thin round. Drizzle a few drops of oil around the edges.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Cook on medium flame for 2–3 minutes until the base is golden and crisp, then flip and cook the other side for 1 minute.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with green chutney or tomato chutney. Repeat with the remaining batter.

tips: Do not add too much water while grinding; a thick batter gives crisp chilas.
Soaking can be done overnight for a quicker morning.
serving_ideas: mint-coriander chutney, plain curd or raita, and a cucumber-tomato salad.
Best time: breakfast, or an early evening meal.
recipes.storage: Batter keeps in the fridge for up to 24 hours; stir and adjust with a little water before use.
