steps.text: Heat oil, add cumin, fennel and hing; this Rajasthani tempering keeps the sabzi dry and tangy.

steps.title: Add the spices
steps.text: Lower the flame and add the turmeric and powdered spices with 1 tbsp water so they do not burn. Stir for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the cabbage and salt and toss well to coat with the masala.

steps.title: Cook covered
steps.text: Cover and cook on low flame for 8 minutes, stirring every few minutes. Sprinkle a little water only if it starts to stick.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Uncover, raise the flame for 1 minute to dry any moisture, then add the coriander leaves and mix gently.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with phulka, paratha or dal-rice.

tips: Cut vegetables to the same size so they cook evenly.
Cook on low heat with the lid on; the vegetables steam in their own moisture and need very little oil.
serving_ideas: phulka, paratha or bhakri, with dal and curd.
Best time: lunch or dinner; also great in tiffin boxes.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1–2 days.

recipes.description: Aloo slow-cooked handi-style with curd and whole spices.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Wash and cut the potato into bite-sized pieces.

steps.title: Make the gravy
steps.text: Heat oil with cumin, bay leaf and cardamom. Sauté the onion until golden, add ginger and garlic, then tomato purée and spices, and cook until thick. Lower the flame and stir in the whisked curd.

steps.title: Adjust
steps.text: Add water as needed for a medium-thick gravy, add salt and bring to a gentle boil.

steps.title: Add the main ingredients
steps.text: Add the potato and stir gently to coat with the gravy.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Cover and simmer on low flame for 12 minutes until everything is cooked and the flavours blend.

steps.title: Finish & serve
steps.text: Add the coriander leaves and serve hot.

tips: Cook the masala until oil separates; this removes the raw taste and gives a rich gravy with less fat.
Add paneer or soft vegetables at the end so they stay soft and hold their shape.
serving_ideas: phulka, multigrain roti, jeera rice or brown rice.
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2 days. Reheat gently, adding a splash of water.

recipes.description: Barnyard Millet pulao with broccoli and whole spices.

steps.title: Rinse & soak
steps.text: Wash the barnyard millet 3–4 times until the water runs clear and soak for 30 minutes. Drain.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee and oil in a heavy pot or cooker. Add the whole spices and fry for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the onion and sauté until light golden, then ginger, garlic and green chilli.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the broccoli and sauté for 2–3 minutes.

steps.title: Add the barnyard millet
steps.text: Add the drained grain and stir gently for 1–2 minutes to coat it with ghee.

steps.title: Add water
steps.text: Add 440 ml hot water and salt; taste the water, it should be slightly salty.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Cover and cook on the lowest flame for 12–15 minutes (or 1 whistle in a pressure cooker) until the water is absorbed and the grains are tender.

steps.title: Rest & fluff
steps.text: Rest covered for 5–10 minutes, then fluff gently with a fork. Garnish and serve.

tips: Rest the rice for 5 minutes after cooking; the grains firm up and stay separate.
Use a heavy-bottomed pot and the lowest flame so the bottom does not burn.
serving_ideas: raita, a green salad and papad (roasted).
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day. Reheat with a sprinkle of water.

recipes.description: Barnyard Millet pulao with patta gobhi and whole spices.

steps.title: Rinse & soak
steps.text: Wash the barnyard millet 3–4 times until the water runs clear and soak for 30 minutes. Drain.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee and oil in a heavy pot or cooker. Add the whole spices and fry for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the onion and sauté until light golden, then ginger, garlic and green chilli.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the cabbage and green peas and sauté for 2–3 minutes.

steps.title: Add the barnyard millet
steps.text: Add the drained grain and stir gently for 1–2 minutes to coat it with ghee.

steps.title: Add water
steps.text: Add 440 ml hot water and salt; taste the water, it should be slightly salty.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Cover and cook on the lowest flame for 12–15 minutes (or 1 whistle in a pressure cooker) until the water is absorbed and the grains are tender.

Best time: lunch or dinner.

recipes.description: Barnyard Millet tossed South Indian style with beetroot.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: Wash and cook the barnyard millet with water and salt until each grain is soft but separate. Spread on a plate to cool completely.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat the oil and crackle the mustard seeds, then add the urad dal, chana dal, dry red chillies, curry leaves, hing and peanuts and fry until the dals and nuts turn golden.

steps.title: Cook the beetroot
steps.text: Sauté until soft and add the spice powder.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Add the cooled rice and gently fold everything together without mashing the grains.

steps.title: Rest & serve
steps.text: Rest for 10 minutes so the flavours soak in. Garnish and serve warm or at room temperature.

tips: Use cooled, day-old or fully cooled rice so the grains stay separate.
serving_ideas: curd or raita, a poriyal and roasted papad.
Best time: lunch and lunch boxes; ideal for travel.
recipes.storage: keeps for 6–8 hours at room temperature (great for travel) or 1 day in the fridge.

steps.text: Heat ghee and oil in a heavy pot or cooker. Add the whole spices and fry for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the onion and sauté until light golden, then ginger, garlic and green chilli.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the capsicum and sauté for 2–3 minutes.

steps.title: Add the brown rice
steps.text: Add the drained grain and stir gently for 1–2 minutes to coat it with ghee.

steps.title: Add water
steps.text: Add 520 ml hot water and salt; taste the water, it should be slightly salty.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Pressure-cook for 3 whistles, or simmer covered for 35–40 minutes.

steps.title: Rest & fluff
steps.text: Rest covered for 5–10 minutes, then fluff gently with a fork. Garnish and serve.

tips: Rest the rice for 5 minutes after cooking; the grains firm up and stay separate.
Use a heavy-bottomed pot and the lowest flame so the bottom does not burn.

Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day. Reheat with a sprinkle of water.

recipes.description: Fragrant layered brown rice biryani with chana.

steps.title: Soak the rice
steps.text: Wash the brown rice gently 3–4 times and soak for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Mix the kabuli chana with the marinade ingredients and rest for at least 30 minutes.

steps.title: Caramelise the onions
steps.text: Heat oil and half the ghee in a heavy pot and fry the sliced onions on medium flame, stirring, until deep golden (12–15 minutes). Remove half for layering.

steps.title: Cook the base
steps.text: Add the marinated kabuli chana to the remaining onions and cook on medium flame until almost done and the masala is thick.

steps.title: Par-boil the rice
steps.text: Boil the water with salt and whole spices. Add the drained rice and cook for 5–6 minutes until 70% done (the grain should still have a bite). Drain.

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: Spread the rice over the base. Top with fried onions, mint, coriander, garam masala, saffron soaked in warm milk and the remaining ghee.

steps.title: Dum
steps.text: Cover tightly (seal with foil or dough) and cook on the lowest flame for 15 minutes, or place the pot on a hot tawa.

steps.title: Rest & serve
steps.text: Rest for 10 minutes, then gently mix from the side and serve with raita.

tips: Par-boil the rice only 70%; it finishes cooking on dum.
Use a heavy pot or place it on a tawa so the bottom layer does not burn.

recipes.name_en: Brown Rice Chana Dal Lauki Khichdi
recipes.name_hi: ब्राउन राइस चना दाल लौकी खिचड़ी
recipes.description: A one-pot khichdi of brown rice with chana dal lauki.

steps.title: Wash & soak
steps.text: Wash the brown rice, chana dal and lauki together until the water runs clear and soak for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee in a pressure cooker, crackle the cumin, add hing, ginger and green chilli.

steps.title: Toast
steps.text: Add the drained grains and stir for 1 minute.

steps.title: Add grains & water
steps.text: Add the drained grains, turmeric, salt and 1280 ml water. Stir well.

steps.title: Pressure-cook
steps.text: Cook for 3–4 whistles on medium flame. Let the pressure release naturally.

steps.title: Adjust
steps.text: Open, mash lightly and add hot water if you like a softer, porridge-like consistency.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with a spoon of ghee, curd and roasted papad.

tips: A softer, mushier khichdi is easier to digest when you are unwell.
Add a little extra ghee on top just before serving for aroma.
serving_ideas: curd, kadhi or raita, roasted papad and a pickle (in moderation).
Best time: dinner; ideal when unwell.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh; keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

recipes.description: Fried brown rice with chicken and crunchy vegetables.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: Cook the brown rice until just done, spread on a plate and cool completely (day-old rice is ideal).

steps.title: Heat the wok
steps.text: Heat oil in a wok on the highest flame until it just starts to smoke.

steps.title: Aromatics
steps.text: Add garlic, ginger and the white part of the spring onions and stir-fry for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Stir-fry
steps.text: Add the vegetables and chicken and toss on high heat for 2–3 minutes; they should stay crunchy.

steps.title: Add rice
steps.text: Add the cold rice, soy sauce, vinegar, pepper and a little salt. Toss on high heat for 2 minutes, breaking up any lumps.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Add the spring onion greens, toss once and serve immediately.

tips: Use cold rice and a very hot wok so the rice does not turn mushy.
Low-sodium soy sauce keeps the salt in check.
serving_ideas: a bowl of clear soup or a light Indo-Chinese gravy.
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh; keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

steps.title: Dum
steps.text: Cover tightly (seal with foil or dough) and cook on the lowest flame for 15 minutes, or place the pot on a hot tawa.

steps.title: Rest & serve
steps.text: Rest for 10 minutes, then gently mix from the side and serve with raita.

tips: Par-boil the rice only 70%; it finishes cooking on dum.
Use a heavy pot or place it on a tawa so the bottom layer does not burn.
serving_ideas: onion-cucumber raita and a fresh salad.
Best time: lunch or festive meals.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1–2 days; sprinkle water and reheat covered.

recipes.description: Fragrant layered brown rice biryani with soya.

steps.title: Soak the rice
steps.text: Wash the brown rice gently 3–4 times and soak for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Mix the soya chunks and green peas with the marinade ingredients and rest for at least 30 minutes.

steps.title: Caramelise the onions
steps.text: Heat oil and half the ghee in a heavy pot and fry the sliced onions on medium flame, stirring, until deep golden (12–15 minutes). Remove half for layering.

steps.title: Cook the base
steps.text: Add the marinated soya chunks and green peas to the remaining onions and cook on medium flame until almost done and the masala is thick.

steps.title: Par-boil the rice
steps.text: Boil the water with salt and whole spices. Add the drained rice and cook for 5–6 minutes until 70% done (the grain should still have a bite). Drain.

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: Spread the rice over the base. Top with fried onions, mint, coriander, garam masala, saffron soaked in warm milk and the remaining ghee.

steps.title: Dum
steps.text: Cover tightly (seal with foil or dough) and cook on the lowest flame for 15 minutes, or place the pot on a hot tawa.

steps.title: Rest & serve
steps.text: Rest for 10 minutes, then gently mix from the side and serve with raita.

tips: Par-boil the rice only 70%; it finishes cooking on dum.
Use a heavy pot or place it on a tawa so the bottom layer does not burn.
serving_ideas: onion-cucumber raita and a fresh salad.
Best time: lunch or festive meals.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1–2 days; sprinkle water and reheat covered.

recipes.description: Fried brown rice with tofu and crunchy vegetables.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: Cook the brown rice until just done, spread on a plate and cool completely (day-old rice is ideal).

steps.title: Heat the wok
steps.text: Heat oil in a wok on the highest flame until it just starts to smoke.

steps.title: Aromatics
steps.text: Add garlic, ginger and the white part of the spring onions and stir-fry for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Stir-fry
steps.text: Add the vegetables and tofu and toss on high heat for 2–3 minutes; they should stay crunchy.

steps.title: Add rice
steps.text: Add the cold rice, soy sauce, vinegar, pepper and a little salt. Toss on high heat for 2 minutes, breaking up any lumps.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Add the spring onion greens, toss once and serve immediately.

tips: Use cold rice and a very hot wok so the rice does not turn mushy.
Low-sodium soy sauce keeps the salt in check.
serving_ideas: a bowl of clear soup or a light Indo-Chinese gravy.
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh; keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

recipes.description: Brown Rice pulao with tofu and whole spices.

steps.title: Rinse & soak
steps.text: Wash the brown rice 3–4 times until the water runs clear and soak for 60 minutes. Drain.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee and oil in a heavy pot or cooker. Add the whole spices and fry for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the onion and sauté until light golden, then ginger, garlic and green chilli.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the tofu and green peas and sauté for 2–3 minutes.

steps.title: Add the brown rice
steps.text: Add the drained grain and stir gently for 1–2 minutes to coat it with ghee.

steps.title: Add water
steps.text: Add 520 ml hot water and salt; taste the water, it should be slightly salty.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Pressure-cook for 3 whistles, or simmer covered for 35–40 minutes.

steps.title: Rest & fluff
steps.text: Rest covered for 5–10 minutes, then fluff gently with a fork. Garnish and serve.

tips: Rest the rice for 5 minutes after cooking; the grains firm up and stay separate.
Use a heavy-bottomed pot and the lowest flame so the bottom does not burn.
serving_ideas: raita, a green salad and papad (roasted).
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day. Reheat with a sprinkle of water.

recipes.description: A one-pot khichdi of brown rice with toor vegetable.

steps.title: Wash & soak
steps.text: Wash the brown rice, toor / arhar dal, carrot and green peas together until the water runs clear and soak for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee in a pressure cooker, crackle the cumin, add hing, ginger and green chilli.

steps.title: Toast
steps.text: Add the drained grains and stir for 1 minute.

steps.title: Add grains & water
steps.text: Add the drained grains, turmeric, salt and 1120 ml water. Stir well.

steps.title: Pressure-cook
steps.text: Cook for 3–4 whistles on medium flame. Let the pressure release naturally.

steps.title: Adjust
steps.text: Open, mash lightly and add hot water if you like a softer, porridge-like consistency.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with a spoon of ghee, curd and roasted papad.

tips: A softer, mushier khichdi is easier to digest when you are unwell.
Add a little extra ghee on top just before serving for aroma.
serving_ideas: curd, kadhi or raita, roasted papad and a pickle (in moderation).
Best time: dinner; ideal when unwell.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh; keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

recipes.description: Barnyard Millet tossed South Indian style with capsicum.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: Wash and cook the barnyard millet with water and salt until each grain is soft but separate. Spread on a plate to cool completely.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat the oil and crackle the mustard seeds, then add the urad dal, chana dal, dry red chillies, curry leaves, hing and peanuts and fry until the dals and nuts turn golden.

steps.title: Cook the capsicum
steps.text: Sauté and add the spice powder.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Add the cooled rice and gently fold everything together without mashing the grains.

steps.title: Rest & serve
steps.text: Rest for 10 minutes so the flavours soak in. Garnish and serve warm or at room temperature.

tips: Use cooled, day-old or fully cooled rice so the grains stay separate.
serving_ideas: curd or raita, a poriyal and roasted papad.
Best time: lunch and lunch boxes; ideal for travel.
recipes.storage: keeps for 6–8 hours at room temperature (great for travel) or 1 day in the fridge.

recipes.description: Fried basmati with corn and crunchy vegetables.

steps.title: Heat the wok
steps.text: Heat oil in a wok on the highest flame until it just starts to smoke.

steps.text: Add the vegetables and sweet corn kernels and red / yellow bell pepper and toss on high heat for 2–3 minutes; they should stay crunchy.

recipes.description: A one-pot khichdi of foxtail with chana dal lauki.

steps.title: Wash & soak
steps.text: Wash the foxtail millet, chana dal and lauki together until the water runs clear and soak for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee in a pressure cooker, crackle the cumin, add hing, ginger and green chilli.

steps.title: Toast
steps.text: Add the drained grains and stir for 1 minute.

steps.title: Add grains & water
steps.text: Add the drained grains, turmeric, salt and 1280 ml water. Stir well.

steps.title: Pressure-cook
steps.text: Cook for 3–4 whistles on medium flame. Let the pressure release naturally.

steps.title: Adjust
steps.text: Open, mash lightly and add hot water if you like a softer, porridge-like consistency.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with a spoon of ghee, curd and roasted papad.

tips: A softer, mushier khichdi is easier to digest when you are unwell.
Add a little extra ghee on top just before serving for aroma.
serving_ideas: curd, kadhi or raita, roasted papad and a pickle (in moderation).
Best time: dinner; ideal when unwell.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh; keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

recipes.description: Foxtail Millet pulao with broccoli and whole spices.

steps.title: Rinse & soak
steps.text: Wash the foxtail millet 3–4 times until the water runs clear and soak for 30 minutes. Drain.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee and oil in a heavy pot or cooker. Add the whole spices and fry for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the onion and sauté until light golden, then ginger, garlic and green chilli.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the broccoli and sauté for 2–3 minutes.

steps.text: Add the drained grain and stir gently for 1–2 minutes to coat it with ghee.

steps.title: Add water
steps.text: Add 440 ml hot water and salt; taste the water, it should be slightly salty.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Cover and cook on the lowest flame for 12–15 minutes (or 1 whistle in a pressure cooker) until the water is absorbed and the grains are tender.

steps.title: Rest & fluff
steps.text: Rest covered for 5–10 minutes, then fluff gently with a fork. Garnish and serve.

tips: Rest the rice for 5 minutes after cooking; the grains firm up and stay separate.
Use a heavy-bottomed pot and the lowest flame so the bottom does not burn.
serving_ideas: raita, a green salad and papad (roasted).
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day. Reheat with a sprinkle of water.

recipes.description: Fragrant layered foxtail millet biryani with chana.

steps.title: Soak the rice
steps.text: Wash the foxtail millet gently 3–4 times and soak for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Mix the kabuli chana with the marinade ingredients and rest for at least 30 minutes.

steps.title: Caramelise the onions
steps.text: Heat oil and half the ghee in a heavy pot and fry the sliced onions on medium flame, stirring, until deep golden (12–15 minutes). Remove half for layering.

steps.title: Cook the base
steps.text: Add the marinated kabuli chana to the remaining onions and cook on medium flame until almost done and the masala is thick.

steps.title: Par-boil the rice
steps.text: Boil the water with salt and whole spices. Add the drained rice and cook for 5–6 minutes until 70% done (the grain should still have a bite). Drain.

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: Spread the rice over the base. Top with fried onions, mint, coriander, garam masala, saffron soaked in warm milk and the remaining ghee.

steps.title: Dum
steps.text: Cover tightly (seal with foil or dough) and cook on the lowest flame for 15 minutes, or place the pot on a hot tawa.

steps.title: Rest & serve
steps.text: Rest for 10 minutes, then gently mix from the side and serve with raita.

tips: Par-boil the rice only 70%; it finishes cooking on dum.
Use a heavy pot or place it on a tawa so the bottom layer does not burn.
serving_ideas: onion-cucumber raita and a fresh salad.
Best time: lunch or festive meals.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1–2 days; sprinkle water and reheat covered.

recipes.description: Foxtail Millet pulao with mushroom matar and whole spices.

steps.title: Rinse & soak
steps.text: Wash the foxtail millet 3–4 times until the water runs clear and soak for 30 minutes. Drain.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee and oil in a heavy pot or cooker. Add the whole spices and fry for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the onion and sauté until light golden, then ginger, garlic and green chilli.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the mushrooms and green peas and sauté for 2–3 minutes.

steps.title: Add the foxtail millet
steps.text: Add the drained grain and stir gently for 1–2 minutes to coat it with ghee.

steps.title: Add water
steps.text: Add 440 ml hot water and salt; taste the water, it should be slightly salty.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Cover and cook on the lowest flame for 12–15 minutes (or 1 whistle in a pressure cooker) until the water is absorbed and the grains are tender.

steps.title: Rest & fluff
steps.text: Rest covered for 5–10 minutes, then fluff gently with a fork. Garnish and serve.

tips: Rest the rice for 5 minutes after cooking; the grains firm up and stay separate.
Use a heavy-bottomed pot and the lowest flame so the bottom does not burn.
serving_ideas: raita, a green salad and papad (roasted).
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day. Reheat with a sprinkle of water.

recipes.description: Fragrant layered foxtail millet biryani with paneer.

steps.title: Soak the rice
steps.text: Wash the foxtail millet gently 3–4 times and soak for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Mix the paneer and capsicum with the marinade ingredients and rest for at least 30 minutes.

steps.title: Caramelise the onions
steps.text: Heat oil and half the ghee in a heavy pot and fry the sliced onions on medium flame, stirring, until deep golden (12–15 minutes). Remove half for layering.

steps.title: Cook the base
steps.text: Add the marinated paneer and capsicum to the remaining onions and cook on medium flame until almost done and the masala is thick.

steps.title: Par-boil the rice
steps.text: Boil the water with salt and whole spices. Add the drained rice and cook for 5–6 minutes until 70% done (the grain should still have a bite). Drain.

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: Spread the rice over the base. Top with fried onions, mint, coriander, garam masala, saffron soaked in warm milk and the remaining ghee.

steps.title: Dum
steps.text: Cover tightly (seal with foil or dough) and cook on the lowest flame for 15 minutes, or place the pot on a hot tawa.

steps.title: Rest & serve
steps.text: Rest for 10 minutes, then gently mix from the side and serve with raita.

tips: Par-boil the rice only 70%; it finishes cooking on dum.
Use a heavy pot or place it on a tawa so the bottom layer does not burn.
serving_ideas: onion-cucumber raita and a fresh salad.
Best time: lunch or festive meals.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1–2 days; sprinkle water and reheat covered.

recipes.description: A one-pot khichdi of foxtail with toor vegetable.

steps.title: Wash & soak
steps.text: Wash the foxtail millet, toor / arhar dal, carrot and green peas together until the water runs clear and soak for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee in a pressure cooker, crackle the cumin, add hing, ginger and green chilli.

steps.title: Toast
steps.text: Add the drained grains and stir for 1 minute.

steps.title: Add grains & water
steps.text: Add the drained grains, turmeric, salt and 1120 ml water. Stir well.

steps.title: Pressure-cook
steps.text: Cook for 3–4 whistles on medium flame. Let the pressure release naturally.

steps.title: Adjust
steps.text: Open, mash lightly and add hot water if you like a softer, porridge-like consistency.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with a spoon of ghee, curd and roasted papad.

tips: A softer, mushier khichdi is easier to digest when you are unwell.
Add a little extra ghee on top just before serving for aroma.
serving_ideas: curd, kadhi or raita, roasted papad and a pickle (in moderation).
Best time: dinner; ideal when unwell.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh; keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

recipes.description: Barnyard Millet tossed South Indian style with garlic.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: Wash and cook the barnyard millet with water and salt until each grain is soft but separate. Spread on a plate to cool completely.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat the oil and crackle the mustard seeds, then add the urad dal, chana dal, dry red chillies, curry leaves, hing and peanuts and fry until the dals and nuts turn golden.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Fry the garlic until golden and add pepper.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Add the cooled rice and gently fold everything together without mashing the grains.

steps.title: Rest & serve
steps.text: Rest for 10 minutes so the flavours soak in. Garnish and serve warm or at room temperature.

tips: Use cooled, day-old or fully cooled rice so the grains stay separate.
serving_ideas: curd or raita, a poriyal and roasted papad.
Best time: lunch and lunch boxes; ideal for travel.
recipes.storage: keeps for 6–8 hours at room temperature (great for travel) or 1 day in the fridge.

steps.text: Add the cooled rice and gently fold everything together without mashing the grains.

steps.title: Wash & soak
steps.text: Wash the kodo millet, chana dal and lauki together until the water runs clear and soak for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee in a pressure cooker, crackle the cumin, add hing, ginger and green chilli.

steps.title: Toast
steps.text: Add the drained grains and stir for 1 minute.

steps.title: Add grains & water

recipes.description: Kodo Millet pulao with broccoli and whole spices.

steps.title: Rinse & soak
steps.text: Wash the kodo millet 3–4 times until the water runs clear and soak for 30 minutes. Drain.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee and oil in a heavy pot or cooker. Add the whole spices and fry for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the onion and sauté until light golden, then ginger, garlic and green chilli.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the broccoli and sauté for 2–3 minutes.

steps.title: Add the kodo millet
steps.text: Add the drained grain and stir gently for 1–2 minutes to coat it with ghee.

steps.title: Add water
steps.text: Add 440 ml hot water and salt; taste the water, it should be slightly salty.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Cover and cook on the lowest flame for 12–15 minutes (or 1 whistle in a pressure cooker) until the water is absorbed and the grains are tender.

steps.title: Rest & fluff
steps.text: Rest covered for 5–10 minutes, then fluff gently with a fork. Garnish and serve.

tips: Rest the rice for 5 minutes after cooking; the grains firm up and stay separate.
Use a heavy-bottomed pot and the lowest flame so the bottom does not burn.
serving_ideas: raita, a green salad and papad (roasted).
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day. Reheat with a sprinkle of water.

steps.text: Add the lauki and sauté for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Add grains & water
steps.text: Add the drained grains, turmeric, salt and 720 ml water. Stir well.

steps.title: Pressure-cook
steps.text: Cook for 3–4 whistles on medium flame. Let the pressure release naturally.

steps.title: Adjust
steps.text: Open, mash lightly and add hot water if you like a softer, porridge-like consistency.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with a spoon of ghee, curd and roasted papad.

tips: A softer, mushier khichdi is easier to digest when you are unwell.
Add a little extra ghee on top just before serving for aroma.

recipes.description: Little Millet pulao with broccoli and whole spices.

steps.title: Rinse & soak
steps.text: Wash the little millet 3–4 times until the water runs clear and soak for 30 minutes. Drain.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee and oil in a heavy pot or cooker. Add the whole spices and fry for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the onion and sauté until light golden, then ginger, garlic and green chilli.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the broccoli and sauté for 2–3 minutes.

steps.title: Add the little millet
steps.text: Add the drained grain and stir gently for 1–2 minutes to coat it with ghee.

steps.title: Add water
steps.text: Add 440 ml hot water and salt; taste the water, it should be slightly salty.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Cover and cook on the lowest flame for 12–15 minutes (or 1 whistle in a pressure cooker) until the water is absorbed and the grains are tender.

steps.title: Rest & fluff
steps.text: Rest covered for 5–10 minutes, then fluff gently with a fork. Garnish and serve.

tips: Rest the rice for 5 minutes after cooking; the grains firm up and stay separate.
Use a heavy-bottomed pot and the lowest flame so the bottom does not burn.
serving_ideas: raita, a green salad and papad (roasted).
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day. Reheat with a sprinkle of water.

recipes.description: Fragrant layered little millet biryani with chana.

steps.title: Soak the rice
steps.text: Wash the little millet gently 3–4 times and soak for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Mix the kabuli chana with the marinade ingredients and rest for at least 30 minutes.

steps.title: Caramelise the onions
steps.text: Heat oil and half the ghee in a heavy pot and fry the sliced onions on medium flame, stirring, until deep golden (12–15 minutes). Remove half for layering.

steps.title: Cook the base
steps.text: Add the marinated kabuli chana to the remaining onions and cook on medium flame until almost done and the masala is thick.

steps.title: Par-boil the rice
steps.text: Boil the water with salt and whole spices. Add the drained rice and cook for 5–6 minutes until 70% done (the grain should still have a bite). Drain.

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: Spread the rice over the base. Top with fried onions, mint, coriander, garam masala, saffron soaked in warm milk and the remaining ghee.

steps.title: Dum
steps.text: Cover tightly (seal with foil or dough) and cook on the lowest flame for 15 minutes, or place the pot on a hot tawa.

steps.title: Rest & serve
steps.text: Rest for 10 minutes, then gently mix from the side and serve with raita.

tips: Par-boil the rice only 70%; it finishes cooking on dum.
Use a heavy pot or place it on a tawa so the bottom layer does not burn.
serving_ideas: onion-cucumber raita and a fresh salad.
Best time: lunch or festive meals.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1–2 days; sprinkle water and reheat covered.

recipes.description: Fried little millet with chicken and crunchy vegetables.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: Cook the little millet until just done, spread on a plate and cool completely (day-old rice is ideal).

steps.title: Heat the wok
steps.text: Heat oil in a wok on the highest flame until it just starts to smoke.

steps.title: Aromatics
steps.text: Add garlic, ginger and the white part of the spring onions and stir-fry for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Stir-fry
steps.text: Add the vegetables and chicken and toss on high heat for 2–3 minutes; they should stay crunchy.

steps.title: Add rice
steps.text: Add the cold rice, soy sauce, vinegar, pepper and a little salt. Toss on high heat for 2 minutes, breaking up any lumps.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Add the spring onion greens, toss once and serve immediately.

tips: Use cold rice and a very hot wok so the rice does not turn mushy.
Low-sodium soy sauce keeps the salt in check.
serving_ideas: a bowl of clear soup or a light Indo-Chinese gravy.
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh; keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

steps.text: Heat ghee and oil in a heavy pot or cooker. Add the whole spices and fry for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the onion and sauté until light golden, then ginger, garlic and green chilli.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the mushrooms and green peas and sauté for 2–3 minutes.

steps.title: Add the little millet
steps.text: Add the drained grain and stir gently for 1–2 minutes to coat it with ghee.

steps.title: Add water
steps.text: Add 440 ml hot water and salt; taste the water, it should be slightly salty.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Cover and cook on the lowest flame for 12–15 minutes (or 1 whistle in a pressure cooker) until the water is absorbed and the grains are tender.

steps.title: Rest & fluff
steps.text: Rest covered for 5–10 minutes, then fluff gently with a fork. Garnish and serve.

tips: Rest the rice for 5 minutes after cooking; the grains firm up and stay separate.
Use a heavy-bottomed pot and the lowest flame so the bottom does not burn.
serving_ideas: raita, a green salad and papad (roasted).
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day. Reheat with a sprinkle of water.

recipes.description: Fragrant layered little millet biryani with paneer.

steps.title: Soak the rice
steps.text: Wash the little millet gently 3–4 times and soak for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Mix the paneer and capsicum with the marinade ingredients and rest for at least 30 minutes.

steps.title: Caramelise the onions
steps.text: Heat oil and half the ghee in a heavy pot and fry the sliced onions on medium flame, stirring, until deep golden (12–15 minutes). Remove half for layering.

steps.title: Cook the base
steps.text: Add the marinated paneer and capsicum to the remaining onions and cook on medium flame until almost done and the masala is thick.

steps.title: Par-boil the rice
steps.text: Boil the water with salt and whole spices. Add the drained rice and cook for 5–6 minutes until 70% done (the grain should still have a bite). Drain.

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: Spread the rice over the base. Top with fried onions, mint, coriander, garam masala, saffron soaked in warm milk and the remaining ghee.

steps.title: Dum
steps.text: Cover tightly (seal with foil or dough) and cook on the lowest flame for 15 minutes, or place the pot on a hot tawa.

steps.title: Rest & serve
steps.text: Rest for 10 minutes, then gently mix from the side and serve with raita.

tips: Par-boil the rice only 70%; it finishes cooking on dum.
Use a heavy pot or place it on a tawa so the bottom layer does not burn.
serving_ideas: onion-cucumber raita and a fresh salad.
Best time: lunch or festive meals.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1–2 days; sprinkle water and reheat covered.

recipes.description: Fried little millet with paneer and crunchy vegetables.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: Cook the little millet until just done, spread on a plate and cool completely (day-old rice is ideal).

steps.title: Heat the wok
steps.text: Heat oil in a wok on the highest flame until it just starts to smoke.

steps.title: Aromatics
steps.text: Add garlic, ginger and the white part of the spring onions and stir-fry for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Stir-fry
steps.text: Add the vegetables and paneer and toss on high heat for 2–3 minutes; they should stay crunchy.

steps.title: Add rice
steps.text: Add the cold rice, soy sauce, vinegar, pepper and a little salt. Toss on high heat for 2 minutes, breaking up any lumps.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Add the spring onion greens, toss once and serve immediately.

tips: Use cold rice and a very hot wok so the rice does not turn mushy.
Low-sodium soy sauce keeps the salt in check.
serving_ideas: a bowl of clear soup or a light Indo-Chinese gravy.
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh; keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

recipes.description: A one-pot khichdi of little millet with toor vegetable.

steps.title: Wash & soak
steps.text: Wash the little millet, toor / arhar dal, carrot and green peas together until the water runs clear and soak for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee in a pressure cooker, crackle the cumin, add hing, ginger and green chilli.

steps.title: Toast
steps.text: Add the drained grains and stir for 1 minute.

steps.title: Add grains & water
steps.text: Add the drained grains, turmeric, salt and 1120 ml water. Stir well.

steps.title: Pressure-cook
steps.text: Cook for 3–4 whistles on medium flame. Let the pressure release naturally.

steps.title: Adjust
steps.text: Open, mash lightly and add hot water if you like a softer, porridge-like consistency.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with a spoon of ghee, curd and roasted papad.

tips: A softer, mushier khichdi is easier to digest when you are unwell.
Add a little extra ghee on top just before serving for aroma.
serving_ideas: curd, kadhi or raita, roasted papad and a pickle (in moderation).
Best time: dinner; ideal when unwell.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh; keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

recipes.description: Barnyard Millet tossed South Indian style with methi.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: Wash and cook the barnyard millet with water and salt until each grain is soft but separate. Spread on a plate to cool completely.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat the oil and crackle the mustard seeds, then add the urad dal, chana dal, dry red chillies, curry leaves, hing and peanuts and fry until the dals and nuts turn golden.

steps.title: Cook the methi
steps.text: Sauté onion and methi for 3 minutes.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Add the cooled rice and gently fold everything together without mashing the grains.

steps.title: Rest & serve
steps.text: Rest for 10 minutes so the flavours soak in. Garnish and serve warm or at room temperature.

tips: Use cooled, day-old or fully cooled rice so the grains stay separate.
serving_ideas: curd or raita, a poriyal and roasted papad.
Best time: lunch and lunch boxes; ideal for travel.
recipes.storage: keeps for 6–8 hours at room temperature (great for travel) or 1 day in the fridge.

recipes.description: Red Rice tossed South Indian style with methi.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: Wash and cook the red / matta rice with water and salt until each grain is soft but separate. Spread on a plate to cool completely.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat the oil and crackle the mustard seeds, then add the urad dal, chana dal, dry red chillies, curry leaves, hing and peanuts and fry until the dals and nuts turn golden.

steps.title: Cook the methi
steps.text: Sauté onion and methi for 3 minutes.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Add the cooled rice and gently fold everything together without mashing the grains.

steps.title: Rest & serve
steps.text: Rest for 10 minutes so the flavours soak in. Garnish and serve warm or at room temperature.

tips: Use cooled, day-old or fully cooled rice so the grains stay separate.

recipes.name_en: Mixed Vegetable Brown Rice Moong Khichdi
recipes.name_hi: मिक्स सब्ज़ी ब्राउन राइस मूंग खिचड़ी
recipes.description: A soft one-pot khichdi of brown rice and moong dal with mixed vegetable.

steps.title: Wash & soak
steps.text: Wash the brown rice and moong dal together until the water runs clear and soak for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee in a pressure cooker, crackle the cumin, add hing, ginger and green chilli.

steps.title: Add vegetables
steps.text: Add the carrot, green peas, french beans and tomato and sauté for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Add grains & water
steps.text: Add the drained grains, turmeric, salt and 720 ml water. Stir well.

steps.title: Pressure-cook
steps.text: Cook for 3–4 whistles on medium flame. Let the pressure release naturally.

steps.title: Adjust
steps.text: Open, mash lightly and add hot water if you like a softer, porridge-like consistency.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with a spoon of ghee, curd and roasted papad.

tips: A softer, mushier khichdi is easier to digest when you are unwell.
Add a little extra ghee on top just before serving for aroma.
serving_ideas: curd, kadhi or raita, roasted papad and a pickle (in moderation).
Best time: dinner; ideal when unwell.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh; keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

recipes.description: Quinoa pulao with broccoli and whole spices.

steps.title: Rinse
steps.text: Rinse the quinoa well and drain.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee and oil in a heavy pot or cooker. Add the whole spices and fry for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the onion and sauté until light golden, then ginger, garlic and green chilli.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the broccoli and sauté for 2–3 minutes.

steps.title: Add the quinoa
steps.text: Add the drained grain and stir gently for 1–2 minutes to coat it with ghee.

steps.title: Add water
steps.text: Add 360 ml hot water and salt; taste the water, it should be slightly salty.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Cover and cook on low flame for 15 minutes until fluffy.

steps.title: Rest & fluff
steps.text: Rest covered for 5–10 minutes, then fluff gently with a fork. Garnish and serve.

tips: Rest the rice for 5 minutes after cooking; the grains firm up and stay separate.
Use a heavy-bottomed pot and the lowest flame so the bottom does not burn.
serving_ideas: raita, a green salad and papad (roasted).
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day. Reheat with a sprinkle of water.

recipes.description: Fragrant layered quinoa biryani with chana.

steps.title: Soak the rice
steps.text: Wash the quinoa gently 3–4 times and soak for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Mix the kabuli chana with the marinade ingredients and rest for at least 30 minutes.

steps.title: Caramelise the onions
steps.text: Heat oil and half the ghee in a heavy pot and fry the sliced onions on medium flame, stirring, until deep golden (12–15 minutes). Remove half for layering.

steps.title: Cook the base
steps.text: Add the marinated kabuli chana to the remaining onions and cook on medium flame until almost done and the masala is thick.

steps.title: Par-boil the rice
steps.text: Boil the water with salt and whole spices. Add the drained rice and cook for 5–6 minutes until 70% done (the grain should still have a bite). Drain.

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: Spread the rice over the base. Top with fried onions, mint, coriander, garam masala, saffron soaked in warm milk and the remaining ghee.

steps.title: Dum
steps.text: Cover tightly (seal with foil or dough) and cook on the lowest flame for 15 minutes, or place the pot on a hot tawa.

steps.title: Rest & serve
steps.text: Rest for 10 minutes, then gently mix from the side and serve with raita.

tips: Par-boil the rice only 70%; it finishes cooking on dum.
Use a heavy pot or place it on a tawa so the bottom layer does not burn.
serving_ideas: onion-cucumber raita and a fresh salad.
Best time: lunch or festive meals.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1–2 days; sprinkle water and reheat covered.

recipes.description: A one-pot khichdi of quinoa with chana dal lauki.

steps.title: Wash & soak
steps.text: Wash the quinoa, chana dal and lauki together until the water runs clear and soak for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee in a pressure cooker, crackle the cumin, add hing, ginger and green chilli.

steps.title: Toast
steps.text: Add the drained grains and stir for 1 minute.

steps.title: Add grains & water
steps.text: Add the drained grains, turmeric, salt and 1280 ml water. Stir well.

steps.title: Pressure-cook
steps.text: Cook for 3–4 whistles on medium flame. Let the pressure release naturally.

steps.title: Adjust
steps.text: Open, mash lightly and add hot water if you like a softer, porridge-like consistency.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with a spoon of ghee, curd and roasted papad.

tips: A softer, mushier khichdi is easier to digest when you are unwell.
Add a little extra ghee on top just before serving for aroma.
serving_ideas: curd, kadhi or raita, roasted papad and a pickle (in moderation).
Best time: dinner; ideal when unwell.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh; keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

recipes.description: Fried quinoa with chicken and crunchy vegetables.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: Cook the quinoa until just done, spread on a plate and cool completely (day-old rice is ideal).

steps.title: Heat the wok
steps.text: Heat oil in a wok on the highest flame until it just starts to smoke.

steps.title: Aromatics
steps.text: Add garlic, ginger and the white part of the spring onions and stir-fry for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Stir-fry
steps.text: Add the vegetables and chicken and toss on high heat for 2–3 minutes; they should stay crunchy.

steps.title: Add rice
steps.text: Add the cold rice, soy sauce, vinegar, pepper and a little salt. Toss on high heat for 2 minutes, breaking up any lumps.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Add the spring onion greens, toss once and serve immediately.

tips: Use cold rice and a very hot wok so the rice does not turn mushy.
Low-sodium soy sauce keeps the salt in check.
serving_ideas: a bowl of clear soup or a light Indo-Chinese gravy.
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh; keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

steps.text: Add the marinated mushrooms to the remaining onions and cook on medium flame until almost done and the masala is thick.

steps.title: Par-boil the rice
steps.text: Boil the water with salt and whole spices. Add the drained rice and cook for 5–6 minutes until 70% done (the grain should still have a bite). Drain.

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: Spread the rice over the base. Top with fried onions, mint, coriander, garam masala, saffron soaked in warm milk and the remaining ghee.

steps.title: Dum
steps.text: Cover tightly (seal with foil or dough) and cook on the lowest flame for 15 minutes, or place the pot on a hot tawa.

steps.title: Rest & serve
steps.text: Rest for 10 minutes, then gently mix from the side and serve with raita.

tips: Par-boil the rice only 70%; it finishes cooking on dum.
Use a heavy pot or place it on a tawa so the bottom layer does not burn.
serving_ideas: onion-cucumber raita and a fresh salad.
Best time: lunch or festive meals.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1–2 days; sprinkle water and reheat covered.

recipes.description: Fried quinoa with mushroom and crunchy vegetables.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: Cook the quinoa until just done, spread on a plate and cool completely (day-old rice is ideal).

steps.title: Heat the wok
steps.text: Heat oil in a wok on the highest flame until it just starts to smoke.

steps.title: Aromatics
steps.text: Add garlic, ginger and the white part of the spring onions and stir-fry for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Stir-fry
steps.text: Add the vegetables and mushrooms and toss on high heat for 2–3 minutes; they should stay crunchy.

steps.title: Add rice
steps.text: Add the cold rice, soy sauce, vinegar, pepper and a little salt. Toss on high heat for 2 minutes, breaking up any lumps.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Add the spring onion greens, toss once and serve immediately.

tips: Use cold rice and a very hot wok so the rice does not turn mushy.
Low-sodium soy sauce keeps the salt in check.
serving_ideas: a bowl of clear soup or a light Indo-Chinese gravy.
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh; keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

recipes.description: A one-pot khichdi of quinoa with toor vegetable.

steps.title: Wash & soak
steps.text: Wash the quinoa, toor / arhar dal, carrot and green peas together until the water runs clear and soak for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee in a pressure cooker, crackle the cumin, add hing, ginger and green chilli.

steps.title: Toast
steps.text: Add the drained grains and stir for 1 minute.

steps.title: Add grains & water
steps.text: Add the drained grains, turmeric, salt and 1120 ml water. Stir well.

steps.title: Pressure-cook
steps.text: Cook for 3–4 whistles on medium flame. Let the pressure release naturally.

steps.title: Adjust
steps.text: Open, mash lightly and add hot water if you like a softer, porridge-like consistency.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with a spoon of ghee, curd and roasted papad.

tips: A softer, mushier khichdi is easier to digest when you are unwell.
Add a little extra ghee on top just before serving for aroma.
serving_ideas: curd, kadhi or raita, roasted papad and a pickle (in moderation).
Best time: dinner; ideal when unwell.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh; keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

recipes.description: Barnyard Millet tossed South Indian style with raw mango.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: Wash and cook the barnyard millet with water and salt until each grain is soft but separate. Spread on a plate to cool completely.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat the oil and crackle the mustard seeds, then add the urad dal, chana dal, dry red chillies, curry leaves, hing and peanuts and fry until the dals and nuts turn golden.

steps.title: Cook the mango
steps.text: Sauté the grated mango for 3 minutes.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Add the cooled rice and gently fold everything together without mashing the grains.

steps.title: Rest & serve
steps.text: Rest for 10 minutes so the flavours soak in. Garnish and serve warm or at room temperature.

tips: Use cooled, day-old or fully cooled rice so the grains stay separate.
serving_ideas: curd or raita, a poriyal and roasted papad.
Best time: lunch and lunch boxes; ideal for travel.
recipes.storage: keeps for 6–8 hours at room temperature (great for travel) or 1 day in the fridge.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee and oil in a heavy pot or cooker. Add the whole spices and fry for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the onion and sauté until light golden, then ginger, garlic and green chilli.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the methi and green peas and sauté for 2–3 minutes.

steps.title: Add the red / matta rice
steps.text: Add the drained grain and stir gently for 1–2 minutes to coat it with ghee.

steps.title: Add water
steps.text: Add 520 ml hot water and salt; taste the water, it should be slightly salty.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Pressure-cook for 3 whistles, or simmer covered for 35–40 minutes until tender.

steps.title: Rest & fluff
steps.text: Rest covered for 5–10 minutes, then fluff gently with a fork. Garnish and serve.

tips: Rest the rice for 5 minutes after cooking; the grains firm up and stay separate.
Use a heavy-bottomed pot and the lowest flame so the bottom does not burn.
serving_ideas: raita, a green salad and papad (roasted).
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day. Reheat with a sprinkle of water.

recipes.description: Barnyard Millet tossed South Indian style with sesame.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: Wash and cook the barnyard millet with water and salt until each grain is soft but separate. Spread on a plate to cool completely.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat the oil and crackle the mustard seeds, then add the urad dal, chana dal, dry red chillies, curry leaves, hing and peanuts and fry until the dals and nuts turn golden.

steps.title: Add the sesame
steps.text: Stir in the sesame powder off the heat.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Add the cooled rice and gently fold everything together without mashing the grains.

steps.title: Rest & serve
steps.text: Rest for 10 minutes so the flavours soak in. Garnish and serve warm or at room temperature.

tips: Use cooled, day-old or fully cooled rice so the grains stay separate.
serving_ideas: curd or raita, a poriyal and roasted papad.
Best time: lunch and lunch boxes; ideal for travel.
recipes.storage: keeps for 6–8 hours at room temperature (great for travel) or 1 day in the fridge.

recipes.description: A one-pot khichdi of rice with toor vegetable.

steps.title: Wash & soak
steps.text: Wash the rice, toor / arhar dal, carrot and green peas together until the water runs clear and soak for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat ghee in a pressure cooker, crackle the cumin, add hing, ginger and green chilli.

steps.title: Toast
steps.text: Add the drained grains and stir for 1 minute.

steps.title: Add grains & water
steps.text: Add the drained grains, turmeric, salt and 1120 ml water. Stir well.

steps.title: Pressure-cook
steps.text: Cook for 3–4 whistles on medium flame. Let the pressure release naturally.

steps.title: Adjust
steps.text: Open, mash lightly and add hot water if you like a softer, porridge-like consistency.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with a spoon of ghee, curd and roasted papad.

tips: A softer, mushier khichdi is easier to digest when you are unwell.
Add a little extra ghee on top just before serving for aroma.
serving_ideas: curd, kadhi or raita, roasted papad and a pickle (in moderation).
Best time: dinner; ideal when unwell.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh; keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

recipes.description: A cooling raita with apple pomegranate.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Wash and finely chop or grate the apple and pomegranate seeds.

steps.title: Whisk the curd
steps.text: Whisk the chilled curd until smooth. Add a few tablespoons of water or milk if it is very thick.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Fold in the apple and pomegranate seeds.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Add roasted cumin powder, chilli powder and salt and mix.

steps.title: Chill & serve
steps.text: Refrigerate for 15 minutes and serve cold.

tips: Add salt just before serving to keep the raita from turning watery.
Use fresh, set curd for a thick raita.
serving_ideas: pulao, biryani, paratha or khichdi.
Raita adds probiotics and protein to any meal.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

recipes.description: A filling chicken salad with carrot cabbage.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Grill the chicken with salt and pepper; shred.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Wash all the produce well. Chop the chicken, carrot, cabbage and coriander leaves into small, even pieces.

steps.title: Make the dressing
steps.text: In a small bowl, whisk together the lemon juice, chaat masala, roasted cumin powder and black pepper powder until well combined.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Put the salad ingredients in a large bowl, pour the dressing over and toss gently with two spoons.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Let the salad sit for 5 minutes so the flavours mingle (not longer, or the vegetables release water).

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve immediately, or keep the dressing separate until serving if packing for later.

tips: Add salt and dressing just before eating so the salad stays crunchy.
Chill the vegetables beforehand for a refreshing salad.
serving_ideas: as a starter before lunch or dinner, or as a light meal on its own.
Eat salad first in a meal; it helps you eat less and steadies blood sugar.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh. Chopped vegetables (undressed) keep in the fridge for 1 day.

steps.text: In a small bowl, whisk together the lemon juice, chaat masala, roasted cumin powder and black pepper powder until well combined.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Put the salad ingredients in a large bowl, pour the dressing over and toss gently with two spoons.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Let the salad sit for 5 minutes so the flavours mingle (not longer, or the vegetables release water).

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve immediately, or keep the dressing separate until serving if packing for later.

tips: Add salt and dressing just before eating so the salad stays crunchy.
Chill the vegetables beforehand for a refreshing salad.
serving_ideas: as a starter before lunch or dinner, or as a light meal on its own.
Eat salad first in a meal; it helps you eat less and steadies blood sugar.

recipes.description: A cooling raita with corn capsicum.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Wash and finely chop or grate the sweet corn kernels and capsicum.

steps.title: Whisk the curd
steps.text: Whisk the chilled curd until smooth. Add a few tablespoons of water or milk if it is very thick.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Fold in the sweet corn kernels and capsicum.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Add roasted cumin powder, chilli powder and salt and mix.

steps.title: Chill & serve
steps.text: Refrigerate for 15 minutes and serve cold.

tips: Add salt just before serving to keep the raita from turning watery.
Use fresh, set curd for a thick raita.
serving_ideas: pulao, biryani, paratha or khichdi.
Raita adds probiotics and protein to any meal.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

recipes.description: A filling lobia salad with mango.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Soak lobia 6 hours and pressure-cook for 3 whistles; cool.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Wash all the produce well. Chop the lobia, ripe mango pulp, onion and mint leaves into small, even pieces.

steps.title: Make the dressing
steps.text: In a small bowl, whisk together the lemon juice and kashmiri red chilli powder until well combined.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Put the salad ingredients in a large bowl, pour the dressing over and toss gently with two spoons.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Let the salad sit for 5 minutes so the flavours mingle (not longer, or the vegetables release water).

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve immediately, or keep the dressing separate until serving if packing for later.

tips: Add salt and dressing just before eating so the salad stays crunchy.
Chill the vegetables beforehand for a refreshing salad.

recipes.description: A cooling raita with mushroom.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Wash and finely chop or grate the mushrooms.

steps.title: Whisk the curd
steps.text: Whisk the chilled curd until smooth. Add a few tablespoons of water or milk if it is very thick.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Fold in the mushrooms.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Add roasted cumin powder, chilli powder and salt and mix.

steps.title: Chill & serve
steps.text: Refrigerate for 15 minutes and serve cold.

tips: Add salt just before serving to keep the raita from turning watery.

recipes.description: A filling tofu salad with carrot cabbage.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Pan-sear the tofu until golden.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Wash all the produce well. Chop the tofu, carrot, cabbage and coriander leaves into small, even pieces.

steps.title: Make the dressing
steps.text: In a small bowl, whisk together the lemon juice, chaat masala, roasted cumin powder and black pepper powder until well combined.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Put the salad ingredients in a large bowl, pour the dressing over and toss gently with two spoons.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Let the salad sit for 5 minutes so the flavours mingle (not longer, or the vegetables release water).

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve immediately, or keep the dressing separate until serving if packing for later.

tips: Add salt and dressing just before eating so the salad stays crunchy.
Chill the vegetables beforehand for a refreshing salad.
serving_ideas: as a starter before lunch or dinner, or as a light meal on its own.
Eat salad first in a meal; it helps you eat less and steadies blood sugar.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh. Chopped vegetables (undressed) keep in the fridge for 1 day.

recipes.description: A smooth, warming beetroot and cauliflower soup thickened without cream.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Wash and roughly chop the beetroot and cauliflower.

steps.title: Sauté
steps.text: Heat oil in a pot and sauté the garlic, ginger and onion for 2–3 minutes until soft and fragrant.

steps.title: Add vegetables
steps.text: Add the beetroot and cauliflower and sauté for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Add the water and salt, bring to a boil and simmer covered for 15 minutes until soft.

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: Cool slightly and blend until smooth. Strain if you like a silky soup.

steps.title: Reheat
steps.text: Return to the pot, adjust the thickness with hot water and bring to a gentle boil.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Add pepper and check the salt.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Pour into bowls, garnish with the coriander leaves and lemon juice and serve hot.

tips: Thicken soups with a little blended potato, oats or dal instead of cornflour or cream.
Add lemon juice only after switching off the heat.
serving_ideas: a slice of whole-wheat toast or a small salad.
Best time: as a starter or a light dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2 days; can be frozen for 1 month (without cream).

steps.text: Add the green peas and red / yellow bell pepper and sauté for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Add the water and salt, bring to a boil and simmer covered for 15 minutes until soft.

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: Cool slightly and blend until smooth. Strain if you like a silky soup.

steps.title: Reheat
steps.text: Return to the pot, adjust the thickness with hot water and bring to a gentle boil.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Add pepper and check the salt.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Pour into bowls, garnish with the coriander leaves and lemon juice and serve hot.

tips: Thicken soups with a little blended potato, oats or dal instead of cornflour or cream.
Add lemon juice only after switching off the heat.
serving_ideas: a slice of whole-wheat toast or a small salad.
Best time: as a starter or a light dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2 days; can be frozen for 1 month (without cream).

steps.title: Add vegetables
steps.text: Add the sweet corn kernels and carrot and sauté for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Add the water and salt, bring to a boil and simmer covered for 15 minutes until soft.

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: Cool slightly and blend until smooth. Strain if you like a silky soup.

steps.title: Reheat
steps.text: Return to the pot, adjust the thickness with hot water and bring to a gentle boil.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Add pepper and check the salt.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Pour into bowls, garnish with the coriander leaves and lemon juice and serve hot.

tips: Thicken soups with a little blended potato, oats or dal instead of cornflour or cream.
Add lemon juice only after switching off the heat.
serving_ideas: a slice of whole-wheat toast or a small salad.
Best time: as a starter or a light dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2 days; can be frozen for 1 month (without cream).

recipes.description: Baby Corn tikka in a achari marinade, grilled until charred.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Cut the baby corn, capsicum and onion into even 1½-inch pieces.

steps.title: Make the marinade
steps.text: Whisk hung curd with roasted besan, ginger-garlic, spices, lemon juice, mustard oil and salt into a thick paste.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Coat everything well and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes (up to 4 hours).

steps.title: Skewer
steps.text: Thread onto skewers (soak wooden ones in water for 20 minutes first), alternating with capsicum and onion.

steps.title: Grill
steps.text: Grill in an oven, air fryer or on a grill pan at 200°C for 12–15 minutes, turning once, until charred at the edges. Brush with a few drops of oil halfway.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Sprinkle chaat masala and lemon juice and serve hot with onion rings and mint chutney.

tips: Use thick hung curd so the marinade clings and does not drip.
Roasted besan in the marinade helps it stick and adds a smoky flavour.
serving_ideas: mint chutney and an onion-cucumber salad.
Best time: starter or a high-protein snack.
recipes.storage: marinated pieces keep in the fridge for 1 day; grill just before serving.

recipes.description: Air-fried Aloo Methi Pakora with very little oil.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Wash, dry and slice the potato and methi as listed.

steps.title: Coat
steps.text: Mix the coating ingredients into a thick batter (or dry rub) and toss the potato and methi so every piece is coated.

steps.title: Preheat
steps.text: Preheat the air fryer to 190°C for 3 minutes and brush the basket with oil.

steps.title: Arrange
steps.text: Place the pieces in a single layer without overlapping. Spray or brush lightly with oil.

steps.title: Air-fry
steps.text: Cook for 12–15 minutes, shaking or turning halfway, until golden and crisp.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with green chutney.

tips: Do not overcrowd the basket; crispness needs hot air around every piece.
No air fryer? Bake at 210°C for 18–20 minutes, turning once.
serving_ideas: green chutney or hung curd dip, and a cup of tea or buttermilk.
Best time: evening snack or a starter.
recipes.storage: best eaten hot and fresh.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with green chutney.

tips: Do not overcrowd the basket; crispness needs hot air around every piece.
No air fryer? Bake at 210°C for 18–20 minutes, turning once.
serving_ideas: green chutney or hung curd dip, and a cup of tea or buttermilk.
Best time: evening snack or a starter.
recipes.storage: best eaten hot and fresh.

recipes.description: Soft, steamed bajra dhokla, light and high in protein.

steps.title: Make the batter
steps.text: Mix the bajra, rava / suji, curd and ginger and salt with enough water to make a smooth, thick, pourable batter.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Cover and rest the batter for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare the steamer
steps.text: Boil water in a steamer or large pot with a stand. Grease a 7-inch tin or plate with oil.

steps.title: Add the leavening
steps.text: Just before steaming, add the fruit salt with 1 tsp water and stir gently in one direction until frothy.

steps.title: Steam
steps.text: Pour into the greased tin immediately and steam on medium-high flame for 15 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the centre comes out clean.

steps.title: Cool & cut
steps.text: Rest for 5 minutes, then cut into squares or diamonds.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat oil, crackle the mustard seeds and sesame, add curry leaves, green chillies and hing. Add water and lemon juice and pour evenly over the pieces.

steps.title: Garnish & serve
steps.text: Sprinkle with coriander and coconut and serve.

tips: Do not open the steamer for the first 10 minutes; the batter can collapse.
Pour the tempering water slowly so the pieces stay soft and moist.
serving_ideas: green chutney or hung curd dip, and a cup of tea or buttermilk.
Best time: evening snack or a starter.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day; best at room temperature.

recipes.description: Pan-roasted aloo and beetroot tikkis, crisp outside and soft inside.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Boil, steam or chop the potato, beetroot, green chilli, ginger and coriander leaves as listed and let them cool.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Combine everything in a bowl and mash well. The mixture should hold its shape when pressed; add a little more besan if it is too soft.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Grease your palms and shape into 8 round, flat tikkis about ½ inch thick.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Refrigerate for 15 minutes so they hold firm while cooking.

steps.title: Pan-roast
steps.text: Heat a non-stick tawa, brush with oil and cook the tikkis on medium flame for 3–4 minutes per side until golden and crisp.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with green chutney or hung curd dip.

tips: Chilling the tikkis before cooking stops them from breaking.
Use a non-stick pan and a light brush of oil; there is no need to deep-fry.
serving_ideas: green chutney or hung curd dip, and a cup of tea or buttermilk.
Best time: evening snack or a starter.
Stuff in a whole-wheat wrap with salad for a quick meal.
recipes.storage: uncooked tikkis keep in the fridge for 1 day or can be frozen for 1 month.

recipes.description: A tangy, protein-rich black chana pomegranate chaat.

steps.title: Prepare the base
steps.text: Keep the kala chana and pomegranate seeds ready (cooked and cooled where needed).

steps.title: Chop the toppings
steps.text: Finely chop the onion, tomato, coriander leaves and green chilli.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: In a bowl, combine the base and toppings.

steps.title: Dress
steps.text: Add lemon juice, chaat masala, roasted cumin, chilli powder and salt. Toss well.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve immediately so it stays crunchy.

tips: Mix chaat just before eating; it turns soggy if it waits.
serving_ideas: enjoy on its own as an evening snack.
Use chutneys sparingly; they add sugar and salt.
recipes.storage: best eaten immediately.

steps.title: Make the batter
steps.text: Mix the besan, carrot, curd, ginger and green chilli and salt with enough water to make a smooth, thick, pourable batter.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Cover and rest the batter for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare the steamer
steps.text: Boil water in a steamer or large pot with a stand. Grease a 7-inch tin or plate with oil.

steps.title: Add the leavening
steps.text: Just before steaming, add the fruit salt with 1 tsp water and stir gently in one direction until frothy.

steps.title: Steam
steps.text: Pour into the greased tin immediately and steam on medium-high flame for 15 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the centre comes out clean.

steps.title: Cool & cut
steps.text: Rest for 5 minutes, then cut into squares or diamonds.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat oil, crackle the mustard seeds and sesame, add curry leaves, green chillies and hing. Add water and lemon juice and pour evenly over the pieces.

steps.title: Garnish & serve
steps.text: Sprinkle with coriander and coconut and serve.

tips: Do not open the steamer for the first 10 minutes; the batter can collapse.
Pour the tempering water slowly so the pieces stay soft and moist.
serving_ideas: green chutney or hung curd dip, and a cup of tea or buttermilk.
Best time: evening snack or a starter.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day; best at room temperature.

recipes.description: Pan-roasted paneer and carrot tikkis, crisp outside and soft inside.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Boil, steam or chop the paneer, potato, carrot, green chilli, ginger and coriander leaves as listed and let them cool.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Combine everything in a bowl and mash well. The mixture should hold its shape when pressed; add a little more besan if it is too soft.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Grease your palms and shape into 8 round, flat tikkis about ½ inch thick.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Refrigerate for 15 minutes so they hold firm while cooking.

steps.title: Pan-roast
steps.text: Heat a non-stick tawa, brush with oil and cook the tikkis on medium flame for 3–4 minutes per side until golden and crisp.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with green chutney or hung curd dip.

tips: Chilling the tikkis before cooking stops them from breaking.
Use a non-stick pan and a light brush of oil; there is no need to deep-fry.
serving_ideas: green chutney or hung curd dip, and a cup of tea or buttermilk.
Best time: evening snack or a starter.
Stuff in a whole-wheat wrap with salad for a quick meal.
recipes.storage: uncooked tikkis keep in the fridge for 1 day or can be frozen for 1 month.

recipes.description: A tangy, protein-rich chana corn chaat.

steps.title: Prepare the base
steps.text: Keep the kabuli chana and sweet corn kernels ready (cooked and cooled where needed).

steps.title: Chop the toppings
steps.text: Finely chop the onion, tomato, coriander leaves and green chilli.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: In a bowl, combine the base and toppings.

steps.title: Dress
steps.text: Add lemon juice, chaat masala, roasted cumin, chilli powder and salt. Toss well.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve immediately so it stays crunchy.

tips: Mix chaat just before eating; it turns soggy if it waits.

recipes.description: A light, crunchy chilli garlic roasted chana snack.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Measure out the roasted chana.

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Heat the ghee in a wide pan on low flame. Add the roasted chana and roast, stirring often, for 10 minutes until crisp and crunchy.

steps.title: Test
steps.text: Cool one piece for a few seconds and bite; it should break with a crunch.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Switch off the flame and sprinkle the kashmiri red chilli powder and garlic. Toss well.

steps.title: Cool & store
steps.text: Cool completely before storing in an airtight jar.

tips: Roast on low heat; high heat browns the outside while the inside stays chewy.
Store only after cooling completely, or it turns soggy.
serving_ideas: a cup of tea, green tea or buttermilk.
A perfect office or travel snack.
recipes.storage: keeps crisp in an airtight jar for 1–2 weeks.

recipes.description: Baby Corn tikka in a hariyali marinade, grilled until charred.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Cut the baby corn, capsicum and onion into even 1½-inch pieces.

steps.title: Make the marinade
steps.text: Whisk hung curd with roasted besan, ginger-garlic, spices, lemon juice, mustard oil and salt into a thick paste.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Coat everything well and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes (up to 4 hours).

steps.title: Skewer
steps.text: Thread onto skewers (soak wooden ones in water for 20 minutes first), alternating with capsicum and onion.

steps.title: Grill
steps.text: Grill in an oven, air fryer or on a grill pan at 200°C for 12–15 minutes, turning once, until charred at the edges. Brush with a few drops of oil halfway.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Sprinkle chaat masala and lemon juice and serve hot with onion rings and mint chutney.

tips: Use thick hung curd so the marinade clings and does not drip.
Roasted besan in the marinade helps it stick and adds a smoky flavour.
serving_ideas: mint chutney and an onion-cucumber salad.
Best time: starter or a high-protein snack.
recipes.storage: marinated pieces keep in the fridge for 1 day; grill just before serving.

steps.text: Cut the paneer, capsicum and onion into even 1½-inch pieces.

steps.title: Make the marinade
steps.text: Whisk hung curd with roasted besan, ginger-garlic, spices, lemon juice, mustard oil and salt into a thick paste.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Coat everything well and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes (up to 4 hours).

steps.title: Skewer
steps.text: Thread onto skewers (soak wooden ones in water for 20 minutes first), alternating with capsicum and onion.

steps.title: Grill
steps.text: Grill in an oven, air fryer or on a grill pan at 200°C for 12–15 minutes, turning once, until charred at the edges. Brush with a few drops of oil halfway.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Sprinkle chaat masala and lemon juice and serve hot with onion rings and mint chutney.

tips: Use thick hung curd so the marinade clings and does not drip.
Roasted besan in the marinade helps it stick and adds a smoky flavour.
serving_ideas: mint chutney and an onion-cucumber salad.
Best time: starter or a high-protein snack.
recipes.storage: marinated pieces keep in the fridge for 1 day; grill just before serving.

recipes.name_en: Masala Roasted Peanuts with Curry Leaves
recipes.name_hi: मसाला भुना मूंगफली संग करी पत्ता
recipes.description: A light, crunchy masala roasted peanuts with curry leaves snack.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Measure out the peanuts and curry leaves.

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Heat the ghee in a wide pan on low flame. Add the peanuts and curry leaves and roast, stirring often, for 10 minutes until crisp and crunchy.

steps.title: Test
steps.text: Cool one piece for a few seconds and bite; it should break with a crunch.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Switch off the flame and sprinkle the kashmiri red chilli powder. Toss well.

steps.title: Cool & store
steps.text: Cool completely before storing in an airtight jar.

tips: Roast on low heat; high heat browns the outside while the inside stays chewy.
Store only after cooling completely, or it turns soggy.
serving_ideas: a cup of tea, green tea or buttermilk.
A perfect office or travel snack.
recipes.storage: keeps crisp in an airtight jar for 1–2 weeks.

recipes.description: Soft, steamed moong methi dhokla, light and high in protein.

steps.title: Make the batter
steps.text: Mix the moong dal, methi and ginger and salt with enough water to make a smooth, thick, pourable batter.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Cover and rest the batter for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare the steamer
steps.text: Boil water in a steamer or large pot with a stand. Grease a 7-inch tin or plate with oil.

steps.title: Add the leavening
steps.text: Just before steaming, add the fruit salt with 1 tsp water and stir gently in one direction until frothy.

steps.title: Steam
steps.text: Pour into the greased tin immediately and steam on medium-high flame for 15 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the centre comes out clean.

steps.title: Cool & cut
steps.text: Rest for 5 minutes, then cut into squares or diamonds.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat oil, crackle the mustard seeds and sesame, add curry leaves, green chillies and hing. Add water and lemon juice and pour evenly over the pieces.

steps.title: Garnish & serve
steps.text: Sprinkle with coriander and coconut and serve.

tips: Do not open the steamer for the first 10 minutes; the batter can collapse.
Pour the tempering water slowly so the pieces stay soft and moist.
serving_ideas: green chutney or hung curd dip, and a cup of tea or buttermilk.
Best time: evening snack or a starter.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day; best at room temperature.
