recipes.description: Pan-roasted aloo and mushroom tikkis, crisp outside and soft inside.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Boil, steam or chop the potato, mushrooms, green chilli, ginger and coriander leaves as listed and let them cool.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Combine everything in a bowl and mash well. The mixture should hold its shape when pressed; add a little more besan if it is too soft.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Grease your palms and shape into 8 round, flat tikkis about ½ inch thick.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Refrigerate for 15 minutes so they hold firm while cooking.

steps.title: Pan-roast
steps.text: Heat a non-stick tawa, brush with oil and cook the tikkis on medium flame for 3–4 minutes per side until golden and crisp.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with green chutney or hung curd dip.

tips: Chilling the tikkis before cooking stops them from breaking.
Use a non-stick pan and a light brush of oil; there is no need to deep-fry.
serving_ideas: green chutney or hung curd dip, and a cup of tea or buttermilk.
Best time: evening snack or a starter.
Stuff in a whole-wheat wrap with salad for a quick meal.
recipes.storage: uncooked tikkis keep in the fridge for 1 day or can be frozen for 1 month.

recipes.description: Soft, steamed oats carrot dhokla, light and high in protein.

steps.title: Make the batter
steps.text: Mix the rolled oats, rava / suji, curd and carrot and salt with enough water to make a smooth, thick, pourable batter.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Cover and rest the batter for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare the steamer
steps.text: Boil water in a steamer or large pot with a stand. Grease a 7-inch tin or plate with oil.

steps.title: Add the leavening
steps.text: Just before steaming, add the fruit salt with 1 tsp water and stir gently in one direction until frothy.

steps.title: Steam
steps.text: Pour into the greased tin immediately and steam on medium-high flame for 15 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the centre comes out clean.

steps.title: Cool & cut
steps.text: Rest for 5 minutes, then cut into squares or diamonds.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat oil, crackle the mustard seeds and sesame, add curry leaves, green chillies and hing. Add water and lemon juice and pour evenly over the pieces.

steps.title: Garnish & serve
steps.text: Sprinkle with coriander and coconut and serve.

tips: Do not open the steamer for the first 10 minutes; the batter can collapse.
Pour the tempering water slowly so the pieces stay soft and moist.
serving_ideas: green chutney or hung curd dip, and a cup of tea or buttermilk.
Best time: evening snack or a starter.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day; best at room temperature.

recipes.description: Baby Corn tikka in a pudina marinade, grilled until charred.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Cut the baby corn, capsicum and onion into even 1½-inch pieces.

steps.title: Make the marinade
steps.text: Whisk hung curd with roasted besan, ginger-garlic, spices, lemon juice, mustard oil and salt into a thick paste.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Coat everything well and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes (up to 4 hours).

steps.title: Skewer
steps.text: Thread onto skewers (soak wooden ones in water for 20 minutes first), alternating with capsicum and onion.

steps.title: Grill
steps.text: Grill in an oven, air fryer or on a grill pan at 200°C for 12–15 minutes, turning once, until charred at the edges. Brush with a few drops of oil halfway.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Sprinkle chaat masala and lemon juice and serve hot with onion rings and mint chutney.

tips: Use thick hung curd so the marinade clings and does not drip.
Roasted besan in the marinade helps it stick and adds a smoky flavour.
serving_ideas: mint chutney and an onion-cucumber salad.
Best time: starter or a high-protein snack.
recipes.storage: marinated pieces keep in the fridge for 1 day; grill just before serving.

recipes.description: A light, crunchy roasted soya nuts snack.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Measure out the soya chunks.

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Heat the ghee in a wide pan on low flame. Add the soya chunks and roast, stirring often, for 10 minutes until crisp and crunchy.

steps.title: Test
steps.text: Cool one piece for a few seconds and bite; it should break with a crunch.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Switch off the flame and sprinkle the chaat masala and kashmiri red chilli powder. Toss well.

steps.title: Cool & store
steps.text: Cool completely before storing in an airtight jar.

tips: Roast on low heat; high heat browns the outside while the inside stays chewy.
Store only after cooling completely, or it turns soggy.
serving_ideas: a cup of tea, green tea or buttermilk.
A perfect office or travel snack.
recipes.storage: keeps crisp in an airtight jar for 1–2 weeks.

recipes.description: Boiled eggs slow-cooked handi-style with curd and whole spices.

steps.title: Boil the eggs
steps.text: Boil the eggs for 10 minutes, cool in cold water and peel. Make shallow slits on each so the masala soaks in.

steps.title: Roast the eggs
steps.text: Toss the eggs in ½ tsp oil with a pinch of turmeric and chilli for 2 minutes until lightly golden. Set aside.

steps.title: Make the gravy
steps.text: Heat oil with cumin, bay leaf and cardamom. Sauté the onion until golden, add ginger and garlic, then tomato purée and spices, and cook until thick. Lower the flame and stir in the whisked curd.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Add water to the consistency you like, add salt and simmer for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Add the eggs
steps.text: Add the eggs and simmer for 4–5 minutes so they absorb the flavours.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with coriander and serve hot.

tips: Slit the boiled eggs so the gravy flavours them all the way through.
serving_ideas: phulka, jeera rice or brown rice, with a salad and curd.
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 1 day.

recipes.description: Chicken curry cooked with arbi.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Wash and drain the chicken. Mix with the marinade ingredients and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes (overnight is best).

steps.title: Make the masala
steps.text: Heat oil, add the whole spices and fry for 30 seconds. Add the onion and sauté for 10–12 minutes until deep golden. Add ginger, garlic and chilli, then the tomato purée and powdered spices, and cook until the oil separates.

steps.title: Add the chicken
steps.text: Add the marinated chicken and cook on high flame for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until it changes colour and is coated in masala.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Add water as needed, cover and simmer on low flame for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is tender and cooked through.

steps.title: Check
steps.text: The chicken is done when the juices run clear and there is no pink near the bone.

steps.title: Finish & serve
steps.text: Add the coriander leaves and serve hot.

tips: Use skinless chicken to cut saturated fat.
Simmer gently; boiling hard makes chicken tough.
serving_ideas: phulka, jeera rice or brown rice, with a salad and curd.
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2 days; freezes for 1 month.

recipes.description: Chicken in a kalimirch marinade, grilled until charred at the edges.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Clean the chicken, pat dry and make deep slits so the marinade penetrates.

steps.title: First marinade
steps.text: Rub with lemon juice, salt and chilli and rest for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Second marinade
steps.text: Mix the remaining marinade ingredients into a thick paste, coat well and refrigerate for at least 2 hours (overnight is best).

steps.title: Preheat
steps.text: Preheat the oven or air fryer to 200°C.

steps.title: Grill
steps.text: Grill for 15–20 minutes, turning once and brushing with a few drops of oil, until charred at the edges and cooked through.

steps.title: Rest & serve
steps.text: Rest for 3 minutes, sprinkle chaat masala and lemon and serve with onion rings and mint chutney.

tips: Hung curd marinade keeps the meat juicy without frying.
Check doneness at the thickest part; there should be no pink.
serving_ideas: mint chutney, onion rings and a green salad.
Best time: a high-protein starter or dinner.
recipes.storage: marinated meat keeps in the fridge for 1 day; cooked tikka keeps 1 day.

recipes.description: Homestyle mutton slow-cooked with arbi, a classic North Indian pairing.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Wash the mutton, drain well and mix with the marinade. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight.

steps.title: Make the masala
steps.text: Heat oil, add the whole spices, then the onions, and sauté until deep golden (12–15 minutes). Add ginger and garlic, then the tomato purée and powdered spices, and cook until the oil separates. Add the arbi for the last 15 minutes.

steps.title: Bhuno
steps.text: Add the marinated mutton and cook on high flame, stirring often, for 8–10 minutes until it is well coated and the masala starts to stick.

steps.title: Pressure-cook
steps.text: Add 1½ cups hot water and pressure-cook for 5–6 whistles on medium flame (or simmer covered for 1½ hours) until the mutton is tender.

steps.title: Reduce
steps.text: Open the cooker and simmer uncovered to the consistency you like.

steps.title: Finish & serve
steps.text: Skim off any surface fat, add the coriander leaves and serve hot.

tips: Choose lean cuts and trim visible fat to lower saturated fat.
Skim the fat that rises after cooking; it makes a big difference.
serving_ideas: phulka, jeera rice or brown rice, with a salad and curd.
Best time: lunch or dinner.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2 days; tastes better the next day. Freezes for 1 month.

recipes.description: Mutton in a hariyali marinade, grilled until charred at the edges.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Clean the mutton, pat dry and make deep slits so the marinade penetrates.

steps.title: First marinade
steps.text: Rub with lemon juice, salt and chilli and rest for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Second marinade
steps.text: Mix the remaining marinade ingredients into a thick paste, coat well and refrigerate for at least 2 hours (overnight is best).

steps.title: Preheat
steps.text: Preheat the oven or air fryer to 200°C.

steps.title: Grill
steps.text: Grill for 25–30 minutes, turning once and brushing with a few drops of oil, until charred at the edges and cooked through.

steps.title: Rest & serve
steps.text: Rest for 3 minutes, sprinkle chaat masala and lemon and serve with onion rings and mint chutney.

tips: Hung curd marinade keeps the meat juicy without frying.
Check doneness at the thickest part; there should be no pink.
serving_ideas: mint chutney, onion rings and a green salad.
Best time: a high-protein starter or dinner.
recipes.storage: marinated meat keeps in the fridge for 1 day; cooked tikka keeps 1 day.

recipes.description: Fish in a creamy black pepper gravy.

steps.title: Clean & season
steps.text: Wash the fish fillets well, pat dry and rub with turmeric, chilli and salt. Rest for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Sear (optional)
steps.text: Lightly sear the pieces in a non-stick pan with a few drops of oil for 1 minute per side; this helps them hold their shape.

steps.title: Make the curry
steps.text: Sauté the onion paste and ginger-garlic, add the crushed pepper and cashew paste, then the whisked curd, and simmer.

steps.title: Boil
steps.text: Add water as needed, check the salt and bring to a gentle boil.

steps.title: Add the fish
steps.text: Slide in the pieces in a single layer. Simmer for 8 minutes without stirring; swirl the pan gently instead.

steps.title: Rest & serve
steps.text: Switch off, cover and rest for 10 minutes so the flavours develop. Serve hot.

tips: Do not stir after adding the fish; swirl the pan so the pieces stay whole.
Fish cooks fast; it is done when it flakes easily.
serving_ideas: steamed rice or red rice, with a vegetable side.
Best time: lunch.

recipes.description: Mackerel coated in a garlic masala and pan-fried until crisp.

steps.title: Clean
steps.text: Wash the mackerel, pat completely dry and make shallow slits.

steps.title: Make the masala
steps.text: Mix the masala ingredients into a thick paste with lemon juice (no water).

steps.title: Coat
steps.text: Rub the paste all over the fish, into the slits, and rest for 20–30 minutes.

steps.title: Heat the pan
steps.text: Heat a non-stick or cast-iron tawa on medium flame and brush with oil.

steps.title: Shallow-fry
steps.text: Place the fish and cook for 3–4 minutes per side, drizzling a little oil around, until crisp and cooked through.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve hot with onion rings and lemon wedges.

tips: Pat the fish completely dry; moisture stops it from crisping.
Flip only once to keep the pieces whole.
serving_ideas: onion rings, lemon wedges and rice with dal or rasam.
Best time: lunch.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh.

recipes.description: Pomfret in a tangy Hyderabadi peanut-sesame-coconut salan.

steps.title: Clean & season
steps.text: Wash the pomfret well, pat dry and rub with turmeric, chilli and salt. Rest for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Sear (optional)
steps.text: Lightly sear the pieces in a non-stick pan with a few drops of oil for 1 minute per side; this helps them hold their shape.

steps.text: Roast the peanuts, sesame and coconut and grind with onion into a smooth paste. Heat oil, add cumin, curry leaves and ginger-garlic, then the paste, spices, tamarind, jaggery and water, and simmer until thick.

steps.title: Boil
steps.text: Add water as needed, check the salt and bring to a gentle boil.

steps.title: Add the fish

steps.text: Clean the prawns, pat dry and make deep slits so the marinade penetrates.

steps.title: First marinade
steps.text: Rub with lemon juice, salt and chilli and rest for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Second marinade
steps.text: Mix the remaining marinade ingredients into a thick paste, coat well and refrigerate for at least 2 hours (overnight is best).

steps.title: Preheat
steps.text: Preheat the oven or air fryer to 200°C.

steps.title: Grill
steps.text: Grill for 8–13 minutes, turning once and brushing with a few drops of oil, until charred at the edges and cooked through.

steps.title: Rest & serve
steps.text: Rest for 3 minutes, sprinkle chaat masala and lemon and serve with onion rings and mint chutney.

tips: Hung curd marinade keeps the meat juicy without frying.
Check doneness at the thickest part; there should be no pink.
serving_ideas: mint chutney, onion rings and a green salad.
Best time: a high-protein starter or dinner.
recipes.storage: marinated meat keeps in the fridge for 1 day; cooked tikka keeps 1 day.

recipes.description: Sugar-free almond ladoos bound with date coconut.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Roast and chop the almond; blend the date coconut.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: In a large bowl, mix the almonds, dates, grated coconut and cardamom powder together well.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: While still warm, take a spoonful and press firmly between your palms into a round ladoo.

steps.title: Set
steps.text: Place on a plate and let them firm up for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Store
steps.text: Store in an airtight box.

tips: If the mixture does not bind, add 1–2 tsp warm ghee or a little more date paste.
Make them small; one ladoo is a satisfying portion.
serving_ideas: one ladoo with a glass of milk, or as a pre-workout snack.
Great for children’s tiffin and for travel.
recipes.storage: keeps in an airtight box for 1–2 weeks (ladoos with fresh coconut: 5 days in the fridge).

recipes.description: A ash gourd dates halwa sweetened with dates instead of sugar.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Prepare the ash gourd as listed.

steps.title: Sauté
steps.text: Heat the ghee in a heavy kadhai and sauté the ash gourd for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Add the liquid
steps.text: Add the toned milk (it will splutter, so pour carefully) and stir continuously.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Cook on medium-low flame for 25 minutes, stirring often, until the liquid is absorbed and the halwa thickens.

steps.title: Sweeten
steps.text: Add the dates and cardamom and cook for 3–4 minutes until the halwa leaves the sides of the pan.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with the almonds and cashews and serve warm.

tips: Halwa needs patient stirring on low heat; do not rush it.
This lighter version uses less ghee and jaggery instead of sugar.
serving_ideas: enjoy a small portion after a meal, or with a cup of tea.
Keep sweets to a small bowl or 1–2 pieces.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 3 days; warm before serving.

recipes.description: A creamy beetroot dates kheer, lightly sweetened.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Wash or roast the beetroot as listed.

steps.title: Boil the toned milk
steps.text: Bring the toned milk to a boil in a heavy-bottomed pan, stirring so it does not stick.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Add the beetroot and simmer on low flame for 20 minutes, stirring often and scraping the sides, until soft and creamy.

steps.title: Flavour
steps.text: Add the cardamom and saffron and simmer for 2 more minutes.

steps.title: Sweeten
steps.text: Switch off the flame and let it cool for 5 minutes, then stir in the dates. Adding jaggery off the heat keeps the milk from curdling.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with the almonds and pistachios and serve warm or chilled.

tips: Use a heavy-bottomed pan and stir often so the milk does not burn.
Kheer thickens as it cools; add a little warm milk to loosen it.
serving_ideas: enjoy a small portion after a meal, or with a cup of tea.
Keep sweets to a small bowl or 1–2 pieces.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

recipes.description: A creamy dalia kheer with coconut jaggery.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Wash or roast the dalia as listed.

steps.title: Boil the toned milk and thin coconut milk
steps.text: Bring the toned milk and thin coconut milk to a boil in a heavy-bottomed pan, stirring so it does not stick.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Add the dalia and simmer on low flame for 25 minutes, stirring often and scraping the sides, until soft and creamy.

steps.text: Add the cardamom and saffron and simmer for 2 more minutes.

steps.title: Sweeten
steps.text: Switch off the flame and let it cool for 5 minutes, then stir in the jaggery. Adding jaggery off the heat keeps the milk from curdling.

steps.text: Garnish with the cashews and grated coconut and serve warm or chilled.

tips: Use a heavy-bottomed pan and stir often so the milk does not burn.
Kheer thickens as it cools; add a little warm milk to loosen it.
serving_ideas: enjoy a small portion after a meal, or with a cup of tea.
Keep sweets to a small bowl or 1–2 pieces.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

steps.text: Bring the toned milk and thin coconut milk to a boil in a heavy-bottomed pan, stirring so it does not stick.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Add the quinoa and simmer on low flame for 25 minutes, stirring often and scraping the sides, until soft and creamy.

steps.title: Flavour
steps.text: Add the cardamom and saffron and simmer for 2 more minutes.

steps.title: Sweeten
steps.text: Switch off the flame and let it cool for 5 minutes, then stir in the jaggery. Adding jaggery off the heat keeps the milk from curdling.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with the cashews and grated coconut and serve warm or chilled.

tips: Use a heavy-bottomed pan and stir often so the milk does not burn.
Kheer thickens as it cools; add a little warm milk to loosen it.
serving_ideas: enjoy a small portion after a meal, or with a cup of tea.
Keep sweets to a small bowl or 1–2 pieces.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

recipes.description: A dalia dates halwa sweetened with dates instead of sugar.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Prepare the dalia as listed.

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Heat the ghee and roast the dalia on low flame, stirring constantly, until golden and aromatic.

steps.title: Add the liquid
steps.text: Add the toned milk (it will splutter, so pour carefully) and stir continuously.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Cook on medium-low flame for 15 minutes, stirring often, until the liquid is absorbed and the halwa thickens.

steps.title: Sweeten
steps.text: Add the dates and cardamom and cook for 3–4 minutes until the halwa leaves the sides of the pan.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with the almonds and cashews and serve warm.

tips: Halwa needs patient stirring on low heat; do not rush it.
This lighter version uses less ghee and jaggery instead of sugar.
serving_ideas: enjoy a small portion after a meal, or with a cup of tea.
Keep sweets to a small bowl or 1–2 pieces.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 3 days; warm before serving.

steps.title: Combine

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: While still warm, take a spoonful and press firmly between your palms into a round ladoo.

steps.title: Set
steps.text: Place on a plate and let them firm up for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Store
steps.text: Store in an airtight box.

tips: If the mixture does not bind, add 1–2 tsp warm ghee or a little more date paste.
Make them small; one ladoo is a satisfying portion.

recipes.description: A sooji dates halwa sweetened with dates instead of sugar.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Prepare the rava / suji as listed.

steps.title: Roast
steps.text: Heat the ghee and roast the rava / suji on low flame, stirring constantly, until golden and aromatic.

steps.title: Add the liquid
steps.text: Add the toned milk (it will splutter, so pour carefully) and stir continuously.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Cook on medium-low flame for 6 minutes, stirring often, until the liquid is absorbed and the halwa thickens.

steps.title: Sweeten
steps.text: Add the dates and cardamom and cook for 3–4 minutes until the halwa leaves the sides of the pan.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Garnish with the almonds and cashews and serve warm.

tips: Halwa needs patient stirring on low heat; do not rush it.
This lighter version uses less ghee and jaggery instead of sugar.
serving_ideas: enjoy a small portion after a meal, or with a cup of tea.
Keep sweets to a small bowl or 1–2 pieces.
recipes.storage: keeps in the fridge for 3 days; warm before serving.

recipes.description: Wholesome sunflower seed ladoos with no refined sugar.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Roast the seeds; blend dates.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: In a large bowl, mix the sunflower seeds, dates and grated coconut together well.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: While still warm, take a spoonful and press firmly between your palms into a round ladoo.

steps.title: Set
steps.text: Place on a plate and let them firm up for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Store
steps.text: Store in an airtight box.

tips: If the mixture does not bind, add 1–2 tsp warm ghee or a little more date paste.
Make them small; one ladoo is a satisfying portion.
serving_ideas: one ladoo with a glass of milk, or as a pre-workout snack.
Great for children’s tiffin and for travel.
recipes.storage: keeps in an airtight box for 1–2 weeks (ladoos with fresh coconut: 5 days in the fridge).

recipes.description: A wholesome aloo matar sandwich.

steps.title: Prepare the filling
steps.text: Slice or mix the potato and green peas as listed and season lightly with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Spread
steps.text: Spread green chutney on one slice and hung curd on the other.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: Layer the filling evenly on one slice and cover with the second.

steps.title: Toast
steps.text: Toast in a sandwich maker or on a tawa with a light brush of oil for 2–3 minutes per side until golden.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Cut and serve with a salad or a glass of buttermilk.

tips: Use whole-wheat or multigrain bread for more fibre.
Hung curd and chutney replace butter and mayonnaise for a lighter sandwich.
serving_ideas: a fresh salad, soup or buttermilk.
Best time: breakfast, tiffin or a light dinner.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh; pack the filling separately for tiffin.

recipes.description: A whole-wheat chicken hariyali wrap for lunch or tiffin.

steps.title: Make the rotis
steps.text: Knead a soft atta dough, rest 15 minutes and roll into 4 thin rotis. Cook lightly on a tawa.

steps.title: Prepare the filling
steps.text: Marinate chicken in green chutney and pan-sear.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: Spread green chutney on a warm roti, add lettuce, a portion of the filling and sliced onion.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Sprinkle chaat masala and a squeeze of lemon.

steps.title: Roll
steps.text: Roll up tightly and wrap the bottom half in butter paper or foil.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve immediately, or pack for lunch.

tips: Warm the rotis just before rolling so they do not crack.
serving_ideas: a salad or a glass of buttermilk.
Best time: lunch, tiffin or a quick dinner.
recipes.storage: best eaten within 4 hours.

recipes.description: A wholesome chicken keema spinach sandwich.

steps.title: Prepare the filling
steps.text: Slice or mix the chicken mince and spinach as listed and season lightly with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Spread
steps.text: Spread green chutney on one slice and hung curd on the other.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: Layer the filling evenly on one slice and cover with the second.

steps.title: Toast
steps.text: Toast in a sandwich maker or on a tawa with a light brush of oil for 2–3 minutes per side until golden.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Cut and serve with a salad or a glass of buttermilk.

tips: Use whole-wheat or multigrain bread for more fibre.
Hung curd and chutney replace butter and mayonnaise for a lighter sandwich.
serving_ideas: a fresh salad, soup or buttermilk.
Best time: breakfast, tiffin or a light dinner.
recipes.storage: best eaten fresh; pack the filling separately for tiffin.
